title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄序
皇上綏猷建極隆億萬載文明之
治四十有三年甲子秋八月
復當賓興之期維時監察御
史王諍奉
命按滇飭令甲脩試事迺檄提學
副使薛天華精簡核毋俾鉤
===
棘靡薄之徒溷焉與試者一
千有奇視往時汰十之三遵
朝命也屆期士咸雲蒸霧合以
待而四方文學亦以徵聘至
乃以德音及教諭毛子翼司
試事教諭盧整揭啓蒲凝翠
許衎則分經校閱之提調則
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄序

皇上綏猷建極，隆億萬載文明之治。四十有三年甲子秋八月，復當賓興之期。維時監察御史王諍奉命按滇，飭令甲，脩試事，迺檄提學副使薛天華精簡核，毋俾鉤棘靡薄之徒溷焉。與試者一千有奇，視往時汰十之三，遵朝命也。屆期，士咸雲蒸霧合以待，而四方文學亦以徵聘至。乃以德音及教諭毛子翼司試事，教諭盧整、揭啓、蒲凝翠、許衎則分經校閱之。提調則
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

His Majesty has secured the imperial order and established the supreme standard, exalting a reign of cultured governance to endure for countless ages. In the eighth month of autumn in the forty-third year of his reign, the jiazi year [1564], the time again arrived to honor and advance worthy candidates through the examination. At this time, Investigating Censor Wang Zheng, commissioned to inspect Yunnan, enforced the regulations and prepared the examination arrangements. He then instructed Xue Tianhua, Vice Commissioner for Education, to select and scrutinize candidates carefully, so that those given to tortuous writing and frivolity would not mingle among them. A little over one thousand candidates took the examination, a reduction of three in ten compared with previous occasions, in compliance with the court’s command.

When the appointed time arrived, the scholars gathered like rising clouds and converging mist to await the examination, while learned men from all quarters also arrived in response to invitations. De Yin [?] and County School Instructor Mao Ziyi were entrusted with conducting the examination. County School Instructors Lu Zheng, Jie Qi, Pu Ningcui, and Xu Kan divided the Classics among themselves for the assessment of papers. As for the Proctors, they were…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
右布政使宋國華左叅議盧
岐嶷監試則副使陸綸僉事
胡庭蘭餘皆慎簡以充而御
史寔監臨之矢天日肅內外
蓋至嚴已旣三試拔儁四十
人幷錄其文以
獻蓋滇南科目人文之盛得視
===
中土自我
皇祖始而專設科廣解額則自我
皇上始猗與盛哉德音不佞濫執
事之列其敢以無言乎德音
之應聘而來也入其境則平
原沃野有水泉灌溉之利魚
鹽果蓏之饒蓋西南奧區也
banxin: 雲南鄉試錄前序 二
punctuated:
右布政使宋國華、左叅議盧岐嶷；監試則副使陸綸、僉事胡庭蘭。餘皆慎簡以充，而御史寔監臨之。矢天日，肅內外，蓋至嚴已。旣三試，拔儁四十人，幷錄其文以獻。
蓋滇南科目人文之盛，得視中土，自我皇祖始；而專設科、廣解額，則自我皇上始。猗與盛哉！德音不佞，濫執事之列，其敢以無言乎？德音之應聘而來也，入其境，則平原沃野，有水泉灌溉之利、魚鹽果蓏之饒，蓋西南奧區也。
translation_en:
…the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, Song Guohua, and the Left Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner, Lu Qini; examination oversight was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lu Lun and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Hu Tinglan. All the remaining personnel were carefully selected to fill their posts, while the Investigating Censor himself served as Supervising Official. They swore an oath before Heaven and the sun and maintained strict discipline inside and outside the examination compound: the arrangements were stringent indeed. After the three sessions, forty outstanding candidates were selected, and their essays were also transcribed for presentation to the throne.
It was under our imperial ancestor that the flourishing of the examinations and literary culture in Yunnan first came to rival that of the central regions; the establishment of a separate examination and the enlargement of the provincial graduate quota began under our present emperor. Ah, how splendid! I, Deyin, unworthy though I am, have been included among those charged with conducting the examination. How could I dare remain silent? When I came in response to the invitation and entered this territory, I found broad plains and fertile fields, benefiting from irrigation by streams and springs and abounding in fish, salt, fruits, and gourds. This is indeed a rich heartland of the southwest.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
途轍所經目冠裳之製耳絃
誦之聲庶幾乎遐陬鄒魯矣
比扃院閱多士之文莫不發
明六籍網羅傳記涉其瀾而
嗜其胾颯颯乎纚纚乎言固
人人殊要之不詭於正道而
適於用乃喟然嘆曰玆非昔
===
日六詔之產靡莫之屬與夫
金馬葉榆山川猶昔日而人
文若此者可不知所自哉有
皇祖混一表正之治其人質以思
故其爲文也奮發而感慨有
列聖豐芑之仁其俗恬以愉故其
爲文也和順而婉約肆我
punctuated: 途轍所經，目冠裳之製，耳絃誦之聲，庶幾乎遐陬鄒魯矣。比扃院，閱多士之文，莫不發明六籍，網羅傳記，涉其瀾而嗜其胾，颯颯乎，纚纚乎！言固人人殊，要之不詭於正道而適於用。乃喟然嘆曰：「玆非昔日六詔之產、靡莫之屬與？夫金馬、葉榆，山川猶昔日，而人文若此者，可不知所自哉？有皇祖混一表正之治，其人質以思，故其爲文也奮發而感慨；有列聖豐芑之仁，其俗恬以愉，故其爲文也和順而婉約。肆我
translation_en:
Along the roads I traveled, I saw the forms of caps and robes and heard the sounds of strings and recitation: this remote corner had almost become another Zou and Lu, the homelands of Confucian learning. Once the examination compound was closed, I read the candidates’ compositions. All elucidated the Six Classics and drew widely upon commentaries and historical records, venturing into their waves and savoring their rich meat. How vigorous, how fluent! Their expression certainly differed from person to person, but in essence it did not depart from the correct Way and was suited to practical use.

Then I sighed deeply and said: “Are these not natives of the former Six Zhao kingdoms, people of the Mimo tribes? The mountains and rivers of Jinma and Yeyu remain as they were in former days, yet literary cultivation has reached such a state. Can we fail to recognize its source? Under our imperial ancestor’s government, which unified the realm and rectified the people by example, the people became unassuming and thoughtful; hence their writing is spirited and deeply expressive. Through the benevolence of successive sage emperors, nurturing talent for future generations, their customs became tranquil and joyful; hence their writing is harmonious, gentle, and restrained. Thus our …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皇上壽考作人棫樸菁莪之化其
澤淪以浹故其爲文也縝密
而典則其所感者然也夫天
之生材爲世用也龜珠角齒
皮革羽毛畢登于
天府不以遠而遺也今得士如此
藉手以
===
獻于
闕下此主司之所喜也雖然實
中其聲謂之端不中其聲謂
之窾不得其端而得其窾又
主司之所懼也多士其知所
繫之重矣乎唐虞三代之舉
賢也曰天工人代曰籲俊尊
punctuated: 皇上壽考作人，棫樸菁莪之化，其澤淪以浹，故其爲文也縝密而典則，其所感者然也。夫天之生材，爲世用也。龜珠角齒，皮革羽毛，畢登于天府，不以遠而遺也。今得士如此，藉手以獻于闕下，此主司之所喜也。雖然，實中其聲謂之端，不中其聲謂之窾。不得其端而得其窾，又主司之所懼也。多士其知所繫之重矣乎！唐虞三代之舉賢也，曰「天工人代」，曰「籲俊尊
translation_en: …His Majesty, long-lived and nurturing worthy men, brings about the transforming influence celebrated in “The Oak Clusters” (Yupu) and “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing’e). His beneficence penetrates deeply and pervades all; thus their writing is meticulous and conforms to classical standards. It is the influence they have received that makes it so. Heaven produces talents for the use of the world. Tortoises, pearls, horns, tusks, hides, leather, feathers, and fur all enter the imperial treasury; none is passed over because it comes from afar. Now that we have obtained scholars such as these, we have something to present at the palace gates: this is what delights those presiding over the examination. Nevertheless, when substance matches reputation, this is called substantial; when it does not match reputation, this is called hollow. To obtain the hollow rather than the substantial is, in turn, what those presiding over the examination fear. Do you assembled scholars understand the weight of the responsibilities that rest upon you? Regarding the advancement of worthy men under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, it was said, “Heaven’s work is performed by men acting in its stead,” and “Call upon outstanding men to honor…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
帝曰
天惟純佑則商實曰以敬事
上帝立民長伯然則
天之生賢以承
君也
君之求賢以事
天也御史率藩臬百執事孜孜以
===
舉賢為務士荷
上休澤感會遘期躍然奮矣乃弗
竭忠宣力以對
恩遇人其謂何
國家重惜民財力唯恐纖芥侈
費至於待士之厚不特居官
有祿秩其賓於鄉也歌鹿鳴
punctuated:
帝」，曰：「天惟純佑。」則商實曰：「以敬事上帝，立民長伯。」然則，天之生賢以承君也，君之求賢以事天也。御史率藩臬百執事，孜孜以舉賢為務。士荷上休澤，感會遘期，躍然奮矣。乃弗竭忠宣力以對恩遇，人其謂何？

國家重惜民財力，唯恐纖芥侈費。至於待士之厚，不特居官有祿秩，其賓於鄉也，歌《鹿鳴》
translation_en:
…the Sovereign on High”; and, “Heaven grants its full protection.” Indeed, the Shang declared: “To serve the Sovereign on High reverently, establish rulers and leaders for the people.” Thus Heaven brings forth worthy men to assist the ruler, and the ruler seeks worthy men to serve Heaven. The Censor leads the provincial administration and surveillance officials and all other functionaries in diligently pursuing the selection of worthy men. Scholars receive the beneficent favor of the throne; moved by this fortunate conjunction and timely opportunity, they eagerly bestir themselves. If they then fail to exert their utmost loyalty and devote their strength to repaying such gracious treatment, what will people say of them?

The state greatly cherishes the people’s wealth and labor, fearing even the slightest extravagance or waste. Yet its generous treatment of scholars extends beyond providing salaries and stipends when they hold office: when it receives them as honored guests in the province, it has “Deer Call” sung…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以選之宴享之唯恐其不豐
續食計偕舟車遠邇相屬於
道館穀之唯恐其乏不慮煩
費者何也為費小而所利之
大也多士亦不見父母之愛
其子者乎裹糧而適郊野暮
而弗歸則倚閭而望之矣適
===
千里浹旬弗反則挈糈而卜
之矣若策名賓貢違親遠游
則甚欣然跋涉萬里無離憂
者何也為幼學而壯行之令
名足為親榮也主司之於多
士非有傾蓋之雅非知其平
日迪履之素也校一日之文
punctuated:
以選之，宴享之，唯恐其不豐。續食計偕，舟車遠邇相屬於道，館穀之，唯恐其乏。不慮煩費者，何也？為費小而所利之大也。
多士亦不見父母之愛其子者乎？裹糧而適郊野，暮而弗歸，則倚閭而望之矣；適千里，浹旬弗反，則挈糈而卜之矣。若策名賓貢，違親遠游，則甚欣然，跋涉萬里無離憂者，何也？為幼學而壯行之令名，足為親榮也。
主司之於多士，非有傾蓋之雅，非知其平日迪履之素也。校一日之文，
translation_en:
…to select them, and entertain them at banquets, fearing only that the fare might not be abundant enough. Provisions are supplied for their journey to the examination; boats and carriages from near and far follow one another along the roads. They are given lodging and food, with concern only that they might lack something. Why is there no concern about the trouble and expense? Because the expense is small and the benefit great.
Have you scholars not also seen how parents love their children? If a child packs provisions and goes into the countryside but has not returned by evening, they lean against the village gate and watch for him. If he travels a thousand li and has not returned after ten days, they take sacrificial grain to seek divination. Yet when his name is entered among those recommended for presentation at court and he leaves his parents to travel afar, they are thoroughly delighted. Why does his journey of ten thousand li cause them no sorrow at parting? Because the good name earned by putting into practice in adulthood what he learned in youth brings sufficient glory to his parents.
The chief examiners have no prior friendship with you scholars, even such as might arise from a chance encounter, nor do they know your customary conduct in daily life. They assess the writing you produce in a single day…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以卜其終身之行是循聲以
責其實者也其中與否非所
敢必在多士之自毖焉耳多
士他日能敬事亮工以忠
君報
國爲急則非惟寵其身榮及其
親耳矣將使滇之人指而稱
===
之曰今日得人之盛彬彬如
此也則
國家賓禮之隆庶其無負而主
司之懼其亦少釋矣乎是舉
也鎮守黔國公沐朝弼飭備
宣威士類有所利賴巡撫右
都御史吕光洵輯近綏遠文
punctuated:
以卜其終身之行，是循聲以責其實者也。其中與否，非所敢必，在多士之自毖焉耳。多士他日能敬事亮工，以忠君報國爲急，則非惟寵其身、榮及其親耳矣，將使滇之人指而稱之曰：「今日得人之盛，彬彬如此也！」則國家賓禮之隆，庶其無負，而主司之懼，其亦少釋矣乎？

是舉也，鎮守黔國公沐朝弼飭備宣威，士類有所利賴；巡撫右都御史吕光洵輯近綏遠，文
translation_en:
…to gauge their conduct throughout their lives: this is to look to their reputation and require that their actual conduct measure up to it. Whether that judgment proves accurate is not something we dare guarantee; it rests solely on the candidates’ own vigilance over themselves. If in days to come they attend reverently to their duties and faithfully perform their work, making loyalty to the ruler and service to the state their foremost concern, they will not merely bring distinction to themselves and honor to their parents. They will also cause the people of Dian to point to them and exclaim: “How splendid is the abundance of worthy men recruited today, so accomplished and refined!” Then, perhaps, they will not have failed to live up to the state’s generous ceremonial treatment of them as honored guests, and the examination officials’ apprehensions may also be somewhat relieved.

For this examination, Mu Chaobi, Duke of Qianguo, stationed here as regional defender, put defenses in order and displayed military authority, providing benefits and security on which the scholars could rely. The Grand Coordinator and Right Censor-in-Chief, Lü Guangxun, brought concord to those nearby and peace to those afar; literary …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敎藉以綱維綜理防範則右
叅議歸大道副使王春復僉
事蕭鳴邦署都指揮僉事史
符署都指揮同知袁廕入
賀
朝宗則左布政使劉斯潔左叅
政汪克用副使繆文龍張天
復署都指揮僉事王世科先
期遷秩則右叅政熊桴協力
分猷皆有功於試事者也於
法得書敢併及之云
四川成都府綿州儒學學正
王德音謹序
punctuated:
敎藉以綱維。綜理防範，則右叅議歸大道、副使王春復、僉事蕭鳴邦、署都指揮僉事史符、署都指揮同知袁廕；入賀朝宗，則左布政使劉斯潔、左叅政汪克用、副使繆文龍、張天復、署都指揮僉事王世科；先期遷秩，則右叅政熊桴。協力分猷，皆有功於試事者也。於法得書，敢併及之云。
四川成都府綿州儒學學正王德音謹序。
translation_en:
…education thereby gained its guiding framework. Those who oversaw arrangements and safeguards were Gui Dadao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Wang Chunfu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Xiao Mingbang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Shi Fu, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; and Yuan Yin, Acting Regional Military Vice Commissioner. Those who went to court to offer congratulations and pay homage were Liu Sijie, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Wang Keyong, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Miao Wenlong and Zhang Tianfu, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Wang Shike, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. Xiong Fu, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, had been promoted before the examination. By pooling their efforts and sharing their counsel, all rendered service to the examination. Since the rules permit their inclusion in the record, I venture to mention them together here.
Preface respectfully written by Wang Deyin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史王諍〔子敬湖廣竹山縣籍浙江永嘉縣人庚戌進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右布政使宋國華〔崇樂江西奉新縣人甲辰進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議盧岐嶷〔希稷福建長泰縣人甲辰進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使陸綸〔理之浙江歸安縣人庚戌進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事胡庭蘭〔伯賢廣東增城縣人庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
四川成都府綿州儒學學正王德音〔伯宣湖廣安化縣人乙卯貢士〕
江西吉安府安福縣儒學教諭毛子翼〔時保浙江餘姚縣人癸卯貢士〕
同考試官
四川敘州府富順縣儒學教諭盧整〔敬甫貴州前衛官籍浙江臨海縣人乙卯貢士〕
直隸徽州府黟縣儒學教諭揭𠗜〔子瞻江西南豐縣人己酉貢士〕
湖廣岳州府澧州石門縣儒學教諭蒲凝翠〔崇厚廣東南海縣人戊午貢士〕
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭許衍〔應中福建龍溪縣人乙卯貢士〕
印卷官
punctuated:
嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試

監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史王諍〔子敬，湖廣竹山縣籍，浙江永嘉縣人，庚戌進士〕。

提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右布政使宋國華〔崇樂，江西奉新縣人，甲辰進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議盧岐嶷〔希稷，福建長泰縣人，甲辰進士〕。

監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使陸綸〔理之，浙江歸安縣人，庚戌進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事胡庭蘭〔伯賢，廣東增城縣人，庚戌進士〕。

考試官
四川成都府綿州儒學學正王德音〔伯宣，湖廣安化縣人，乙卯貢士〕。
江西吉安府安福縣儒學教諭毛子翼〔時保，浙江餘姚縣人，癸卯貢士〕。

同考試官

江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭許衍〔應中，福建龍溪縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

印卷官
translation_en:
Yunnan Provincial Examination, Forty-third Year of Jiajing (1564)

Supervising Official
Wang Zheng, Regional Inspector of Yunnan and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Zijing. He was registered in Zhushan County, Huguang, and was a native of Yongjia County, Zhejiang; he became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the gengxu year.

Proctors
Song Guohua, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Chongle. A native of Fengxin County, Jiangxi, he became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.
Lu Qiyi, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Xiji. A native of Changtai County, Fujian, he became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.

Invigilating Officials
Lu Lun, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Lizhi. A native of Gui’an County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.
Hu Tinglan, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Boxian. A native of Zengcheng County, Guangdong, he became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Examiners
Wang Deyin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, had the courtesy name Boxuan. A native of Anhua County, Huguang, he became a tribute student (gongshi) in the yimao year.
Mao Ziyi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Shibao. A native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, he became a tribute student in the guimao year.

Associate Examiners
Lu Zheng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, had the courtesy name Jingfu. He held official-household registration in Guizhou Front Guard and was a native of Linhai County, Zhejiang; he became a tribute student in the yimao year.
Jie 𠗜 [given-name reading uncertain], Instructor at the Confucian School of Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Zizhan. A native of Nanfeng County, Jiangxi, he became a tribute student in the jiyou year.
Pu Ningcui, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shimen County, Lizhou, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Chonghou. A native of Nanhai County, Guangdong, he became a tribute student in the wuwu year.
Xu Yan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Yingzhong. A native of Longxi County, Fujian, he became a tribute student in the yimao year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校李國元〔子一四川富順縣人監生〕
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷董秊〔子粹直隸涇縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
大理府知府羅𤐣〔文望貴州永寧衛籍直隸泰州人甲午貢士〕
永昌軍民府同知張澤〔汝濟山西榆次縣人甲午貢士〕
受卷官
永昌軍民府知府楊朗〔啓東江西南昌縣人庚子貢士〕
麗江軍民府同知辜用琥〔子壽湖廣竹山縣籍江西南昌縣人癸卯貢士〕
雲南府通判潘應奎〔文瑞湖廣五開衛官籍江西德化縣人監生〕
===
永昌軍民府推官趙龍〔季震四川廣安州籍江西進賢縣人己酉貢士〕
彌封官
臨安府推官湯惟允〔時中江西安仁縣人甲午貢士〕
雲南府嵩明州知州張効〔惟忠貴州烏撒衛籍河南澠池縣人庚子貢士〕
曲靖軍民府霑益州知州姜時棠〔思召湖廣通山縣人己酉貢士〕
澂江府新興州知州湯克俊〔仲登貴州宣慰司籍直隸桃源縣人乙卯貢士〕
謄錄官
大理府趙州知州符有光〔汝謙貴州思南府籍江西新喻縣人癸卯貢士〕
白鹽井鹽課提舉司提舉王朴〔子厚貴州清平衛官籍浙江嵊縣人辛卯貢士〕
punctuated:
雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校李國元〔子一，四川富順縣人，監生〕。雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷董秊〔子粹，直隸涇縣人，監生〕。

受卷官：永昌軍民府知府楊朗〔啓東，江西南昌縣人，庚子貢士〕。麗江軍民府同知辜用琥〔子壽，湖廣竹山縣籍，江西南昌縣人，癸卯貢士〕。雲南府通判潘應奎〔文瑞，湖廣五開衛官籍，江西德化縣人，監生〕。永昌軍民府推官趙龍〔季震，四川廣安州籍，江西進賢縣人，己酉貢士〕。

彌封官：臨安府推官湯惟允〔時中，江西安仁縣人，甲午貢士〕。雲南府嵩明州知州張効〔惟忠，貴州烏撒衛籍，河南澠池縣人，庚子貢士〕。曲靖軍民府霑益州知州姜時棠〔思召，湖廣通山縣人，己酉貢士〕。澂江府新興州知州湯克俊〔仲登，貴州宣慰司籍，直隸桃源縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

translation_en:
Li Guoyuan, Inspector in the Records Office of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Ziyi. He was a native of Fushun County, Sichuan, and an Imperial University student. Dong Nian, Registrar in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zicui. He was a native of Jing County in the directly administered territory and an Imperial University student.

Officials responsible for custody of examination scripts:
Luo 𤐣 (reading of the given name uncertain [?]), Prefect of Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Wenwang. He was registered in Yongning Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Taizhou in the directly administered territory, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiawu year. Zhang Ze, Vice Prefect of Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruji. He was a native of Yuci County, Shanxi, and a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.

Officials receiving examination scripts:
Yang Lang, Prefect of Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Qidong. He was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and a tribute scholar of the gengzi year. Gu Yonghu, Vice Prefect of Lijiang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zishou. He was registered in Zhushan County, Huguang, was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the guimao year. Pan Yingkui, Assistant Prefect of Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Wenrui. He belonged to an official household registered in Wukai Guard, Huguang, was a native of Dehua County, Jiangxi, and was an Imperial University student. Zhao Long, Prefectural Judge of Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jizhen. He was registered in Guang'an Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a native of Jinxian County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.

Officials sealing candidates’ identifying information:
Tang Weiyun, Prefectural Judge of Lin'an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shizhong. He was a native of Anren County, Jiangxi, and a tribute scholar of the jiawu year. Zhang Xiao, Magistrate of Songming Subprefecture in Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weizhong. He was registered in Wusa Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Mianchi County, Henan, and was a tribute scholar of the gengzi year. Jiang Shitang, Magistrate of Zhanyi Subprefecture in Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Sizhao. He was a native of Tongshan County, Huguang, and a tribute scholar of the jiyou year. Tang Kejun, Magistrate of Xinxing Subprefecture in Chengjiang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhongdeng. He was registered under the Guizhou Pacification Commission, was a native of Taoyuan County in the directly administered territory, and was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.

Officials supervising transcription:
Fu Youguang, Magistrate of Zhaozhou Subprefecture in Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruqian. He was registered in Sinan Prefecture, Guizhou, was a native of Xinyu County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the guimao year. Wang Pu, Superintendent of the Baiyanjing Salt Tax Superintendency, had the courtesy name Zihou. He belonged to an official household registered in Qingping Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Sheng County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄

雲南左衛指揮僉事馬文春〔季元直隸和州人〕

雲南前衛指揮僉事楊春育〔體仁雲南安寧州人〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:

Gan Shiyuan was examiner in the Records Office of Yunnan Prefecture. His courtesy name was Tiangui; he was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi, and was a Confucian scholar.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也夫然後行
天地之道博也厚也高也明也悠也久也
今夫天斯昭昭之多及其無窮也日月
星辰繫焉萬物覆焉今夫地一撮土之
多及其廣厚載華嶽而不重振河海而
不洩萬物載焉今夫山一卷石之多及
===
其廣大草木生之禽獸居之寶藏興焉
今夫水一勺之多及其不測黿鼉蛟龍
魚鼈生焉貨財殖焉
公事畢然後敢治私事
易
天地養萬物聖人養賢以及萬民頤之時
大矣哉
受玆介福以中正也
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也，夫然後行。

天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。今夫天，斯昭昭之多，及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多，及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。今夫山，一卷石之多，及其廣大，草木生之，禽獸居之，寶藏興焉。今夫水，一勺之多，及其不測，黿鼉蛟龍魚鼈生焉，貨財殖焉。

公事畢，然後敢治私事。

易

天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬民，頤之時大矣哉！

受玆介福，以中正也。

是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When standing, see these principles present before you; when riding in a carriage, see them resting against its crossbar. Only then can you put them into practice.

The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, substantial, lofty, luminous, enduring, and lasting. Now Heaven, taken in a small portion, is merely this patch of brightness; yet in its infinity, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended within it, and all things are covered by it. Now Earth, taken in a small portion, is merely a handful of soil; yet in its breadth and depth, it bears Mount Hua without feeling its weight, holds the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and supports all things. Now a mountain, taken in a small portion, is merely a small stone; yet in its breadth and greatness, plants and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell upon it, and precious deposits arise within it. Now water, taken in a small portion, is merely a spoonful; yet in its unfathomable depths, giant turtles, alligators, dragons, fish, and soft-shelled turtles live within it, and goods and wealth multiply there.

Only after the public work is finished do they dare attend to their private affairs.

Book of Changes

Heaven and Earth nourish all things; the sage nourishes the worthy and thereby extends nourishment to all the people. Great indeed is the significance of the time of Nourishment!

He receives this great blessing because he is central and correct.

Thus, among patterns to emulate, none are greater than Heaven and Earth; among transformations and adaptations, none are greater than the four seasons …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以爲天下利莫大
乎聖人
象也者像也
書
惟德動天無遠弗届
織皮崑崙析支渠搜西戎卽敘
惟曰欲至于萬年
立政任人準夫牧作三事虎賁綴衣趣馬
===
小尹左右攜僕百司庶府大都小伯藝
人表臣百司太史尹伯庶常吉士司徒
司馬司空亞旅夷微盧烝三亳阪尹
詩
游環脅驅陰靷鋈續
賓之初筵左右秩秩籩豆有楚殽核維旅
酒旣和旨飮酒孔偕鐘鼓旣設擧醻逸
逸大侯旣抗弓矢斯張射夫旣同獻爾
發功發彼有的以祈爾爵
punctuated:
縣象著明，莫大乎日月；崇高，莫大乎富貴；備物致用，立成器以爲天下利，莫大乎聖人。
象也者，像也。

書
惟德動天，無遠弗届。
織皮崑崙、析支、渠搜，西戎卽敘。
惟曰欲至于萬年。
立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事；虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹、左右攜僕、百司、庶府、大都、小伯、藝人、表臣、百司、太史、尹伯、庶常吉士、司徒、司馬、司空、亞旅、夷、微、盧、烝、三亳阪尹。

詩
游環脅驅，陰靷鋈續。
賓之初筵，左右秩秩。籩豆有楚，殽核維旅。酒旣和旨，飮酒孔偕。鐘鼓旣設，擧醻逸逸。大侯旣抗，弓矢斯張。射夫旣同，獻爾發功。發彼有的，以祈爾爵。
translation_en:
…Of the images suspended on high and shining brightly, none are greater than the sun and moon. Of exalted conditions, none are greater than wealth and honor. In providing things for use and fashioning implements to benefit all under Heaven, none are greater than the sages.
An image is a likeness.

Book of Documents
Only virtue moves Heaven; there is no distance beyond its reach.
The fur-clad peoples of Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou—the western Rong—came into due order.
They said only that they wished to endure for ten thousand years.
In establishing government: those entrusted with office, the officers administering the laws, and the regional governors undertake the three principal duties; the guards, keepers of robes, equerries, lesser administrators, personal attendants on the left and right, officials of every department, keepers of the various repositories, officers of the great capitals, lesser chiefs, artisans, frontier ministers, the various officials, Grand Scribes, chief administrators, the many regular officers of worthy character, the Minister of Education, Minister of War, Minister of Works, subordinate officers, the Yi, Wei, and Lu peoples, the multitudes, and the administrators of the slopes of the three Bo settlements [?].

Book of Odes
The sliding rings and side straps guide the horses; the concealed traces have plated metal fittings.
As the guests first take their places at the feast, those on the left and right are in orderly ranks. The bamboo and wooden vessels are neatly arranged; meats and fruits are set out. The wine is well blended and delicious; all drink in harmony. Bells and drums are in place; the cups are raised in gracious exchange. The great archery target has been erected; bows and arrows are made ready. The archers have assembled: display your skill in shooting! Shoot at that marked target, to seek your wine cup.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
廼立皐門皐門有伉廼立應門應門將將
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
春秋
秋郳黎來來朝莊公五年
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會
于陽穀僖公三年春王三月宋人執
滕子嬰齊夏六月宋公曹人邾人盟
于曹南僖公十有九年
===
夏季孫行父如齊宣公元年夏公會齊
侯于夾谷公至自夾谷定公十年
秋季孫意如會晉韓起齊國弱宋華亥衞
北宮佗鄭罕虎曹人杞人于厥憖昭公
十有一年
禮記
考禮正刑一德以尊于天子
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
punctuated:
廼立皐門，皐門有伉；廼立應門，應門將將。聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。

春秋
秋，郳黎來來朝。莊公五年。八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。僖公元年。秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。僖公三年。春，王三月，宋人執滕子嬰齊。夏，六月，宋公、曹人、邾人盟于曹南。僖公十有九年。夏，季孫行父如齊。宣公元年。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。定公十年。秋，季孫意如會晉韓起、齊國弱、宋華亥、衞北宮佗、鄭罕虎、曹人、杞人于厥憖。昭公十有一年。

禮記
考禮，正刑，一德，以尊于天子。
故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂
translation_en:
Then he erected the Gao Gate; the Gao Gate stood lofty. Then he erected the Ying Gate; the Ying Gate stood majestic. His sagely reverence increased daily; his radiant influence gradually reached afar. He revered the Lord on High.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, Lilai of Ni came to court. Fifth year of Duke Zhuang.
In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. First year of Duke Xi.
In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. Third year of Duke Xi.
In spring, in the third month of the royal calendar, men of Song seized Yingqi, Viscount of Teng. In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke of Song and representatives of Cao and Zhu made a covenant south of Cao. Nineteenth year of Duke Xi.
In summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. First year of Duke Xuan.
In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke returned from Jiagu. Tenth year of Duke Ding.
In autumn, Jisun Yiru met Han Qi of Jin, Guo Ruo of Qi, Hua Hai of Song, Beigong Tuo of Wei, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Cao and Qi at Jueyin. Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.

Book of Rites
Examine the rites, rectify punishments, and unify moral conduct, thereby honoring the Son of Heaven.
Thus, human feelings are the field of the sage king. He cultivates the rites to plow it, sets forth righteousness to sow it, expounds learning to weed it, takes benevolence as the foundation for gathering its harvest, and disseminates music …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以安之
移風易俗天下皆寧
外無敵內順治此之謂盛德
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉茂材異等詔〔元封五年〕
擬唐加李靖光祿大夫誥〔貞觀四年〕
===
擬禮部尚書陶凱進宴享九奏樂章表〔洪〕
〔武四年〕
判語〔五條〕
官文書稽程
私借官車船
不操練軍士
因公擅科斂
依告狀鞫獄
第參場
punctuated:
以安之。
移風易俗，天下皆寧。
外無敵，內順治，此之謂盛德。
第貳場
論
聖人，太極之全體。
詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉茂材異等詔〔元封五年〕。
擬唐加李靖光祿大夫誥〔貞觀四年〕。
擬禮部尚書陶凱進宴享九奏樂章表〔洪〕〔武四年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官文書稽程。
私借官車船。
不操練軍士。
因公擅科斂。
依告狀鞫獄。
第參場
translation_en:
…to bring them peace.

Transform prevailing customs and change established practices, and all under Heaven will be at peace.

Without enemies abroad and with orderly government at home: this is called consummate virtue.

Second Session

Discourse

The sage embodies the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials〔One question from among these [?].〕

Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor calling for the recommendation of men of outstanding talent and exceptional ability.〔Fifth year of Yuanfeng.〕

Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor conferring on Li Jing the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.〔Fourth year of Zhenguan.〕

Compose a memorial in the voice of Tao Kai, Minister of Rites, presenting the lyrics for the nine musical performances at court banquets.〔Fourth year of Hongwu.〕

Legal Judgments〔Five items.〕

Delays beyond prescribed time limits in processing official documents.

Privately borrowing government carriages or boats.

Failure to drill soldiers.

Unauthorized levies under the pretext of official business.

Trying cases in accordance with the written complaint.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
策〔五道〕
問我
聖祖肇建區宇再開闢乾坤之功自書契以來未
之有也矧滇南則用夏變夷
德澤尤深渥矣甞攷兹土自漢以來叛服不
常今則尺地悉入版圖夷落盡爲編户
非漢唐所可倫矣當時戡定混一之功
有可得而言者與方
王師之深入致討也胡元遺孽屯兵厚集曲
===
靖以禦我師矣白石江之戰出其不意
而獲達里麻我兵之進攻大理也段氏
以五萬之衆先扼下關據險以守矣分
遣奇兵攻其無備而擒段世此豈天之
所啓與抑將之多算與曲靖旣下雲南
何以不戰而服大理旣得諸夷何以相
率來歸與楊苴甞糾衆二十萬以寇雲
南卒之校營宵遁諸蠻授首平緬甞率
衆三十萬以寇定邊卒之戰象不反醜
punctuated:
策〔五道〕
問：我聖祖肇建區宇，再開闢乾坤之功，自書契以來未之有也。矧滇南，則用夏變夷，德澤尤深渥矣。甞攷兹土，自漢以來，叛服不常；今則尺地悉入版圖，夷落盡爲編户，非漢唐所可倫矣。當時戡定混一之功，有可得而言者與？方王師之深入致討也，胡元遺孽屯兵厚集曲靖，以禦我師矣。白石江之戰，出其不意而獲達里麻。我兵之進攻大理也，段氏以五萬之衆先扼下關，據險以守矣。分遣奇兵，攻其無備而擒段世。此豈天之所啓與？抑將之多算與？曲靖旣下，雲南何以不戰而服？大理旣得，諸夷何以相率來歸與？楊苴甞糾衆二十萬以寇雲南，卒之校營宵遁，諸蠻授首；平緬甞率衆三十萬以寇定邊，卒之戰象不反，醜
translation_en:
Policy questions〔five〕
Question: Our sagely founding emperor established the realm anew. His achievement in opening Heaven and Earth afresh was unparalleled since the beginning of written records. How much more profound and abundant were his virtue and beneficence in southern Yunnan, where he transformed the non-Han peoples through Chinese civilization! I have examined the history of this land: since the Han, it had alternated unpredictably between rebellion and submission. Now every foot of land lies within our mapped territory, and all the tribal settlements have become registered households. The Han and Tang cannot compare with this. Can you give an account of the achievements by which it was then pacified and unified?
When the imperial army advanced deep into the region on its punitive expedition, the surviving remnants of the barbarian Yuan massed substantial forces at Qujing to resist our troops. In the battle at the Baishi River, our forces caught them unawares and captured Dalima. When our troops advanced against Dali, the Duan clan had already occupied Xiaguan with fifty thousand men, holding its strategic terrain for defense. Special detachments were dispatched to attack where they were unprepared, capturing Duan Shi [?]. Was this an opportunity opened by Heaven, or the result of the generals’ thorough planning? Once Qujing had fallen, why did Yunnan submit without a battle? Once Dali had been taken, why did the various non-Han peoples follow one another in pledging allegiance?
Yang Ju once mustered two hundred thousand men to invade Yunnan, but in the end his encampment [?] fled by night, and the various tribal foes were beheaded. Pingmian once led three hundred thousand men to invade Dingbian, but in the end the war elephants did not return, and the vile …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
類盡殲何也穎川之弘烈西平之偉績
固也然聞
聖祖命將出師時已授成算及再
勅穎川侯傅友德諭以平定安輯之策則
神謨遠略所以圖始慮終者已先定矣其詳亦
可得聞與及南中既平雖偏州下邑莫
不設爲庠序以化導之歷今二百餘年
文物衣冠之盛與中國齒齊民號易治
豈非學道易使之效哉恭惟
===
皇上至德廣淵
聖學緝熈
敬一有箴四箴有註
頒布天下鐫之學宮故遐方僻壤青衿之士
涵濡
聖化彬彬嚮風益非昔比矣間者醜虜匪茹即
命將徂征莫不仰仗
玄威以收屢捷之功南中最爾夷酋時或梗化
即撲滅不旋踵諸部落渠率尺檄調發
punctuated:
類盡殲，何也？穎川之弘烈，西平之偉績，固也。然聞聖祖命將出師時，已授成算；及再勅穎川侯傅友德，諭以平定安輯之策，則神謨遠略，所以圖始慮終者，已先定矣。其詳亦可得聞與？及南中既平，雖偏州下邑，莫不設爲庠序以化導之。歷今二百餘年，文物衣冠之盛，與中國齒齊，民號易治，豈非學道易使之效哉？
恭惟皇上至德廣淵，聖學緝熈，敬一有箴，四箴有註，頒布天下，鐫之學宮。故遐方僻壤青衿之士，涵濡聖化，彬彬嚮風，益非昔比矣。間者醜虜匪茹，即命將徂征，莫不仰仗玄威，以收屢捷之功。南中最爾夷酋，時或梗化，即撲滅不旋踵。諸部落渠率，尺檄調發
translation_en:
…their kind were utterly annihilated—why was this? Certainly, these were the glorious achievements of Yingchuan and the magnificent accomplishments of Xiping. Yet we have heard that when the sagely founder commissioned his generals and sent out the army, he had already supplied a settled plan. When he again issued an edict to Fu Youde, Marquis of Yingchuan, instructing him in measures for pacification and the restoration of order, his inspired designs and far-reaching strategy, planning the beginning and considering the outcome, had thus already been determined. May we also hear the details? Once the southern region had been pacified, schools were established even in remote prefectures and lesser towns to transform and guide the people. More than two hundred years have now passed. The flourishing of cultural institutions and cultivated society equals that of the Central Lands, and the people are reputed easy to govern. Is this not the result of their learning the Way and thus becoming easy to direct?
We reverently consider how Your Majesty’s consummate virtue is vast and profound, and your sagely learning ever more radiant. You have composed an Admonition on Revering the One and annotations on the Four Admonitions, promulgated them throughout the realm, and had them engraved in the schools. Thus even students in distant and secluded places, steeped in your sagely transforming influence, have become refined and responsive to your example, increasingly surpassing those of former times. Recently, when the vile foes would not submit [?], you immediately ordered generals to campaign against them. All relied upon your mysterious might to achieve repeated victories. In the southern region, whenever the petty [?] native chieftains obstructed your transforming influence, they were crushed without a moment’s delay. The leaders of the various tribes, summoned and mobilized by a brief written dispatch…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
奔命恐後惟畏
威也夫
聖祖以武功定天下而文教之誕敷
皇上以文教致太平而武功之駿發雖典謨所
稱帝德廣運聖神文武者又何以加焉
此固多士躬逢而目覩者願揄揚之以
鳴
國家之盛
問性者萬物一原之理故孔子曰性相近
===
也語最渾然子思懼其義之未彰也乃
以天命表之孟軻懼其實之未著也乃
以利善言之故天下之言性惟本於子
思孟軻則相近之旨得矣後世儒者擇
焉不精語焉不詳不免角出以相勝如
曰天就不可以學事矣而又謂質樸必
成於教化教化之成豈即天之就與如
曰繕俗以復其初矣而又謂隨氣所適
之善惡善惡之適豈即初之使然與四
punctuated:
奔命恐後，惟畏威也。夫聖祖以武功定天下，而文教之誕敷；皇上以文教致太平，而武功之駿發。雖典謨所稱「帝德廣運，聖神文武」者，又何以加焉？此固多士躬逢而目覩者，願揄揚之，以鳴國家之盛。
問：性者，萬物一原之理，故孔子曰：「性相近也。」語最渾然。子思懼其義之未彰也，乃以天命表之；孟軻懼其實之未著也，乃以利善言之。故天下之言性，惟本於子思、孟軻，則相近之旨得矣。後世儒者擇焉不精，語焉不詳，不免角出以相勝。如曰「天就不可以學事」矣，而又謂「質樸必成於教化」，教化之成，豈即天之就與？如曰「繕俗以復其初」矣，而又謂「隨氣所適之善惡」，善惡之適，豈即初之使然與？四
translation_en:
…they hasten to obey commands, fearing to fall behind, solely out of awe for imperial might. The sagely founder settled the realm through military achievement and spread civil instruction far and wide; His Majesty has brought about Great Peace through civil instruction and has displayed magnificent military achievements. Even the sovereign virtue celebrated in the Canons and Counsels as “far-reaching and all-embracing, sagely and numinous, accomplished in civil and military affairs”—how could it surpass this? These are things that you candidates have personally lived through and witnessed. We ask you to extol them, proclaiming the flourishing condition of the dynasty.
Question: Human nature is the principle by which all things share a single source. Thus Confucius said, “By nature, people are close to one another.” These words are supremely comprehensive. Zisi, fearing that their meaning was not yet manifest, explained it through Heaven’s mandate. Meng Ke, fearing that their substance was not yet evident, spoke of it in terms of “benefit and goodness” [?]. Thus, when people discuss human nature, only by grounding themselves in Zisi and Meng Ke can they grasp the purport of “close to one another.” Later Confucian scholars were insufficiently discriminating in their judgments and insufficiently thorough in their explanations; inevitably, they advanced competing claims, each seeking to prevail over the others. For example, one says, “What Heaven brings to completion cannot be made the business of learning,” yet also maintains that “native simplicity must be perfected through teaching and moral transformation.” Is perfection through teaching and moral transformation then the very same as completion by Heaven? Another says, “Reform customary practices to recover the original state,” yet also speaks of “good and evil toward which one’s vital energy inclines.” Are these inclinations toward good and evil then caused by that original state? title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
儒者間與孟子而竝稱果得利善之要
歸否與其曰剛柔善惡中而已者義至
備也而又曰仁義禮智人性之綱則何
惡之可易與其曰性者道之形體心者
性之郛郭名最善也而又曰自內以立
本自外以致用則何形體郛郭之可岐
與四儒者皆以子思為正傳果得天命
之名義否與彼生之謂性告子之妄而
飲食男女則生之類也而曰皆性何與
===
惡以言性荀氏之謬蓋惡者氣之戾也
而曰亦不可不謂之性何與既以性之
動為情而又以性之動為心然則心統
性情非與既以感物而動為欲而又以
不能無感謂性然則至靜無感非與其
究愈深而其說愈長矣玆專主相近而
言則渾淪而似乎善惡之混主天命而
言則太廣而同乎人物之生主利善而
言則太峻而遺乎氣質之稟無異乎諸
punctuated: 儒者間與孟子而竝稱，果得利善之要歸否與？其曰「剛柔善惡中而已」者，義至備也，而又曰「仁義禮智，人性之綱」，則何惡之可易與？其曰「性者道之形體，心者性之郛郭」，名最善也，而又曰「自內以立本，自外以致用」，則何形體郛郭之可岐與？四儒者皆以子思為正傳，果得天命之名義否與？彼「生之謂性」，告子之妄，而飲食男女則生之類也，而曰皆性，何與？惡以言性，荀氏之謬，蓋惡者氣之戾也，而曰亦不可不謂之性，何與？既以性之動為情，而又以性之動為心，然則心統性情非與？既以感物而動為欲，而又以不能無感謂性，然則至靜無感非與？其究愈深，而其說愈長矣。玆專主相近而言，則渾淪而似乎善惡之混；主天命而言，則太廣而同乎人物之生；主利善而言，則太峻而遺乎氣質之稟，無異乎諸
translation_en:
…scholars are sometimes named alongside Mengzi, but have they truly grasped the essential purport of benefit and goodness? The statement, “It is simply firmness, softness, goodness, evil, and the mean,” is most comprehensive in meaning. Yet it is also said, “Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are the guiding principles of human nature.” What evil, then, could there be to change? The statement, “Nature is the embodied form of the Way; the mind is the outer wall of nature,” offers excellent definitions. Yet it is also said, “Establish the foundation from within; bring its functioning to realization from without.” How, then, can this embodied form and its outer wall be divided? All four scholars regard Zisi as the orthodox transmitter, but have they truly grasped the meaning of the term “Heaven’s mandate”?

“Life is what is meant by nature” was Gaozi’s mistaken claim. Yet eating, drinking, and relations between men and women belong to the activities of life. Why, then, call them all nature? To describe nature in terms of evil was Xunzi’s error: evil is, after all, the perversity of qi. Why, then, say that it too must be called nature? Having defined the activity of nature as the feelings, they also define the activity of nature as the mind. Does this mean that “the mind governs nature and the feelings” is wrong? Having defined being stirred into activity by things as desire, they also describe nature as incapable of remaining unaffected. Does this mean that “utterly still and unaffected” is wrong? The deeper their investigations, the more extended their explanations become.

Now, if one speaks exclusively in terms of the closeness of human natures, the account is undifferentiated and seems to mingle good and evil. If one speaks in terms of Heaven’s mandate, the account is too broad and places the life of humans and other beings on the same footing. If one speaks in terms of benefit and goodness, the account is too lofty and leaves out the endowment of qi and material constitution. This is no different from the various…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
儒之角出以相勝也折衷之論必以告
於執事者
問氏族之重自古記之要皆掌於王官者
也五代以降散佚不傳士庶子孫别而
爲氏者不勝其多或氏於國或氏於謚
或氏於官或氏於爵或氏於事枝分縷
析叅錯而難考固也至於近代則世守
一氏相傳而不變固宜其簡而易知矣
而人顧罕能辨其源焉何也昔柳芳作
===
氏族論謂漢高帝興徒步始尚官魏氏
立九品始尚姓至謂山東之人尚婚姻
江右之人尚人物關中之人尚冠冕代
北之人尚貴戚果若是其不同耶滇南
雖在荒徼外自漢唐通道置郡卽有中
土人士錯居其間至我
朝洪武中始開拓成一統又取衣冠之族分
置列郡然則今日滇中士族固中國之
流裔也諸士子生長斯土必能推知其
punctuated:
儒之角出以相勝也。折衷之論，必以告於執事者。

問：氏族之重，自古記之，要皆掌於王官者也。五代以降，散佚不傳，士庶子孫别而爲氏者，不勝其多。或氏於國，或氏於謚，或氏於官，或氏於爵，或氏於事，枝分縷析，叅錯而難考，固也。至於近代，則世守一氏，相傳而不變，固宜其簡而易知矣。而人顧罕能辨其源焉，何也？昔柳芳作《氏族論》，謂漢高帝興徒步，始尚官；魏氏立九品，始尚姓。至謂山東之人尚婚姻，江右之人尚人物，關中之人尚冠冕，代北之人尚貴戚，果若是其不同耶？滇南雖在荒徼外，自漢唐通道置郡，卽有中土人士錯居其間。至我朝洪武中，始開拓成一統，又取衣冠之族分置列郡。然則今日滇中士族，固中國之流裔也。諸士子生長斯土，必能推知其
translation_en:
…the Confucian scholars putting forward rival views to prevail over one another. Be sure to present a balanced judgment to those conducting this examination.

Question: The importance of clans and lineages has been recorded since antiquity, and their records were, in the main, kept by royal officials. From the Five Dynasties onward, these records were dispersed and lost, and ceased to be transmitted. Descendants of men of service and commoners who branched off and adopted surnames were innumerable. Some took surnames from a state, some from a posthumous title, some from an office, some from a noble rank, and some from an event. With branches dividing and subdividing, their tangled relationships were naturally difficult to trace. In more recent times, however, families have maintained a single surname, transmitting it unchanged from generation to generation. This should surely make matters simple and easy to understand. Yet people seldom can distinguish their origins. Why is this?

In his Discourse on Clans and Lineages, Liu Fang stated that when Emperor Gao of Han rose from the ranks of ordinary men, official position first came to be prized; when the Wei ruling house established the nine ranks, pedigree first came to be prized. He went so far as to say that the people of Shandong prized marriage alliances, those of Jiangyou prized outstanding individuals, those of Guanzhong prized official rank, and those of Daibei prized noble imperial relatives. Were their preferences truly so different?

Although Diannan lies beyond the remote frontier, once routes were opened and commanderies established under the Han and Tang, people from the central lands came to live interspersed among its inhabitants. Only in the Hongwu reign of our dynasty was the territory opened up and brought under unified rule; families of official standing were also taken and settled throughout its prefectures. Thus the gentry lineages of Yunnan today are indeed descendants of people from the central lands. You examination candidates, born and raised in this land, must be able to trace their…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
本矣願論其世與其所尚以觀博雅之
學
問古者兵農合而文武出於一後世兵農
分而文武出於二古者國有大師則公
卿寔職之如有扈之戰乃召六卿南征
之役方叔涖止之類是也有因地出兵
者則列國寔職之如征徐命魯公追貊
以韓侯之類是也逮及春秋晉楚用兵
此意猶存其詳可得聞與後世兵農旣
===
判文武殊途章縫之士諱言戰伐而世
俗之論亦謂書生不可任以軍旅矣若
夫推誠布公以討賊興劉爲事者豈章
句之儒哉而史臣反以短於將略譏之
聞雞起舞以廓清中原自誓者非忠義
之士乎而史臣復以職爲貪亂少之能
爲攻心之說矣而不免街亭之敗能爲
鑄錢之議矣而不免陳濤斜之敗謂儒
者無裨於成敗非過也然經略陝西遏
punctuated:
本矣。願論其世與其所尚，以觀博雅之學。
問：古者兵農合，而文武出於一；後世兵農分，而文武出於二。古者國有大師，則公卿寔職之，如有扈之戰乃召六卿、南征之役方叔涖止之類是也。有因地出兵者，則列國寔職之，如征徐命魯公、追貊以韓侯之類是也。逮及春秋，晉楚用兵，此意猶存，其詳可得聞與？後世兵農旣判，文武殊途，章縫之士諱言戰伐，而世俗之論亦謂書生不可任以軍旅矣。若夫推誠布公，以討賊興劉爲事者，豈章句之儒哉？而史臣反以短於將略譏之。聞雞起舞，以廓清中原自誓者，非忠義之士乎？而史臣復以職爲貪亂少之。能爲攻心之說矣，而不免街亭之敗；能爲鑄錢之議矣，而不免陳濤斜之敗。謂儒者無裨於成敗，非過也。然經略陝西，遏
translation_en:
…their origins. Discuss their lineages and what they esteem, so that we may see the breadth and refinement of your learning.
Policy question: In antiquity, soldiers and farmers were one, and civil and military pursuits came from a single source; in later ages, soldiers and farmers were separated, and civil and military pursuits came from two different sources. In antiquity, when the state undertook a major military expedition, its dukes and ministers were indeed responsible for it. Examples include the summoning of the six ministers for the battle against Youhu, and Fang Shu’s arrival to command the southern expedition. When troops were raised on a territorial basis, the regional states were indeed responsible: examples include ordering the Duke of Lu to campaign against Xu and employing the Marquis of Han to pursue the Mo. Even in the Spring and Autumn period, this principle remained in the military operations of Jin and Chu. May we hear its particulars?
In later ages, soldiers and farmers had become separate, and civil and military pursuits followed different paths. Men wearing the caps of scholars shunned talk of warfare, while common opinion likewise held that scholars could not be entrusted with military affairs. Yet was the man who acted with sincerity and impartiality, making it his task to punish rebels and restore the Liu house, merely a scholar of textual minutiae? The historian nevertheless criticized him for shortcomings in generalship. Was the man who rose at cockcrow to practice swordsmanship, vowing to clear the Central Plain of enemies, not a man of loyalty and righteousness? Yet the historian again disparaged him as simply eager for disorder [?]. One could advance the doctrine of winning over hearts, yet could not avert the defeat at Jieting; another could propose the casting of coinage, yet could not avert the defeat at Chentaoxie. To say that Confucian scholars contribute nothing toward securing victory or averting defeat is no excessive criticism. Yet, in directing affairs in Shaanxi and checking…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
元昊之跳梁而軍中有一韓一范之謡
犒師江上破金虜之輈張而宿將有吾
輩愧汗之言又非儒者之效哉今
聖明在上文武忠良之臣咸奮勵以圖表見誠
千載一時也諸生固
國家之所培養以待用者卽使他日當折衝
之任必不以章句自諉而思以古人自
期待也錯綜人物因以道志執事者願
有聞焉
===
問班固謂春秋內中國外四夷而繼之曰
地不可耕民不可畜固矣然自滇省觀
之則以中國之人而處夷僰之間其所
謂夷僰者固亦耕田供稅非化外不五
穀不布帛者也故郭欽之疏江統之論
昔人以爲萬世之長策者殆不可承用
於玆土矣邇者羣蠻不靖致勤師旅雖
折首獲醜旋卽厎定顧撲滅之勳孰與
輯綏玆欲不假兵威使自讋服者抑有
punctuated:
元昊之跳梁，而軍中有「一韓一范」之謡；犒師江上，破金虜之輈張，而宿將有「吾輩愧汗」之言，又非儒者之效哉？今聖明在上，文武忠良之臣咸奮勵以圖表見，誠千載一時也！諸生固國家之所培養以待用者，卽使他日當折衝之任，必不以章句自諉，而思以古人自期待也。錯綜人物，因以道志，執事者願有聞焉。

問：班固謂《春秋》內中國、外四夷，而繼之曰：「地不可耕，民不可畜。」固矣。然自滇省觀之，則以中國之人而處夷僰之間，其所謂夷僰者，固亦耕田供稅，非化外不五穀、不布帛者也。故郭欽之疏、江統之論，昔人以爲萬世之長策者，殆不可承用於玆土矣。邇者羣蠻不靖，致勤師旅，雖折首獲醜，旋卽厎定，顧撲滅之勳孰與輯綏？玆欲不假兵威，使自讋服者，抑有
translation_en:
…Yuanhao’s rampages were checked, and the troops sang of “a Han and a Fan”; when troops were rewarded beside the Yangzi and the Jin invaders’ onslaught was defeated, veteran generals said, “We sweat with shame.” Were these not also achievements of Confucian scholars? Now a sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, and loyal and worthy civil and military officials all exert themselves, seeking to distinguish themselves through service. This is truly an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years! You students are those whom the state has nurtured in preparation for service. Should you one day bear responsibility for repelling aggression, you surely will not excuse yourselves as mere scholars of textual interpretation, but will aspire to measure up to the men of antiquity. Compare and assess these figures, and thereby express your own aspirations. We who conduct this examination wish to hear your views.

Question: Ban Gu said that the Spring and Autumn Annals treats the Central States as the inner realm and the barbarians of the four quarters as the outer, adding: “Their lands cannot be cultivated, and their people cannot be nurtured.” Granted. Yet viewed from Yunnan Province, people of the Central States live among the Yi and Bo, and those called Yi and Bo also till fields and pay taxes. They are not people beyond the reach of civilizing influence who neither grow the five grains nor use cloth and silk. Thus Guo Qin’s memorial and Jiang Tong’s discourse, which earlier men regarded as enduring policies for ten thousand generations, probably cannot be adopted here. Recently, unrest among the various Man peoples necessitated military expeditions. Although their leaders were beheaded and their followers captured, and order was quickly restored, how do the merits of extermination compare with those of conciliation and pacification? Now, if we wish to make them submit in awe of their own accord without resorting to military force, might there be…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
道乎嘗讀元樞使李京作雲南志謂孔
明用其豪傑而財賦足以給軍國梁毗
清節自持酋長感悅不然即冤憤竊發
勢實使然虞集以為其術最簡易可鑒
觀其信然否諸生擇其可行者以為當
路之助可也
punctuated: 道乎？嘗讀元樞使李京作《雲南志》，謂孔明用其豪傑，而財賦足以給軍國；梁毗清節自持，酋長感悅；不然，即冤憤竊發，勢實使然。虞集以為其術最簡易，可鑒觀。其信然否？諸生擇其可行者，以為當路之助，可也。
translation_en: …a way to do so? I once read the Gazetteer of Yunnan (Yunnan zhi), written by Li Jing, a Yuan-dynasty Military Affairs Commissioner. It states that Kongming employed the region’s outstanding men, and its revenues sufficed to support the army and the state; Liang Pi maintained his integrity and purity of conduct, and the chieftains were moved and pleased. Otherwise, resentment at injustice would erupt into covert rebellion: circumstances themselves would make this happen. Yu Ji considered these methods exceedingly simple and easy to implement, and worthy of study as a guide. Is this indeed so? You candidates may select those measures that can be put into practice, thereby assisting those in authority.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人四十名
第一名許鎡石屏州學生詩
第二名張震蒙化府學生書
第三名李維唐雲南府學生易
第四名楊道東姚安府學生春秋
第五名俞世傑楚雄縣學生禮記
第六名趙友仁臨安府學生詩
第七名許嘉榮臨安府學增廣生易
===
第八名木從繩保山縣學生書
第九名曾婥臨安府學生詩
第十名蘇湖大理府學增廣生易
第十一名楊京趙州學生春秋
第十二名鐵世材永昌府學生詩
第十三名馬騰漢臨安府學生易
第十四名施從政安寧州學生書
第十五名李三樂劒川州學生詩
第十六名許國良石屏州學附學生易
punctuated:
中式舉人四十名。
第一名許鎡，石屏州學生，詩。
第二名張震，蒙化府學生，書。
第三名李維唐，雲南府學生，易。
第四名楊道東，姚安府學生，春秋。
第五名俞世傑，楚雄縣學生，禮記。
第六名趙友仁，臨安府學生，詩。
第七名許嘉榮，臨安府學增廣生，易。
第八名木從繩，保山縣學生，書。
第九名曾婥，臨安府學生，詩。
第十名蘇湖，大理府學增廣生，易。
第十一名楊京，趙州學生，春秋。
第十二名鐵世材，永昌府學生，詩。
第十三名馬騰漢，臨安府學生，易。
第十四名施從政，安寧州學生，書。
第十五名李三樂，劒川州學生，詩。

===
隨在而心與理遇斯可以語行矣夫忠信篤敬
之理達之天下而根於心者也心一不存其將
何以行之哉子張以務外之心問行夫子欲其
於心求之也若曰行之機非由於外至心之理
未易以遽純忠信篤敬之行乎蠻貊固也然豈
待行焉而後用其力哉何則忠信者非可以僞
爲也其必未言之先所以顧諟之者常存存而
不息篤敬者非可以色取也其必未行之先所
以服膺之者恒亹亹而匪懈方其立也本無所
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

translation_en:

Four Books

Xu Zi 許鎡

Comment by Associate Examiner Pu, Instructor: “His wording and understanding of principle do not follow current fashions. This can serve as a model; include it.”

Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: “He brings out what contemporary examination essays have yet to express.”

Only when the mind encounters principle wherever one may be can we speak of acting. The principles of loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence extend throughout the world and are rooted in the mind. Once the mind ceases to preserve them, how could one put them into practice? Zizhang asked about acting with a mind intent on outward things; the Master wished him to seek the answer within his mind. It was as though he said: “The mainspring of action does not come from outside; the principles within the mind cannot readily be made pure all at once. Certainly, loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence hold good even among the Man and Mo peoples. But why wait until acting among them before applying oneself to these principles? Why is this so? Loyalty and trustworthiness cannot be counterfeited. Even before speaking, one must constantly preserve, without interruption, the attention through which one keeps these principles in view. Earnestness and reverence cannot be attained through outward appearance. Even before acting, one must remain constantly diligent and unflagging in holding them close to one’s heart. title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於參也而心不忘道固有前若為參者焉參不
以象而以神其吾心對越之真乎方其在輿也
本無所於倚也而心不忘道固有衡若為倚者
焉倚不以迹而以理其吾心陟降之實乎道體
無往而非真心體隨時而常覺斯固君子存誠
之學也而何以利於行耶蓋言固所以行也其
未施信而民信者非言所能與行亦所以行也
其未施敬而民敬者非行所能為惟未言而忠
信之理存焉夫然後其言者皆立與在輿之心
===
也天地雖至大且不能違況囿於天地者乎惟
未行而篤敬之理存焉夫然後其行者皆參前
倚衡之心也豚魚雖難化且無不孚況未必豚
魚者乎故曰雖蠻貊之邦行矣是行也者固必
有為之先者也子欲求行可不俛焉先於心求
之而徒以務外為哉雖然此內聖外王之學也
存其心而蠻貊可行者感應之自然也若以行
乎蠻貊之故而始存其心則雖其所存者不越
乎天理而憧憧往來亦卒歸於偽焉已矣故天
punctuated: 於參也，而心不忘道，固有前若為參者焉。參不以象而以神，其吾心對越之真乎？方其在輿也，本無所於倚也，而心不忘道，固有衡若為倚者焉。倚不以迹而以理，其吾心陟降之實乎？道體無往而非真，心體隨時而常覺，斯固君子存誠之學也，而何以利於行耶？蓋言固所以行也，其未施信而民信者，非言所能與；行亦所以行也，其未施敬而民敬者，非行所能為。惟未言而忠信之理存焉，夫然後其言者皆立與在輿之心也。天地雖至大，且不能違，況囿於天地者乎？惟未行而篤敬之理存焉，夫然後其行者皆參前倚衡之心也。豚魚雖難化，且無不孚，況未必豚魚者乎？故曰：「雖蠻貊之邦行矣。」是行也者，固必有為之先者也。子欲求行，可不俛焉先於心求之，而徒以務外為哉？雖然，此內聖外王之學也。存其心而蠻貊可行者，感應之自然也。若以行乎蠻貊之故而始存其心，則雖其所存者不越乎天理，而憧憧往來，亦卒歸於偽焉已矣。故天
translation_en:
…for these principles to stand before him; yet because his mind does not forget the Way, there is indeed something before him, as though they stood there. They stand there not as an image but as a spiritual presence: is this not the truth of my mind’s reverent attendance upon them? When he is in his carriage, there is originally nothing resting against its crossbar; yet because his mind does not forget the Way, there is indeed something at the crossbar, as though these principles rested there. They rest there not as a physical trace but as principle: is this not the reality of my mind’s activity in ascending and descending? The substance of the Way is real wherever one goes, and the substance of the mind remains aware at all times. This is indeed the gentleman’s learning of preserving sincerity. But how does it enable him to conduct himself successfully?

Speech is certainly a means of conducting oneself. Yet that the people trust him before he has displayed trustworthiness is something speech cannot accomplish. Conduct, too, is a means of making one’s way. Yet that the people respect him before he has displayed reverence is something conduct cannot achieve. Only when the principles of wholeheartedness and trustworthiness are preserved before he speaks will all his words express the mind he maintains both when standing and when riding in his carriage. Vast though Heaven and Earth are, even they cannot run counter to it; how much less can those encompassed by Heaven and Earth! Only when the principles of earnestness and reverence are preserved before he acts will all his actions express the mind that sees them standing before him and resting against the carriage crossbar. Difficult though pigs and fish are to transform, even they invariably respond to sincerity; how much more will those who are not necessarily like pigs and fish! Thus it is said: “Even in the lands of the Man and Mo, he can conduct himself successfully.” Such successful conduct must indeed have something that precedes it. If you wish to conduct yourself successfully, can you fail to apply yourself first to seeking this within your mind, and merely attend to external things?

Nevertheless, this is the learning of inward sagehood and outward kingliness. That one can conduct oneself successfully among the Man and Mo by preserving one’s mind is the natural working of influence and response. If, however, one begins to preserve one’s mind only for the sake of conducting oneself successfully among the Man and Mo, then, even though what one preserves does not depart from heavenly principle, one’s restless coming and going in thought will ultimately amount to nothing but contrivance. Thus, Heaven…

text:

咸無心者也而易以速言之觀於此可以知無
心之感其感深矣
天地之道博也厚也高也明也悠也久也
今夫天斯昭昭之多及其無窮也日月
星辰繫焉萬物覆焉今夫地一撮土之
多及其廣厚載華嶽而不重振河海而
不洩萬物載焉今夫山一卷石之多及
其廣大草木生之禽獸居之寶藏興焉
===
今夫水一勺之多及其不測黿鼉蛟龍
魚鼈生焉貨財殖焉
李維唐

矣
考試官教諭毛 批 辭不費而意已盡
考試官學正王 批 渾厚且曲盡可錄以式矣
中庸本造化之極盛而因著其生物之功焉夫

punctuated:
下之人，可以無心感之，不可以有心必之也。夫咸，無心者也，而《易》以速言之。觀於此，可以知無心之感，其感深矣。
天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。今夫天，斯昭昭之多，及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多，及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。今夫山，一卷石之多，及其廣大，草木生之，禽獸居之，寶藏興焉。今夫水，一勺之多，及其不測，黿鼉蛟龍魚鼈生焉，貨財殖焉。

《中庸》本造化之極盛，而因著其生物之功焉。夫造化之所本，誠而已矣，則其極盛而生物者，非
translation_en:
…the people of the world may be moved without deliberate intention, but one cannot deliberately insist upon moving them. Xian (Influence) is without intention—the character 咸 is 感, “to move,” without its “heart” component—and the Book of Changes speaks of its swiftness. From this one may understand how profound is the influence exerted without deliberate intention.
The way of Heaven and Earth is broad, substantial, lofty, bright, enduring, and lasting. Now Heaven is merely this accumulation of shining light; yet in its boundlessness, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended within it, and all things are covered by it. Earth is merely a handful of soil; yet in its breadth and depth, it bears Mount Hua without finding it heavy, holds the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and supports all things. A mountain is merely a small stone; yet in its breadth and greatness, plants and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell upon it, and precious deposits arise within it. Water is merely a spoonful; yet in its unfathomable depths, giant turtles, alligators, dragons, fish, and soft-shelled turtles live, and goods and wealth proliferate.
Li Weitang
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Words that reach the principle naturally stand apart. This may rank first among all the candidates.”

What these creative transformations rest upon is sincerity alone. Thus, that which attains supreme fullness and brings things into being—is it not …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
一誠之所爲與此中庸以言天道也若曰誠者
聖人之本亦天地之本也觀聖人所以隆無疆
之業盍觀天地所以妙不測之功者乎夫天地
惟其不貳也則實理所積含弘妙無方之化而
靜深立萬有之根博且厚焉地道何盛也實理
所發清通超峻極之神而輝光被萬象之表高
且明焉天道何盛也且往來不迫引之後先而
不匱其行寬裕有常窮之終始而莫得其朕是
悠也乆也所謂乾健之不息坤順之無疆天地
===
之所爲極盛者也夫其盛如此則其生物之功
何如今自昭昭以言天固生物之無幾也極之
而無窮則日月懸象星辰爲章盡萬物而覆之
孰非天之統元氣者乎自一撮以言地固生物
之有限也極之而廣厚則河海淵涵華嶽奠麗
盡萬物而載之孰非地之統元形者乎結而爲
山不止卷石及廣大之極則草木之繁蕪也禽
獸之咸若也而寳藏亦發其英華矣融而爲水
不止一勺及不測之極則黿鼉蛟龍之胤靈也
punctuated: 一誠之所爲與？此中庸以言天道也。若曰：誠者，聖人之本，亦天地之本也。觀聖人所以隆無疆之業，盍觀天地所以妙不測之功者乎？夫天地惟其不貳也，則實理所積，含弘妙無方之化，而靜深立萬有之根，博且厚焉，地道何盛也！實理所發，清通超峻極之神，而輝光被萬象之表，高且明焉，天道何盛也！且往來不迫，引之後先而不匱其行；寬裕有常，窮之終始而莫得其朕。是悠也，乆也，所謂乾健之不息、坤順之無疆，天地之所爲極盛者也。夫其盛如此，則其生物之功何如？今自昭昭以言天，固生物之無幾也；極之而無窮，則日月懸象，星辰爲章，盡萬物而覆之，孰非天之統元氣者乎？自一撮以言地，固生物之有限也；極之而廣厚，則河海淵涵，華嶽奠麗，盡萬物而載之，孰非地之統元形者乎？結而爲山，不止卷石，及廣大之極，則草木之繁蕪也，禽獸之咸若也，而寳藏亦發其英華矣。融而爲水，不止一勺，及不測之極，則黿鼉蛟龍之胤靈也，
translation_en:
…the work of a single sincerity? This is how the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven. It is as though it said: sincerity is the foundation of the sage and also the foundation of Heaven and Earth. To see how the sage brings boundless achievements to greatness, should we not observe how Heaven and Earth wondrously accomplish their unfathomable work? Because Heaven and Earth are undivided, substantial principle accumulates: embracing and accommodating all, it wondrously effects transformations without fixed bounds, while in stillness and depth it establishes the root of all existence. Broad and thick—how flourishing is the Way of Earth! Substantial principle issues forth: pure and unobstructed, its spiritual efficacy surpasses the loftiest heights, while its radiance clothes the outward forms of all phenomena. High and bright—how flourishing is the Way of Heaven! Moreover, their coming and going are unhurried; extend them backward and forward in time, and their movement is never exhausted. Spacious and constant, they yield no discernible trace even when pursued from beginning to end. This is their far-reaching duration and their enduring constancy: what is called the unceasing vigor of Qian and the boundless compliance of Kun. These constitute the utmost flourishing of Heaven and Earth.

Since their flourishing is such, what is their achievement in bringing things into being? If we speak of Heaven as merely a small patch of brightness, it can indeed bring few things into being. But taken to its utmost, it is inexhaustible: the sun and moon hang as images, the stars and constellations form patterns, and it covers every living thing. Which of these is not an expression of Heaven’s governance of primordial qi? If we speak of Earth as merely a pinch of soil, its capacity to bring things into being is indeed limited. But taken to its utmost breadth and thickness, rivers and seas are contained within its depths, Mount Hua and the other great peaks stand firmly upon it, and it bears every living thing. Which of these is not an expression of Earth’s governance of primordial form?

凝Congealing into mountains, it is more than a fist-sized stone. At the utmost extent of their breadth and greatness, plants and trees grow luxuriantly, birds and beasts all thrive, and precious deposits also reveal their finest splendor. Flowing together as water, it is more than a single ladleful. At the utmost extent of its unfathomable depths, great turtles, alligators, and dragons propagate their numinous kind [?] …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
魚鼈之滋息也而貨財亦豐於利用矣是山水
之生物孰非天地之所爲生物者乎吁其極盛
也聖人同體之妙也其不測也聖人同用之神
也體妙用神非天下之至誠其孰能與於此雖
然誠非自外至也吾性分中之實理也天地具
此實理運乎無疆聖人體此實理配乎天地故
聖人者天地之心天地者聖人之郛郭而實理
者天地聖人合一不測之蘊也學者不知而求
之瀰漫六合之際不若反而求之性分之中立
===
其誠焉而天下之道歸矣
公事畢然後敢治私事
張震
同考試官教諭盧批田制旣定則斯民奉公之意自
有不容已者此作得之
考試官教諭毛批善道斯民意中事
考試官學正王批發明先公之義曲盡
卽治田者必先于公而田制之善見矣夫人情
莫不顧其私也井田之民不敢以私先公非立
punctuated:
魚鼈之滋息也，而貨財亦豐於利用矣。是山水之生物，孰非天地之所爲生物者乎？吁！其極盛也，聖人同體之妙也；其不測也，聖人同用之神也。體妙用神，非天下之至誠，其孰能與於此？雖然，誠非自外至也，吾性分中之實理也。天地具此實理，運乎無疆；聖人體此實理，配乎天地。故聖人者，天地之心；天地者，聖人之郛郭；而實理者，天地聖人合一不測之蘊也。學者不知而求之瀰漫六合之際，不若反而求之性分之中，立其誠焉，而天下之道歸矣。
公事畢，然後敢治私事。
張震
同考試官教諭盧批：田制旣定，則斯民奉公之意，自有不容已者，此作得之。
考試官教諭毛批：善道斯民意中事。
考試官學正王批：發明先公之義曲盡。
卽治田者必先于公，而田制之善見矣。夫人情莫不顧其私也，井田之民不敢以私先公，非立
translation_en:
…fish and turtles multiply, and material resources also abound for practical use. Of the living things produced by mountains and waters, which are not produced through Heaven and Earth? Ah! Their utmost abundance is the subtlety of the substance the sage shares with them; their unfathomability is the wondrous efficacy of the functioning the sage shares with them. With such subtlety of substance and wondrous efficacy of functioning, who but one possessed of the utmost sincerity in all the world could participate in this? Yet sincerity does not come from outside: it is the real principle within our inherent nature. Heaven and Earth possess this real principle and operate without limit; the sage embodies this real principle and matches Heaven and Earth. Thus the sage is the heart of Heaven and Earth; Heaven and Earth are the sage’s outer walls; and real principle is the unfathomable inner essence through which Heaven, Earth, and the sage become one. Scholars who do not understand this seek it throughout the vast expanse of the six directions. Better to turn back and seek it within their own inherent nature: establish sincerity there, and all the ways of the world converge upon it.
“Only after public work is finished do they dare attend to private work.”
Zhang Zhen
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: Once the land system is established, the people’s intention to serve the public interest naturally becomes irrepressible. This composition captures that.
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: It aptly expresses what is in these people’s minds.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: It elucidates exhaustively, in all its particulars, the meaning of putting public duties first.
Even those who cultivate the fields must give priority to public work, and therein the excellence of the land system becomes apparent. Now, it is human nature for everyone to attend to private interests. Yet the people under the well-field system did not dare put private work before public work. Were it not for the establishment…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
法之善其何以有此哉孟子告畢戰以井田之
制而及此也意若曰不觀斯民趨事之情無以
見先王經制之備蓋自井田之法行而中外之
界定治公田以為君子之養者其事謂之公治
私田以為小人之依者其事謂之私斯民於此
何以用情哉謂公田雖屬乎公然非上之所能
自治也故公事未治則不敢以或後謂私田雖
切於身然非可與公田比也故公事未畢則不
敢以或先時乎東作也必助耕之既終而後躬
===
耕者乃得以盡駿發之力時乎西成也必公田
之既穫而後受田者乃得以收穡人之功是非
不以百畝之不易為已憂也而所務有大於此
者以為吾人之得利其利皆上之賜故雨澤之
降於天尚冀公田之先被也况吾之奉乎公者
而敢或怠哉非不以農事之不可緩為已慮也
而所急有甚於此者以為吾人之得樂其樂皆
上之惠故雨澤之普於施尚欲私田之後及也
况其力之出於身者而敢自愛哉嗣爾股肱皆
punctuated: 法之善，其何以有此哉？孟子告畢戰以井田之制而及此也，意若曰：不觀斯民趨事之情，無以見先王經制之備。蓋自井田之法行，而中外之界定，治公田以為君子之養者，其事謂之公；治私田以為小人之依者，其事謂之私。斯民於此，何以用情哉？謂公田雖屬乎公，然非上之所能自治也，故公事未治，則不敢以或後；謂私田雖切於身，然非可與公田比也，故公事未畢，則不敢以或先。時乎東作也，必助耕之既終，而後躬耕者乃得以盡駿發之力；時乎西成也，必公田之既穫，而後受田者乃得以收穡人之功。是非不以百畝之不易為已憂也，而所務有大於此者，以為吾人之得利，其利皆上之賜，故雨澤之降於天，尚冀公田之先被也，况吾之奉乎公者，而敢或怠哉？非不以農事之不可緩為已慮也，而所急有甚於此者，以為吾人之得樂，其樂皆上之惠，故雨澤之普於施，尚欲私田之後及也，况其力之出於身者，而敢自愛哉？嗣爾股肱，皆
translation_en:
…the excellence of the regulations—how else could this have come about? When Mengzi explained the well-field system to Bi Zhan and reached this point, his meaning was as follows: unless one observes the disposition with which the people attend to their tasks, one cannot perceive the completeness of the former kings’ institutions. Once the well-field system was implemented, the boundaries between the central and outer plots were fixed. Cultivating the public field to provide sustenance for the governing gentlemen was called public business; cultivating the private fields to provide a livelihood for the common people was called private business. How, then, did the people direct their concerns?

They considered that, although the public field belonged to the public domain, those above could not cultivate it themselves. Thus, while public work remained undone, they dared not let it fall behind. They considered that, although their private fields directly concerned their own livelihood, these could not rank alongside the public field. Thus, until public work was finished, they dared not give their own work precedence. At the time of spring cultivation, they had to complete their labor in aid of the public field before those cultivating their own plots could devote their full strength to vigorous plowing. At the time of the autumn harvest, the public field had to be reaped before those allotted fields could gather the fruits of their husbandry.

It was not that they felt no concern about their hundred mu remaining uncultivated; rather, they had a greater duty to pursue. They believed that whatever benefits they enjoyed were all gifts from those above. Thus, even when rain descended from Heaven, they hoped that the public field would receive it first. How, then, could they dare be negligent in their own service to the public? It was not that they were unconcerned about the urgency of agricultural work; rather, something else demanded still greater urgency. They believed that whatever happiness they enjoyed came entirely from the kindness of those above. Thus, even when rain spread its bounty everywhere, they wished their private fields to receive it only afterward. How, then, could they dare spare the strength of their own bodies? ‘Continue the labors of your limbs’—all …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
藉斯民之力而事不容於並施分田制禄皆爲
當務之急而序不容於少紊先後異治而同功
公私異分而各足助法之善何以踰此不然則
公私無辨與貢法等耳何以曰治地莫善於助
耶抑於是而知三代之所以敎民非但學校庠
序爲然也觀治田之事而上下之義明敎道行
乎其間先王體國經野之意深矣不特此也凡
所以使之出入相友守望相助和順親睦固結
聯絡者亦寓兵於農之意也豈特養民敎民巳
===
哉吁後之井田不可復矣爲治者師其意而不
泥其迹可也
易
受兹介福以中正也
許嘉榮
同考試官敎諭許批人臣承寵本於中正此作得之
足占素蘊取之不徒以其文也
考試官敎諭毛批豐潤中有精思
考試官學正王批體製宏邃詞意昌達
punctuated:
藉斯民之力，而事不容於並施。分田制禄，皆爲當務之急，而序不容於少紊。先後異治而同功，公私異分而各足，助法之善何以踰此？不然，則公私無辨，與貢法等耳，何以曰治地莫善於助耶？抑於是而知三代之所以敎民，非但學校庠序爲然也。觀治田之事，而上下之義明，敎道行乎其間，先王體國經野之意深矣！不特此也，凡所以使之出入相友、守望相助、和順親睦、固結聯絡者，亦寓兵於農之意也，豈特養民敎民巳哉？吁！後之井田不可復矣，爲治者師其意而不泥其迹可也。

易
受兹介福，以中正也。
許嘉榮

同考試官敎諭許批：「人臣承寵，本於中正，此作得之，足占素蘊。取之不徒以其文也。」
考試官敎諭毛批：「豐潤中有精思。」
考試官學正王批：「體製宏邃，詞意昌達。」
translation_en:
…rely on the strength of these people, yet the tasks cannot be carried out simultaneously. Allocating fields and establishing emoluments are both urgent matters, but their proper sequence must not be disturbed in the slightest. Though undertaken separately, earlier and later, they contribute to the same result; though public and private shares are distinct, each receives enough. How could anything surpass the excellence of the labor-assistance system? Otherwise, public and private would be indistinguishable, and it would be no different from the tribute system. Why, then, would it be said that no system of managing the land is better than labor assistance? From this we also understand that the Three Dynasties educated the people through more than their schools and academies. Consider the management of the fields: the proper relations between superiors and inferiors became clear, and moral instruction operated within it. Profound indeed was the intention of the former kings in organizing the state and laying out the countryside! Nor was this all. The arrangements that made the people companions in their comings and goings, helpers in keeping watch and ward, harmonious and affectionate toward one another, and firmly bound together also embodied the intention of incorporating military organization into agriculture. Was this merely a matter of nourishing and educating the people? Alas! In later ages the well-field system cannot be restored. Those who govern should emulate its intent without clinging rigidly to its outward forms.

Book of Changes
“He receives this great blessing because he is central and correct.”
Xu Jiarong

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “A minister’s receipt of favor is rooted in centrality and correctness. This composition grasps that point and sufficiently reveals the learning he has long cultivated. Its selection is not based merely on its literary qualities.”

Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: “Within its richness and fullness there is finely considered thought.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Its form and structure are expansive and profound; its language and ideas are abundant and lucid.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
象申爻之承天寵者而著其由於德也夫臣之
福莫大乎承天之寵也二以中正之德承之斯
其為明良相遭之盛與且晉之六五以柔中之
德履上行之位而際文明之世固宜天之福之
以錫其極于天下也而為人臣者亦孰不願輸
忠于時而共迓乎天之休也然有不可必得者
矣晉六二之辭曰受玆介福是為臣者宅臣鄰
之寄非獨詔之爵已也而遐福於是乎仰承膺
弼直之司非徒詔之祿已也而繁祉於是乎駢
===
錫王者祈天以永命萬福固攸同矣而王者不
以自私也祈天之祐與佐代天之責者共焉帝
心簡在二寔有以臻其盛矣維皇建極以錫民
五福固時斂矣而維皇不以獨享也建極之祜
與身輔極之任者同焉帝賚方殷二寔有以值
其休矣玆固六五之介福而二受之也然豈五
之私於二哉蓋福者人君厚下之典也德者人
臣承福之基也六二居中而得正焉是其精一
之功懋於緝熈既以昭夫明德之體居貞之守
punctuated: 象申爻之承天寵者，而著其由於德也。夫臣之福，莫大乎承天之寵也。二以中正之德承之，斯其為明良相遭之盛與！且晉之六五，以柔中之德，履上行之位，而際文明之世，固宜天之福之，以錫其極于天下也。而為人臣者，亦孰不願輸忠于時，而共迓乎天之休也？然有不可必得者矣。晉六二之辭曰：「受玆介福。」是為臣者，宅臣鄰之寄，非獨詔之爵已也，而遐福於是乎仰承；膺弼直之司，非徒詔之祿已也，而繁祉於是乎駢錫。王者祈天以永命，萬福固攸同矣，而王者不以自私也。祈天之祐，與佐代天之責者共焉。帝心簡在，二寔有以臻其盛矣。維皇建極以錫民，五福固時斂矣，而維皇不以獨享也。建極之祜，與身輔極之任者同焉。帝賚方殷，二寔有以值其休矣。玆固六五之介福，而二受之也。然豈五之私於二哉？蓋福者，人君厚下之典也；德者，人臣承福之基也。六二居中而得正焉，是其精一之功懋於緝熈，既以昭夫明德之體；居貞之守，
translation_en:
The Commentary on the Images elaborates upon the line’s reception of the sovereign’s favor, making clear that it derives from virtue. For a minister, no blessing is greater than receiving the sovereign’s favor. The second line receives it through the virtues of centrality and correctness: is this not the splendid meeting of an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister?

Moreover, the six in the fifth place of Jin (Advance), possessing the virtue of yielding centrality, occupies the position of upward advance and encounters an age of luminous culture. It is surely fitting that Heaven should bless the ruler, enabling him to bestow his supreme standard upon all under Heaven. And among those who serve as ministers, who would not wish to offer their loyalty to the age and together welcome Heaven’s favor? Yet this is not something they can be certain of obtaining.

The statement for the six in the second place of Jin says, “Receive this great blessing.” Thus, when a minister occupies a position of trust as the ruler’s close associate, it is not merely a rank that is conferred upon him: enduring blessings are thereby reverently received from above. When he undertakes the office of assisting and correcting the ruler, it is not merely a stipend that is conferred upon him: abundant blessings are thereby bestowed together.

The king prays to Heaven to prolong his mandate, and myriad blessings indeed converge upon him; yet he does not keep them for himself. The protection for which he prays to Heaven he shares with those who assist him in discharging his responsibility to act on Heaven’s behalf. Chosen in the sovereign’s heart, the second line truly possesses the means to attain this abundance. The august ruler establishes the supreme standard to bestow blessings upon the people, and the five blessings are indeed gathered together; yet the august ruler does not enjoy them alone. The blessing of establishing the supreme standard he shares with those who personally bear responsibility for sustaining it. As the sovereign’s gifts grow abundant, the second line truly possesses the means to encounter his favor.

These are indeed the great blessings of the six in the fifth place, received by the second. But could this be favoritism on the part of the fifth toward the second? Blessings are the means by which a ruler generously treats his subordinates; virtue is the foundation upon which a minister receives blessings. The six in the second place occupies the center and attains correctness. Its effort to achieve refinement and singleness of purpose flourishes through the continuation of luminous virtue, thereby already making manifest the substance of bright virtue; its steadfast adherence to correctness …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
純於豫養又以裕乎康國之用其立之也中黃
離之德所為協也則上之所以弘建中之治者
在必資焉而承以遐福夫固玄德之升聞者感
之矣不然初之摧如且罔孚也何以結知於明
主哉其行之也正玉鉉之節所為著也則上之
所以敷表正之化者將必賴焉而錫以繁祉夫
固一德之咸有者致之矣不然四之鼫鼠且有
厲也何以承毗於盛王哉噫夫子申易及此其
思以身際其盛而喜幸之意藹然於言表矣大
===
抵臣之幸莫大乎寵之承莫不幸乎有恃寵之
心故人臣遇知於君而益勵其匪懈之節者凡
以盡臣道而保恩寵也苟為不然是先自失其
中正也已何以徼介福於有終哉隨之九四有
之有孚在道以明何咎此人臣居寵之正也
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以為天下利莫大
乎聖人
punctuated:
純於豫養，又以裕乎康國之用。其立之也中，黃離之德所為協也，則上之所以弘建中之治者，在必資焉；而承以遐福，夫固玄德之升聞者感之矣。不然，初之摧如且罔孚也，何以結知於明主哉？其行之也正，玉鉉之節所為著也，則上之所以敷表正之化者，將必賴焉；而錫以繁祉，夫固一德之咸有者致之矣。不然，四之鼫鼠且有厲也，何以承毗於盛王哉？噫！夫子申易及此，其思以身際其盛，而喜幸之意藹然於言表矣。大抵臣之幸，莫大乎寵之承；莫不幸乎有恃寵之心。故人臣遇知於君，而益勵其匪懈之節者，凡以盡臣道而保恩寵也。苟為不然，是先自失其中正也已，何以徼介福於有終哉？隨之九四有之：「有孚在道，以明，何咎？」此人臣居寵之正也。
是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，縣象著明莫大乎日月，崇高莫大乎富貴，備物致用、立成器以為天下利莫大乎聖人。
translation_en:
…is made pure through cultivation beforehand, further enriching his capacity to bring peace to the state. His stance is centered, in accord with the virtue of “yellow radiance.” Thus the ruler must draw upon him to extend a government founded upon the mean. That he receives far-reaching blessings is surely a response to his profound virtue becoming known above. Otherwise, if he were like the initial line, “checked in his advance” and still “not trusted,” how could he win an enlightened ruler’s recognition? His conduct is correct, manifesting the integrity symbolized by the jade carrying bar of the cauldron. Thus the ruler must rely upon him to spread the transforming influence of an upright example. That abundant blessings are bestowed upon him is surely brought about by his full possession of undivided virtue. Otherwise, if he were like the fourth line’s “large rat,” exposed to danger, how could he support and assist a flourishing king? Ah! When the Master elaborated upon the Changes to this point, he thought of personally encountering such flourishing conditions; his joy and sense of good fortune overflowed beyond his words. Generally, no good fortune for a minister exceeds receiving favor, and no misfortune exceeds harboring a disposition to presume upon it. Thus, when a minister wins his ruler’s recognition and strives still harder to maintain tireless integrity, it is entirely to fulfill the minister’s proper role and preserve the ruler’s gracious favor. If he fails to do so, he has already forfeited his own centeredness and correctness. How then can he seek great blessings and carry matters through to a good conclusion? The fourth, yang line of Following (Sui) says: “With sincerity, abiding in the Way, and with clarity, what blame can there be?” This is the proper way for a minister to remain in favor.
Therefore, among models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth; in change and adaptation, none are greater than the four seasons; among images suspended above and shining brightly, none are greater than the sun and moon; in exalted standing, none are greater than wealth and rank; and in providing things for use and fashioning finished implements to benefit all under Heaven, none are greater than the sage.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
蘇湖
同考試官教諭許批闡明莫大之意最爲詳盡而詞
又冲雅深於易者也
考試官教諭毛批詞意典贍傑作也
考試官學正王批明健可錄
大傳欲賛神物之功徵諸造化而歸於聖人也
夫以前民用而配造化神物之功大矣然非聖
人在天子之位其孰能與之以前其用哉夫子
懼天下以卜筮小易也故先言此若曰人知蓍
===
龜之生所以紹天之明而闡易之秘者也抑孰
知其興於德位兼隆之聖人乎夫凡以氣浮者
皆法象也而非其大也天則確然無所不覆有
以宰四時日月之樞大莫大於天矣凡以形附
者皆法象也而非其大也地則隤然無所不載
有以統四時日月之運大莫大於地矣以言乎
變通則四時也者運神道以出入天地之化所
以錯行而不已者此也否則歲成之利幾乎毀
矣孰有大於四時乎以言乎懸象著明則日月
punctuated:
蘇湖

同考試官教諭許批：闡明莫大之意，最爲詳盡，而詞又冲雅，深於易者也。
考試官教諭毛批：詞意典贍，傑作也。
考試官學正王批：明健，可錄。

大傳欲賛神物之功，徵諸造化而歸於聖人也。夫以前民用而配造化，神物之功大矣。然非聖人在天子之位，其孰能與之以前其用哉？夫子懼天下以卜筮小易也，故先言此。若曰：人知蓍龜之生，所以紹天之明而闡易之秘者也，抑孰知其興於德位兼隆之聖人乎？夫凡以氣浮者，皆法象也，而非其大也。天則確然，無所不覆，有以宰四時日月之樞，大莫大於天矣。凡以形附者，皆法象也，而非其大也。地則隤然，無所不載，有以統四時日月之運，大莫大於地矣。以言乎變通，則四時也者，運神道以出入天地之化，所以錯行而不已者，此也。否則歲成之利幾乎毀矣，孰有大於四時乎？以言乎懸象著明，則日月
translation_en:
Su Hu

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: His exposition of the meaning of “none greater” is exceptionally thorough, and his language is also restrained and elegant. He has a profound understanding of the Book of Changes.
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: Classical and ample in both language and thought—a masterpiece.
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: Clear and vigorous; worthy of selection.

The Great Commentary, wishing to praise the efficacy of the numinous objects, adduces the workings of creation as evidence and attributes their achievement ultimately to the sage. In guiding the people’s use of things and matching the workings of creation, the efficacy of the numinous objects is indeed great. Yet unless a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven, who could assist them in thus guiding their use? The Master feared that the world would belittle the Book of Changes as merely a work of divination; hence he first made this statement. It is as though he said: People know that the production of milfoil and tortoises serves to carry forward Heaven’s illumination and disclose the mysteries of the Changes. But who knows that their rise depends upon a sage exalted in both virtue and position?

All things that float by virtue of their vital force offer patterns and images, yet they are not the greatest of these. Heaven, firm and strong, leaves nothing uncovered and governs the pivotal workings of the four seasons, sun, and moon: nothing is greater than Heaven. All things that rest upon the earth by virtue of their physical form offer patterns and images, yet they are not the greatest of these. Earth, yielding and receptive, leaves nothing unsupported and commands the courses of the four seasons, sun, and moon: nothing is greater than Earth.

Speaking of transformation and free passage, the four seasons set the numinous Way in motion, bringing forth and withdrawing the transformations of Heaven and Earth. This is what makes them proceed in alternation without cease. Otherwise, the benefits of the year’s completed cycle would all but be destroyed. What could be greater than the four seasons? Speaking of images suspended on high that shine brightly, the sun and moon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也者麗太虛以旋轉天地之化所以久照而不
窮者此也否則明生之利幾乎息矣孰有大於
日月乎凡此皆造化也以至列爵五焉分土三
焉非不可言崇高矣然其分猶有限也乃若作
君作師而中和建天地之極四時以爲吏也日
月以爲官也制作之權自我操之所謂貴爲天
子富有四海之內者是已其崇高之大何如哉
智者創之巧者述之非不可言利用矣然其用
猶有窮也乃若盡物盡制而裁成極天地之利
===
四時以爲柄也日月以爲量也聰明之德自天
縱之所謂聖人不勉而中不思而得者是已其
利用之大何如哉夫曰富貴則位隆矣曰聖人
則德隆矣二者備而蓍龜興焉此其所以定吉
凶成亹亹而天地之撰斯其體之矣不然其孰
定而孰成之哉雖然神物之興聖人也其所以
幽賛之者亦聖人也是故百莖之生非偶合也
九疇之文非虛出也彼其靈然而生粹然而宰
斯豈泛鍾於氣化者之能哉蓋包犧神禹有以
punctuated: 也者，麗太虛以旋轉天地之化，所以久照而不窮者，此也。否則明生之利幾乎息矣，孰有大於日月乎？凡此皆造化也。以至列爵五焉，分土三焉，非不可言崇高矣，然其分猶有限也。乃若作君作師，而中和建天地之極，四時以爲吏也，日月以爲官也，制作之權自我操之，所謂貴爲天子、富有四海之內者是已。其崇高之大何如哉？智者創之，巧者述之，非不可言利用矣，然其用猶有窮也。乃若盡物盡制，而裁成極天地之利，四時以爲柄也，日月以爲量也，聰明之德自天縱之，所謂聖人不勉而中、不思而得者是已。其利用之大何如哉？夫曰富貴，則位隆矣；曰聖人，則德隆矣。二者備而蓍龜興焉，此其所以定吉凶、成亹亹，而天地之撰斯其體之矣。不然，其孰定而孰成之哉？雖然，神物之興，聖人也；其所以幽賛之者，亦聖人也。是故百莖之生非偶合也，九疇之文非虛出也。彼其靈然而生，粹然而宰，斯豈泛鍾於氣化者之能哉？蓋包犧神禹有以
translation_en:
…the sun and moon cleave to the great void and carry forward the transformations of Heaven and Earth. This is why they shine enduringly without exhaustion. Otherwise, the benefits of their life-giving light would all but cease. What could be greater than the sun and moon? All these belong to the workings of creation. As for establishing five ranks of nobility and dividing territories into three grades, these may indeed be called lofty and exalted, yet their allotted standing remains limited. But consider one who serves as ruler and teacher, establishing through equilibrium and harmony the supreme standard of Heaven and Earth: he takes the four seasons as his clerks and the sun and moon as his officers, and holds in his own hands the authority to create institutions and establish regulations. This is what is meant by being honored as the Son of Heaven and possessing all within the Four Seas as his wealth. How great is the loftiness of such a one!

The wise invent things, and the skillful carry their work forward. This may indeed be called making things useful, yet their usefulness still has limits. But consider one who fully comprehends things and institutions [?], shaping and completing them so as to realize to the utmost the benefits of Heaven and Earth: he takes the four seasons as his handles of authority and the sun and moon as his measures. Heaven itself has endowed him abundantly with the virtue of clear perception. This is what is meant by the sage who hits the mark without effort and attains understanding without deliberation. How great is his achievement in making things useful!

To speak of wealth and honor, then, is to speak of exalted position; to speak of a sage is to speak of exalted virtue. When both are present, milfoil and tortoise-shell divination arise. Through these, auspicious and inauspicious outcomes are determined and tireless endeavors brought to completion; thus the workings of Heaven and Earth are embodied. Otherwise, who could determine the former and accomplish the latter? Nevertheless, it is the sage who brings these numinous objects into use, and it is also the sage who assists their hidden workings.
