Thus the growth of a hundred stalks of milfoil is no mere coincidence, and the text of the Nine Categories did not emerge without cause. Their numinous emergence and their pure power to govern—could these be the accomplishments of things merely endowed at random through the transformations of vital energy? Surely Baoxi and the divine Yu had the means to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
贊之者矣此乾於九五大人所爲言先天也而
作易不與焉噫天人之際其深矣哉
書
織皮崑崙析支渠搜西戎卽叙
木從繩
同考試官敎諭盧批講不治夷狄意得禹貢之旨取
之
考試官敎諭毛批語意明備超出衆作
考試官學正王批雅健不浮必究心於經學者
===
史臣記三國貢物之同而見遠人之順治焉夫
未易感者遠人之心也卽土賦之通於西戎而
順治之功不可見也哉史臣記大禹雍州之成
功而及此也意謂聖人功之所成者大則化之
所及者遠雍州之水土旣平則任土以作貢者
豈但境內之球琳琅玕已哉彼享上者匪物無
以昭其敬而織皮則物之足以爲裘罽者也是
物也奉以入貢者則有河源之崑崙河西之析
支朔方之渠搜焉爲國雖異而所獻則未甞異
punctuated:
贊之者矣。此乾於九五大人所爲言先天也，而作易不與焉。噫！天人之際，其深矣哉！

書
織皮崑崙析支渠搜西戎卽叙。
木從繩

同考試官敎諭盧批：講不治夷狄意，得禹貢之旨，取之。
考試官敎諭毛批：語意明備，超出衆作。
考試官學正王批：雅健不浮，必究心於經學者。

史臣記三國貢物之同，而見遠人之順治焉。夫未易感者，遠人之心也。卽土賦之通於西戎，而順治之功不可見也哉？史臣記大禹雍州之成功而及此也，意謂聖人功之所成者大，則化之所及者遠。雍州之水土旣平，則任土以作貢者，豈但境內之球琳琅玕已哉？彼享上者，匪物無以昭其敬，而織皮則物之足以爲裘罽者也。是物也，奉以入貢者，則有河源之崑崙、河西之析支、朔方之渠搜焉。爲國雖異，而所獻則未甞異。
translation_en:
…there were those who assisted them. This is what is meant by “preceding Heaven” in the discussion of the great man at the nine in the fifth place of Qian; the making of the Changes is not included here. Ah! How profound is the relationship between Heaven and humanity!

Book of Documents
“Woven skins; Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou—the Western Rong came into due order.”
By Mu Congsheng.

Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The exposition of the idea of not governing the Yi and Di captures the purport of the ‘Tribute of Yu.’ Accept it.”
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning are clear and complete, surpassing the other compositions.”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous, without superficiality: this must be someone who has devoted himself to the study of the Classics.”

The historiographer records that the tribute goods of the three countries were the same, thereby revealing that distant peoples had submitted to orderly rule. Now, the hearts of distant peoples are not easily moved. Yet when tribute assessed upon the land extended to the Western Rong, could the achievement of bringing them into orderly submission fail to be seen? The historiographer touches upon this when recording Great Yu’s accomplishments in Yongzhou. His meaning is that when a sage’s achievements are great, his transforming influence reaches far. Once the waters and lands of Yongzhou had been put in order, could the tribute rendered according to the resources of the land have consisted only of the fine jades and langgan stones within its borders? Those presenting offerings to their superior cannot manifest their reverence without material objects, and woven skins are materials suitable for making fur garments and woollen cloth. Those who respectfully brought these goods as tribute included Kunlun at the source of the Yellow River, Xizhi west of the Yellow River, and Qusou in the northern region. Though they were different countries, what they presented was invariably the same…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其視冀之皮服同一任土之宜乎爲名雖殊而
所執則未始殊其視青之檿絲同一方物之輸
乎雖曰中國之常有也然王者不貴異物取其
誠不取其物也雖曰裘服之常事也然王者不
賤用物取其常不取其異也夫是三國者雖附
於雍而非分土於雍是西方之戎近於雍者也
向也洪水橫流鳥獸迫人何有於物今則睹懷
襄之旣息而志切於慕義卽其假物以輸誠可
以驗迪德之大同奉正朔而尊王化者自奔走
===
之恐後向也原隰沮洳道路未通何有于貢今
則幸天地之平成而人樂于嚮風卽其通道以
底貢可以知文命之旣敷親中國而爲外臣者
咸效順之爭先夷狄固治之以不治而其翕然
來歸者亦順受之而已此其就功之驗蓋方與
三苗同一丕敘矣戎狄固待之以無心而其不
忍自絕者亦與其進而已此其順治之機蓋將
與中國同一惟敘矣吁禹績之遠不亦可見哉
抑史臣於西戎島夷萊夷淮夷之貢賦必繫之
punctuated: 其視冀之皮服，同一任土之宜乎？爲名雖殊，而所執則未始殊，其視青之檿絲，同一方物之輸乎？雖曰中國之常有也，然王者不貴異物，取其誠，不取其物也；雖曰裘服之常事也，然王者不賤用物，取其常，不取其異也。夫是三國者，雖附於雍，而非分土於雍，是西方之戎近於雍者也。向也洪水橫流，鳥獸迫人，何有於物？今則睹懷襄之旣息，而志切於慕義，卽其假物以輸誠，可以驗迪德之大同；奉正朔而尊王化者，自奔走之恐後。向也原隰沮洳，道路未通，何有于貢？今則幸天地之平成，而人樂于嚮風，卽其通道以底貢，可以知文命之旣敷；親中國而爲外臣者，咸效順之爭先。夷狄固治之以不治，而其翕然來歸者，亦順受之而已。此其就功之驗，蓋方與三苗同一丕敘矣。戎狄固待之以無心，而其不忍自絕者，亦與其進而已。此其順治之機，蓋將與中國同一惟敘矣。吁！禹績之遠，不亦可見哉？抑史臣於西戎、島夷、萊夷、淮夷之貢賦，必繫之
translation_en:
…Compared with the hides and garments of Ji, are these not equally appropriate products of their lands? Although their names differ, the offerings they present are essentially alike. Compared with the wild-silkworm silk of Qing, are these not equally contributions of local products? Though these are things commonly found in the central lands, the true king does not prize exotic objects: he values their sincerity, not their goods. Though these are ordinary articles used for fur garments, the true king does not disdain useful objects: he values their regular provision, not their rarity.

These three countries, though attached to Yong, were not territories apportioned within Yong; they were the western Rong peoples living near it. Formerly, when floodwaters surged unchecked and birds and beasts pressed upon people, how could there have been goods to offer? Now, seeing that the overwhelming floods had subsided, they earnestly aspired to righteousness. Their use of goods to convey sincerity demonstrates their shared acceptance of moral guidance. Those who honored the royal calendar and revered the king’s transforming influence hurried forward, fearing to fall behind. Formerly, when uplands and lowlands were waterlogged and roads impassable, how could there have been tribute? Now they rejoiced that heaven and earth had been brought to order, and people gladly turned toward his influence. Their opening of routes to deliver tribute shows that his civilizing teaching had spread abroad. Those who drew close to the central lands and became outer subjects all competed to be foremost in demonstrating obedience.

The Yi and Di are indeed governed by leaving them ungoverned; when they come together in allegiance, one simply accepts them as they come. This evidence of completed achievement shows that they were now being brought into the same great order as the Sanmiao. The Rong and Di are indeed treated without calculated designs; when they cannot bear to sever themselves from us, one simply approves their advance. This opening for their willing submission to good government means that they would share the same orderly condition as the central lands. Ah! Is not the far-reaching extent of Yu’s achievements evident here?

Yet whenever the historian records the tribute of the western Rong, the island Yi, the Lai Yi, and the Huai Yi, he invariably appends…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
戎夷以別之島夷萊夷淮夷皆在冀州青徐之
間而西戎亦近於雍別之如此其嚴也得聖人
內夏外夷之旨矣以此為訓猶有以諸夏而致
金繒之奉以戎狄而位侯王之上如漢世者
惟曰欲至于萬年
施從政
同考試官教諭盧批發出周臣祈君永命之意忠愛
藹然佳士也
考試官教諭毛批詞語不贅而題意明備
===
考試官學正王批純暢典切
周臣祈君以永年之至忠愛之意見矣夫國之
永命存乎德也周臣以萬年為期其深於愛君
者與昔周臣進戒于君而復期之永命也意蓋
曰人君之御世也固有不容已之治而人臣之
事君也亦有不容已之情臣之所以納忠於王
而欲王監之者豈無意哉亦惟遠有所期耳蓋
以諸侯國之屏也王之明德以懷遠則屏樹矣
民國之本也王之用德以和民則本固矣將見
punctuated:
戎夷以別之。島夷、萊夷、淮夷皆在冀州、青徐之間，而西戎亦近於雍，別之如此其嚴也，得聖人內夏外夷之旨矣。以此為訓，猶有以諸夏而致金繒之奉，以戎狄而位侯王之上，如漢世者。
惟曰欲至于萬年
施從政
同考試官教諭盧批：發出周臣祈君永命之意，忠愛藹然，佳士也。
考試官教諭毛批：詞語不贅，而題意明備。
考試官學正王批：純暢典切。
周臣祈君以永年之至，忠愛之意見矣。夫國之永命存乎德也，周臣以萬年為期，其深於愛君者與！昔周臣進戒于君，而復期之永命也，意蓋曰：人君之御世也，固有不容已之治，而人臣之事君也，亦有不容已之情。臣之所以納忠於王而欲王監之者，豈無意哉？亦惟遠有所期耳。蓋以諸侯，國之屏也，王之明德以懷遠，則屏樹矣；民，國之本也，王之用德以和民，則本固矣。將見
translation_en:
…the designations Rong and Yi, to distinguish them. The Island Yi, Lai Yi, and Huai Yi all lived in the region of Jizhou, Qingzhou, and Xuzhou, while the Western Rong were also near Yongzhou. So strict was this distinction: it grasped the sage’s intent to treat the Xia as belonging within and the Yi as belonging outside. Even with this as an instruction, there were still cases, as under the Han, in which the various Xia peoples rendered tribute of gold and silk, while the Rong and Di were ranked above marquises and kings.
“I Desire Only That It May Extend to Ten Thousand Years”
Shi Congzheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: “He brings out the Zhou minister’s wish that his ruler’s mandate endure forever. Loyalty and affection abound: a fine scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: “The wording is free of excess, and the meaning of the topic is clearly and fully expressed.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Pure and fluent, classical and apt.”
The Zhou minister wishes his ruler the utmost longevity, revealing his loyalty and affection. Now, the enduring mandate of a state rests upon virtue. When the Zhou minister sets his hopes on ten thousand years, how profound is his affection for his ruler! In ancient times, the Zhou minister offered admonitions to his ruler and also expressed the hope that his mandate would endure forever. His meaning was probably this: in governing the world, a ruler certainly has duties of government that he cannot relinquish; and in serving his ruler, a minister likewise has feelings that he cannot suppress. Could there be no purpose in my offering loyal counsel to the king and wishing him to heed it? It is simply that I have hopes extending into the distant future. The feudal lords are the state’s bulwark: if the king manifests his virtue to win over those far away, that bulwark will be established. The people are the state’s foundation: if the king employs virtue to bring harmony to the people, that foundation will be secure. We shall then see…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其未射也預爲之賓以行禮必肄之筵以禮賓
此固君子之所不廢也而君子豈徒飲哉吾見
賓之登筵者左焉秩秩也右焉秩秩也獻酬雖
未行而位列已不紊矣物之優賓者有籩豆殽
核也有旨酒思柔也勸侑雖未舉而品物已曲
全矣於是凡百君子酌彼康爵將之以德成禮
而不繼以淫也行之以敬合歡而不及於亂也
其端莊齊一之度蓋無爽於即席之初矣是則
未射而飲者不猶見其禮儀之盛乎及其將射
===
也遷鐘鼓於堂下避射位於厥明此固射儀之
所由行也而君子豈徒然哉吾見舉其酬爵焉
則賓主以交少長以徧禮尚往來整暇而有序
矣供其射具焉則大侯既抗弓矢亦張既備乃
事從容而有節矣於是因左右之既比而拾發
以獻功眾耦期於巧力庶幾可以言中也各心
競於純竒庶幾飲汝以爵也其雍容揖遜之節
蓋藹然於序賓之時矣是則既飲而射者不猶
見其禮儀之盛乎夫有酒以行射而有禮以飲
punctuated: 其未射也，預爲之賓以行禮，必肄之筵以禮賓。此固君子之所不廢也，而君子豈徒飲哉？吾見賓之登筵者，左焉秩秩也，右焉秩秩也；獻酬雖未行，而位列已不紊矣。物之優賓者，有籩豆殽核也，有旨酒思柔也；勸侑雖未舉，而品物已曲全矣。於是凡百君子，酌彼康爵，將之以德，成禮而不繼以淫也；行之以敬，合歡而不及於亂也。其端莊齊一之度，蓋無爽於即席之初矣。是則未射而飲者，不猶見其禮儀之盛乎？及其將射也，遷鐘鼓於堂下，避射位於厥明。此固射儀之所由行也，而君子豈徒然哉？吾見舉其酬爵焉，則賓主以交，少長以徧，禮尚往來，整暇而有序矣。供其射具焉，則大侯既抗，弓矢亦張，既備乃事，從容而有節矣。於是因左右之既比，而拾發以獻功，眾耦期於巧力，庶幾可以言中也；各心競於純竒，庶幾飲汝以爵也。其雍容揖遜之節，蓋藹然於序賓之時矣。是則既飲而射者，不猶見其禮儀之盛乎？夫有酒以行射，而有禮以飲
translation_en:
…Before the archery begins, guests are designated in advance for the performance of the rites, and mats must be laid out [?] to receive them with due ceremony. These are things that gentlemen certainly do not neglect. Yet do gentlemen merely drink? I see the guests taking their places upon the mats, those on the left in orderly ranks and those on the right likewise. Although the offering and reciprocation of wine have not yet begun, their assigned places are already free of confusion. Among the provisions that generously honor the guests are bamboo baskets and wooden stands bearing meat dishes and fruits, and fine, mellow wine. Although the urging of guests to partake has not yet begun, the provisions are already complete in every detail. Then all the gentlemen pour wine into those ample cups and conduct themselves with virtue, completing the rites without proceeding to excess. They act with reverence, joining in merriment without descending into disorder. Their dignified and consistently composed bearing remains just as it was when they first took their seats. Does this drinking before the archery not also reveal the fullness of their ritual propriety?

When they are about to shoot, the bells and drums are moved below the hall, clearing the shooting positions on the following morning. This is certainly how the archery ceremony proceeds. Yet do gentlemen merely go through these motions? I see them raise the cups of reciprocal toasting: hosts and guests exchange courtesies, and younger and older alike are included. Ritual values reciprocity; they are composed, unhurried, and orderly. When their archery equipment is supplied, the great target has been raised, and bows and arrows are also made ready. Only once preparations are complete do they begin, proceeding calmly and with due measure. Then, once those on the left and right have been paired, they shoot in alternation to display their accomplishments. All the pairs aspire to skill and strength, hoping to score hits; each sets his heart on competing over the even and odd tallies [?], hoping to make his opponent drink from the cup. Their gracious observance of bowing and yielding is abundantly evident as the guests are placed in order. Does this archery after drinking not also reveal the fullness of their ritual propriety? Thus there is wine for conducting the archery, and ritual propriety for drinking…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天子萬年君臣之間相期於脩德誠民以爲永
年永世之本者不一而足其享國之長久也有
以也哉
詩
賓之初筵左右秩秩籩豆有楚殽核維旅
酒旣和旨飲酒孔偕鐘鼓旣設舉鼏逸
逸大侯旣抗弓矢斯張射夫旣同獻爾
發功發彼有的以祈爾爵
趙友仁
===
同考試官敎諭蒲 批 〔此題不難於敷演而難於整潔是作芟去蔓冗發揮本旨殆盡錄之以式多士〕
考試官敎諭毛 批 〔詞不煩而理自足善說雅義者〕
考試官學正王 批 〔簡淨醇雅無一長語邃養之士也〕
詩人詳射者之善其飲所以寓自省之意也夫
一於禮而不苟此射飲之所以善也由是則亦
何有於過舉也哉衛武公作此詩意謂酒所以
洽禮亦所以長過洽禮者其始也長過者其流
也蓋嘗觀於射而知君子之靡不有初者矣方
punctuated:
天子萬年，君臣之間相期於脩德誠民，以爲永年永世之本者，不一而足。其享國之長久也，有以也哉！

詩
賓之初筵，左右秩秩。籩豆有楚，殽核維旅。酒旣和旨，飲酒孔偕。鐘鼓旣設，舉鼏逸逸。大侯旣抗，弓矢斯張。射夫旣同，獻爾發功。發彼有的，以祈爾爵。
趙友仁

同考試官敎諭蒲批〔此題不難於敷演，而難於整潔。是作芟去蔓冗，發揮本旨殆盡，錄之以式多士。〕
考試官敎諭毛批〔詞不煩而理自足，善說雅義者。〕
考試官學正王批〔簡淨醇雅，無一長語，邃養之士也。〕

詩人詳射者之善其飲，所以寓自省之意也。夫一於禮而不苟，此射飲之所以善也。由是則亦何有於過舉也哉？衛武公作此詩，意謂酒所以洽禮，亦所以長過。洽禮者其始也，長過者其流也。蓋嘗觀於射而知君子之靡不有初者矣。方
translation_en:
…May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years! Sovereign and ministers look to one another to cultivate virtue and make the people sincere, thereby establishing the foundation for enduring life and an enduring dynasty; their efforts cannot be exhausted in a single enumeration. Surely there is a reason why his rule endures so long!

Book of Odes
“When the guests first take their places at the feast,
Those on the left and right are orderly.
The bamboo baskets and wooden dishes stand in neat array;
Meats and fruits are set out.
The wine is well blended and delicious;
The drinkers are most harmonious.
The bells and drums have been set in place;
They raise the vessel lids [?] with ease and grace.
The great archery target has been raised;
Bows and arrows are made ready.
The archers have assembled:
Display your skill in shooting!
Shoot at that target’s center,
To seek your cup of wine.”
Zhao Youren

Comment by Associate Examiner Pu, Instructor: 〔The difficulty of this topic lies not in elaborating it but in treating it with order and concision. This composition cuts away sprawling and superfluous material and brings out almost the whole of the original meaning. It is recorded here as a model for the candidates.〕
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: 〔The language is economical, yet the reasoning is complete: this writer explains well the meaning of the Elegantiae.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Concise, clean, refined, and elegant, without a single superfluous expression. This is a man of profound cultivation.〕

The poet describes in detail how the archers conduct their drinking properly, thereby conveying an intention of self-examination. Complete adherence to ritual, without carelessness: this is what makes the drinking at the archery ceremony proper. Proceeding in this way, how could there be any misconduct? Duke Wu of Wei composed this poem with the idea that wine serves to bring ritual observance to fulfillment, but also serves to foster faults. Bringing ritual observance to fulfillment is its beginning; fostering faults is its subsequent course. Indeed, by observing the archery ceremony, one recognizes that gentlemen all make a good beginning. Just when…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其未射也預爲之賓以行禮必肄之筵以禮賓
此固君子之所不廢也而君子豈徒飲哉吾見
賓之登筵者左焉秩秩也右焉秩秩也獻酬雖
未行而位列已不紊矣物之優賓者有籩豆殽
核也有旨酒思柔也勸侑雖未舉而品物已曲
全矣於是凡百君子酌彼康爵將之以德成禮
而不繼以淫也行之以敬合歡而不及於亂也
其端莊齊一之度蓋無爽於即席之初矣是則
未射而飲者不猶見其禮儀之盛乎及其將射
===
也遷鐘鼓於堂下避射位於厥明此固射儀之
所由行也而君子豈徒然哉吾見舉其酬爵焉
則賓主以交少長以徧禮尚往來整暇而有序
矣供其射具焉則大侯既抗弓矢亦張既備乃
事從容而有節矣於是因左右之既比而拾發
以獻功眾耦期於巧力庶幾可以言中也各心
競於純奇庶幾飲汝以爵也其雍容揖遜之節
蓋藹然於序賓之時矣是則既飲而射者不猶
見其禮儀之盛乎夫有酒以行射而有禮以飲
punctuated: 其未射也，預爲之賓以行禮，必肄之筵以禮賓，此固君子之所不廢也。而君子豈徒飲哉？吾見賓之登筵者，左焉秩秩也，右焉秩秩也，獻酬雖未行，而位列已不紊矣。物之優賓者，有籩豆殽核也，有旨酒思柔也，勸侑雖未舉，而品物已曲全矣。於是凡百君子，酌彼康爵，將之以德，成禮而不繼以淫也；行之以敬，合歡而不及於亂也。其端莊齊一之度，蓋無爽於即席之初矣。是則未射而飲者，不猶見其禮儀之盛乎？及其將射也，遷鐘鼓於堂下，避射位於厥明，此固射儀之所由行也。而君子豈徒然哉？吾見舉其酬爵焉，則賓主以交，少長以徧，禮尚往來，整暇而有序矣。供其射具焉，則大侯既抗，弓矢亦張，既備乃事，從容而有節矣。於是因左右之既比，而拾發以獻功，眾耦期於巧力，庶幾可以言中也；各心競於純奇，庶幾飲汝以爵也。其雍容揖遜之節，蓋藹然於序賓之時矣。是則既飲而射者，不猶見其禮儀之盛乎？夫有酒以行射，而有禮以飲
translation_en:
…before the archery begins, guests are designated in advance for the performance of the rites, and mats must be spread to receive them with due ceremony. These are certainly things that gentlemen do not neglect. Yet do gentlemen merely drink? I see the guests taking their places on the mats, orderly on the left and orderly on the right. Though the offering and reciprocation of cups have not yet begun, the seating is already free from confusion. Among the provisions generously supplied to the guests are bamboo baskets and wooden stands bearing meats and fruits, and fine, mellow wine. Though the urging of guests to partake has not yet begun, the provisions are already complete in every detail. Then all the gentlemen pour wine into those great cups and conduct themselves with virtue, completing the rites without proceeding to excess. They act with reverence, joining in convivial pleasure without descending into disorder. Their dignified, composed bearing remains just as it was when they first took their seats. Does this drinking before the archery not likewise reveal the fullness of their ritual propriety?

When the archery is about to begin, bells and drums are moved below the hall, clearing the shooting positions the following morning. These are indeed the arrangements through which the archery ceremony is performed. Yet do gentlemen merely go through these motions? I see them raise their cups in reciprocal toasts: host and guests engage with one another, and the cups pass among young and old alike. Ritual values reciprocity, and they are composed, unhurried, and orderly. When the archery equipment is supplied, the great target has been raised, and bows and arrows are also made ready. Only when everything is prepared do they proceed, unhurried and measured in their movements. Thus, once the archers on the left and right have been paired, they shoot in turn to display their skill. Each pair aspires to skill and strength, hoping to score hits. Each contestant sets his mind on competing over paired and odd tallies [?], hoping to make his opponent drink from the cup. Their gracious bows and courteous yielding are fully evident as the guests are arranged in order. Does this archery after drinking not likewise reveal the fullness of their ritual propriety? For there is wine with which to conduct the archery ceremony, and ritual with which to govern drinking…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
酒此固善飲者之始於治者也使由此而克終
焉夫何酒過之有也哉抑武王封康叔作酒誥
則如禹之絶旨酒可也顧又曰飲惟祀曰無彝
飲武公作賓筵以悔過亦宜痛絶之也而又曰
飲酒孔偕曰舉醻逸逸是何也蓋先王不以酒
過廢大禮故司徒之陽禮則教之以飲酒鄉大
夫之賓興則賓之以飲酒凡以禮也然曰賓主
百拜而酒三行曰終日飲酒而不得醉焉則所
以備酒過者固自有道矣
===
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
曾倬
同考試官教諭蒲批聖人脩德本于敬發明親切此
篇得之
考試官教諭毛批渾厚有味
考試官學正王批詞義明順
商人頌聖人敬德之懋惟以昭事乎天焉夫敬
聖人所以神明其德者也成湯之昭事一於此
則其會天之命爲有道矣昔商人祖契而宗湯
punctuated:
酒，此固善飲者之始於治者也。使由此而克終焉，夫何酒過之有也哉？抑武王封康叔，作《酒誥》，則如禹之絶旨酒可也。顧又曰「飲惟祀」，曰「無彝飲」。武公作《賓筵》以悔過，亦宜痛絶之也，而又曰「飲酒孔偕」，曰「舉醻逸逸」，是何也？蓋先王不以酒過廢大禮，故司徒之陽禮則教之以飲酒，鄉大夫之賓興則賓之以飲酒，凡以禮也。然曰「賓主百拜而酒三行」，曰「終日飲酒而不得醉焉」，則所以備酒過者固自有道矣。

聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。
曾倬
同考試官教諭蒲批：聖人脩德本于敬，發明親切，此篇得之。
考試官教諭毛批：渾厚有味。
考試官學正王批：詞義明順。

商人頌聖人敬德之懋，惟以昭事乎天焉。夫敬，聖人所以神明其德者也。成湯之昭事一於此，則其會天之命爲有道矣。昔商人祖契而宗湯，
translation_en:
…wine: this is indeed how those skilled in drinking begin in good order. If they can follow this through to the end, what excesses of drinking could there be? Yet when King Wu enfeoffed Kang Shu and composed the Announcement on Wine (Jiu gao), it would have been fitting to follow Yu in renouncing fine wine. Why, then, did he also say, “Drink only at sacrifices,” and “Do not drink habitually”? When Duke Wu composed Guests at the Feast (Bin yan) to repent his faults, he too ought to have renounced drinking utterly. Yet he also said, “Drinking wine in perfect harmony,” and “Offering toasts with unhurried ease.” Why was this? The former kings did not abolish great rites because of the excesses of drinking. Thus, in the Minister of Education’s rites of the yang sphere, people were instructed through wine drinking; and when the District Grand Master entertained and recommended worthy men, he honored them as guests with wine. All this was governed by ritual propriety. Yet it is said, “The host and guests bow a hundred times, while the wine makes only three rounds,” and “They drink wine all day but may not become drunk.” There was thus assuredly a proper way to guard against the excesses of drinking.

“His sagely reverence rose daily; his luminous influence reached far and endured; he revered the Lord on High.”
Zeng Zhuo
Associate Examiner Pu, Instructor, comments: “The sage’s cultivation of virtue is rooted in reverence. This essay captures that point, expounding it with precision and immediacy.”
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Substantial and rich in savor.”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The wording and meaning are clear and coherent.”

The people of Shang praised the sage’s assiduous reverence for virtue, through which alone he luminously served Heaven. Reverence is what enables a sage to make his virtue spiritually perceptive. Since Cheng Tang’s luminous service rested wholly upon this, he had a proper way to accord with Heaven’s mandate. In former times, the people of Shang honored Xie as their founding ancestor and Tang as their dynastic ancestor…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此其祫祭之詩也若曰天之篤生聖人也固豫
乎寵綏之命而聖祖之懋敬厥德也適昭乎基
命之符今夫脩敬之功有所强勉可以言敬而
未可以言聖敬也居德之力猶有間斷可以言
敬而未可以言日躋也以此而事天吾未見其
能永孚矣惟我烈祖也一德妙于性生而嚴威
以作所者每存存而不忘至道凝于天錫而恂
慄以中存者恒亹亹而不已德旣聖矣而心不
自聖檢身不及之誠日新又新不有與日而俱
===
升者乎敬已純矣而志不自滿昧爽丕顯之德
惟日不足不有與日而俱積者乎存之自下而
昭之自上夙興夜寐莫非昊天之欽若焉蓋以
此而懋脩則以此而對越矣積之自躬而假之
自天亦臨亦保一惟上帝之祗順焉蓋以此而
洗心則以此而靈承矣天運無窮而聖人之心
亦無窮合冲漠以流通誠有先之而不違後之
而奉時者自事天之外豈復有餘事哉帝命不
息而聖人之敬亦不息泯聲臭于淵微誠有動
punctuated: 此其祫祭之詩也。若曰：天之篤生聖人也，固豫乎寵綏之命；而聖祖之懋敬厥德也，適昭乎基命之符。今夫脩敬之功有所强勉，可以言敬，而未可以言聖敬也；居德之力猶有間斷，可以言敬，而未可以言日躋也。以此而事天，吾未見其能永孚矣。惟我烈祖也，一德妙于性生，而嚴威以作所者，每存存而不忘；至道凝于天錫，而恂慄以中存者，恒亹亹而不已。德旣聖矣，而心不自聖，檢身不及之誠，日新又新，不有與日而俱升者乎？敬已純矣，而志不自滿，昧爽丕顯之德，惟日不足，不有與日而俱積者乎？存之自下，而昭之自上，夙興夜寐，莫非昊天之欽若焉。蓋以此而懋脩，則以此而對越矣。積之自躬，而假之自天，亦臨亦保，一惟上帝之祗順焉。蓋以此而洗心，則以此而靈承矣。天運無窮，而聖人之心亦無窮，合冲漠以流通，誠有先之而不違、後之而奉時者，自事天之外，豈復有餘事哉？帝命不息，而聖人之敬亦不息，泯聲臭于淵微，誠有動
translation_en:
…This is the poem for their joint ancestral sacrifice. It is as though it says: When Heaven brought forth the sage with its abundant favor, it had already provided a mandate to favor and secure him; the sagely ancestor’s diligent reverence in cultivating his virtue duly manifested the sign that established his mandate. Now, if the work of cultivating reverence involves forced effort, it may be called reverence, but cannot yet be called sagely reverence. If the effort to abide in virtue still suffers interruptions, it may be called reverence, but cannot yet be said to rise daily. In serving Heaven in this way, I do not see how one could remain forever in accord with it.

Only our illustrious ancestor possessed a single, undivided virtue, wondrously inherent in his nature from birth. With solemn dignity he established a dwelling place for it [?], constantly preserving it without forgetting. The ultimate Way was concentrated in Heaven’s endowment, and he maintained it within through awe and trembling, always striving without cease. His virtue was already sagely, yet in his heart he did not deem himself a sage. Sincerely examining himself as though he still fell short, he renewed himself daily, again and again. Was there not something that rose with each passing day? His reverence was already pure, yet his aspirations were never complacent. His virtue shone forth even before dawn, and he felt that each day afforded insufficient time. Was there not something that accumulated with each passing day?

He preserved it here below, and it was made manifest from above. Rising early and retiring late, everything he did reverently accorded with August Heaven. Thus, that by which he diligently cultivated himself was also that by which he stood reverently before Heaven. He accumulated it in his own person, and Heaven’s influence reached him. Whether watching over him or protecting him, the Lord on High alone was the object of his reverent obedience. Thus, that by which he cleansed his heart was also that by which he received Heaven’s numinous influence.

Heaven’s revolutions are inexhaustible, and the sage’s heart is likewise inexhaustible. United with the still and formless, it flows freely. Truly, he could precede Heaven without departing from it, or follow Heaven and accord with its seasons. Beyond serving Heaven, could there be any further undertaking? The Lord’s mandate never ceases, and the sage’s reverence likewise never ceases. Sound and scent vanish in its profound subtlety; truly, in movement…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
焉而與俱靜焉而與游者自敬帝之外豈復有
餘心哉是知敬德之純事天之至也此成湯之
所以會成王業而終玄王相土之烈者也商人
特祫致頌以宗之可謂知所本矣抑書稱成湯
之德曰不邇不殖曰制事制心曰改過檢身善
至備矣至于廟頌則惟一敬是稱焉何哉夫敬
德之聚也所以祈天永命之本也堯之欽舜之
恭禹之祗皆是物也蘊之爲天德之純發之爲
王道之大聖聖授受惟此一道而已敬肆幾希
===
之間相越不啻千里故曰敬者聖學所以成始
成終也
春秋
秋郳黎來來朝〔莊公五年〕
楊道東
考試官敎諭毛批〔書名書朝二意發揮殆盡〕
考試官學正王批〔措詞切實正合作經之法〕
遠人脩禮于內春秋旣外之而復進之也此黎
來稱名而特書曰朝春秋馭夷勸善之意備矣
punctuated:
焉而與俱，靜焉而與游者，自敬帝之外，豈復有餘心哉？是知敬德之純，事天之至也。此成湯之所以會成王業，而終玄王、相土之烈者也。商人特祫致頌以宗之，可謂知所本矣。抑《書》稱成湯之德，曰不邇不殖，曰制事制心，曰改過檢身，善至備矣。至于廟頌，則惟一敬是稱焉，何哉？夫敬，德之聚也，所以祈天永命之本也。堯之欽，舜之恭，禹之祗，皆是物也。蘊之爲天德之純，發之爲王道之大。聖聖授受，惟此一道而已。敬肆幾希之間，相越不啻千里。故曰：敬者，聖學所以成始成終也。
春秋
秋，郳黎來來朝。〔莊公五年〕
楊道東
考試官敎諭毛批〔書名書朝，二意發揮殆盡。〕
考試官學正王批〔措詞切實，正合作經之法。〕
遠人脩禮于內，《春秋》旣外之而復進之也。此黎來稱名，而特書曰朝，《春秋》馭夷勸善之意備矣。
translation_en:
…in movement, accompanying it, and in stillness, communing with it. Beyond revering the Lord on High, could there be any other concern in his heart? Thus we know that purity in reverent virtue is the utmost in serving Heaven. This is how Cheng Tang brought the royal enterprise to completion and fulfilled the achievements of Xuan Wang and Xiang Tu. The people of Shang presented hymns to honor him as their ancestor at the individual and combined ancestral sacrifices [?]; they may indeed be said to have understood their origins.
Moreover, the Book of Documents praises Cheng Tang’s virtue, saying that he did not approach sensual pleasures or accumulate wealth, that he regulated affairs and his own mind, and that he corrected his faults and examined his conduct. These virtues were supremely complete. Yet the ancestral-temple hymn praises reverence alone. Why? Reverence is where the virtues converge; it is the foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. Yao’s reverence, Shun’s respect, and Yu’s deference were all this same thing. Held within, it constitutes the purity of heavenly virtue; expressed outwardly, it constitutes the greatness of the kingly Way. What sage after sage transmitted and received was this one Way alone. Though the divide between reverence and heedlessness is minute, their outcomes differ by more than a thousand miles. Thus it is said: reverence is what enables the learning of the sages to fulfill both its beginning and its end.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In autumn, Li Lai of Ni came to pay court.” 〔Fifth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Yang Daodong
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: 〔The two implications—recording his personal name and recording his court visit—are developed almost exhaustively.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Schoolmaster: 〔The wording is precise and sound, fully conforming to the proper method of composing an essay on a Classic.〕
When a man from afar observed the rites within the central states, the Spring and Autumn Annals, having treated him as an outsider, nevertheless accorded him advancement. Here Li Lai is designated by his personal name, yet the text specifically records that he ‘paid court.’ In this, the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals to govern the non-Chinese peoples and encourage goodness is fully expressed.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
莊公五年郳君黎來親造我魯之邦用脩覲見
之禮夫國君不名例也郳國也曷書其名以其
爲夷狄之附庸也蓋内夏外夷天地之常經夷
狄之賤不可混于華也明矣故先王列諸男甸
采衛之外而太司馬有九畿之正職方氏有四
夷之辯凡以嚴爲之限而不使亂之也郳之來
雖可進也然果盟蔑之儀父乎朝榖之蕭叔乎
正朔不加聲敎不及斯固王道之所必外者也
其與中國冠帶之君則甚異矣苟不辯之何以
===
正夫華夷之分哉故特以名稱外之也所以防
其紊也而窺内之釁庶乎其不萌矣若夷狄書
來亦例也郳夷也曷書來朝以其能脩乎朝禮
也蓋殷聘世朝諸侯之常禮夷狄之陋無望其
脩此也久矣故先王制爲以時入賓之儀而象
胥掌傳言之令懷方氏掌送逆之節凡以引之
使進而不欲泯之也郳之國雖可外也然果來
襄之白狄乎來僖之介葛盧乎禮文是尚誠敬
是將斯固君子之所樂取者也厥後天王錫爵
punctuated: 莊公五年，郳君黎來親造我魯之邦，用脩覲見之禮。夫國君不名，例也。郳，國也，曷書其名？以其爲夷狄之附庸也。蓋内夏外夷，天地之常經；夷狄之賤，不可混于華也，明矣。故先王列諸男甸采衛之外，而太司馬有九畿之正，職方氏有四夷之辯，凡以嚴爲之限而不使亂之也。郳之來，雖可進也，然果盟蔑之儀父乎？朝榖之蕭叔乎？正朔不加，聲敎不及，斯固王道之所必外者也。其與中國冠帶之君則甚異矣。苟不辯之，何以正夫華夷之分哉？故特以名稱，外之也，所以防其紊也。而窺内之釁，庶乎其不萌矣。若夷狄書來，亦例也。郳，夷也，曷書來朝？以其能脩乎朝禮也。蓋殷聘世朝，諸侯之常禮；夷狄之陋，無望其脩此也久矣。故先王制爲以時入賓之儀，而象胥掌傳言之令，懷方氏掌送逆之節，凡以引之使進而不欲泯之也。郳之國，雖可外也，然果來襄之白狄乎？來僖之介葛盧乎？禮文是尚，誠敬是將，斯固君子之所樂取者也。厥後天王錫爵
translation_en:
In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang, Li Lai, ruler of Ni, personally came to our state of Lu to perform the rites of an audience. It is a convention that rulers of states are not recorded by their personal names. Ni was a state: why, then, was its ruler’s personal name recorded? Because it was a subordinate domain of the Yi and Di. To treat the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders is the constant order of Heaven and Earth. Clearly, the lowly Yi and Di must not be confounded with the Hua. Thus the former kings placed them beyond the nan, dian, cai, and wei zones. The Grand Marshal had regulations for the nine territorial zones, and the Director of Territorial Administration distinguished the peoples of the four quarters. All this established strict boundaries for them, preventing them from disrupting the order. Although Ni’s coming could merit advancement, was its ruler really like Yifu, who covenanted at Mie, or Xiao Shu, who attended an audience at Gu? The royal calendar did not extend to him, nor did the transforming influence of royal instruction reach him. He was therefore necessarily excluded under the kingly Way. He differed greatly from the capped and girdled rulers of the central states. Without distinguishing them, how could the division between Hua and Yi be properly maintained? Thus the text deliberately calls him by his personal name, treating him as an outsider to prevent his confounding the order. In this way, it was hoped that designs upon the inner states would never arise.

As for recording the Yi and Di simply as having “come,” this too is a convention. Ni belonged to the Yi: why, then, record that its ruler “came to court”? Because he was able to observe the rites of a court audience. Full diplomatic visits and a personal court audience in each generation were regular rites for the feudal lords. Given the uncultivated ways of the Yi and Di, there had long been no expectation that they would observe these rites. Thus the former kings established ceremonies for their coming as guests at appointed times. The Interpreters were responsible for transmitting speech, and the Officers for Cherishing Distant Regions for the protocols of welcoming and seeing them off. All this was intended to guide them toward advancement, without wishing to efface them. Although the state of Ni could be treated as an outsider, was its ruler really like the Baidi who came during Duke Xiang’s reign, or Jie Gelu who came during Duke Xi’s? He esteemed ritual forms and presented himself with sincerity and reverence: these were certainly qualities that the gentleman delighted in acknowledging. Later, the Heavenly King’s bestowal of a noble title…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之榮基于此矣苟不與之不有以阻其自新之
志哉故特書曰朝進之也所以昭其順也而慕
義之夷庶乎其知效矣是則類所當外春秋不
以善而廢其防者立法之嚴也善所可進春秋
不因類而廢其行者宅心之恕也嚴以示萬世
之經恕以寓一時之勸聖訓其精矣乎雖然夷
屬例書名矣州寔乃中國諸侯也何以亦書其
名脩禮特書朝矣祭伯亦能脩禮者也何以止
書曰來蓋春秋化工也中國不名而名州寔者
===
所以著諸侯自取之戒來朝必錄而略祭伯者
所以正人臣私交之失或名或不名或與或不
與眞如造物賦形之妙而可以一例拘哉先儒
謂春秋非聖人莫能脩信矣
夏季孫行父如齊〔宣公元年〕夏公會齊
侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
楊京
考試官敎諭毛批理明詞正深切題意
考試官學正王批詞有根據可錄
punctuated:
之榮，基于此矣。苟不與之，不有以阻其自新之志哉？故特書曰「朝」，進之也，所以昭其順也，而慕義之夷庶乎其知效矣。是則類所當外，《春秋》不以善而廢其防者，立法之嚴也；善所可進，《春秋》不因類而廢其行者，宅心之恕也。嚴以示萬世之經，恕以寓一時之勸，聖訓其精矣乎！雖然，夷屬例書名矣，州寔乃中國諸侯也，何以亦書其名？脩禮特書「朝」矣，祭伯亦能脩禮者也，何以止書曰「來」？蓋《春秋》化工也，中國不名而名州寔者，所以著諸侯自取之戒；來朝必錄而略祭伯者，所以正人臣私交之失。或名或不名，或與或不與，眞如造物賦形之妙，而可以一例拘哉？先儒謂《春秋》非聖人莫能脩，信矣。
夏，季孫行父如齊。〔宣公元年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕
楊京
考試官敎諭毛批：理明詞正，深切題意。
考試官學正王批：詞有根據，可錄。
translation_en:
…the honor of receiving a rank from the Heavenly King had its foundation in this. If approval were withheld, would that not obstruct his resolve to reform himself? Thus the text specifically writes “paid court”: this advances him in standing and makes manifest his submission, so that the Yi who admire righteousness may learn to emulate him. Thus, where their category calls for exclusion, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not abandon its safeguards because of good conduct: this is strictness in establishing rules. Where goodness warrants advancement, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not discount their conduct because of their category: this is generosity of heart. Strictness displays a constant standard for all ages; generosity conveys encouragement suited to the moment. How subtle is the sage’s teaching!
Nevertheless, those belonging to the Yi are, by convention, recorded by personal name. Shi of Zhou was a lord of the central states: why, then, is his personal name also recorded? Observance of ritual is specifically recorded as “paid court.” The Earl of Ji was also capable of observing ritual: why, then, does the text merely say “came”? The Spring and Autumn Annals works like the transforming power of creation. Although rulers of the central states are not recorded by personal name, it names Shi of Zhou to make plain a warning about what the feudal lords bring upon themselves. Although court visits must be recorded, it abbreviates the Earl of Ji’s visit to correct the fault of a subject’s forming private relations. Sometimes it names, sometimes it does not; sometimes it approves, sometimes it does not. Truly, this resembles the wondrous subtlety with which creation gives things their forms. How could it be confined to a single rule? Earlier scholars said that none but a sage could have compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals. How true!
“In summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi.” 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 “In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Yang Jing
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: “The reasoning is clear and the language correct; it penetrates deeply into the meaning of the topic.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “The wording has a sound basis; worthy of inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
脩禮以求安者大夫謀國之失順理以化强者
聖人相國之功此行父之如齊所以爲可貶而
聖人之神化則於夾谷之會而有徵矣宣之元
年遣卿如齊魯求安于鄰也時則將其命者實
行父焉夫敬嬴謀而出姜歸宣仲之惡極矣沐
浴之請吾於斯人有望也何乃任公室之輔甘
心納賂之行負忠良之名忍爲請會之舉私好
繼定而天討免加是則惡之黨也已噫相三君
而無私積范文子所以稱其賢也顯君之業固
===
所能爲使非有黨逆之累則勤勞恭儉之勳其
建立不有可觀哉君子謂行父使齊之失起於
三思之惑也不待貶而罪自見矣定之十年會
齊夾谷魯脩平于鄰也時則相是會者有孔子
焉夫犁彌謀而萊兵劫齊人之橫甚矣感動之
機信非聖人不能也幸而神人德義之對既以
格其心裔夷盟好之責又以昭其罪君知悔過
而臣請謝質是則化之神也已噫率其君以行
古道齊景公所以屬其臣也俄頃之功於斯可
punctuated:
脩禮以求安者，大夫謀國之失；順理以化强者，聖人相國之功。此行父之如齊所以爲可貶，而聖人之神化則於夾谷之會而有徵矣。宣之元年，遣卿如齊，魯求安于鄰也。時則將其命者，實行父焉。夫敬嬴謀而出姜歸，宣仲之惡極矣。沐浴之請，吾於斯人有望也。何乃任公室之輔，甘心納賂之行；負忠良之名，忍爲請會之舉？私好繼定，而天討免加，是則惡之黨也已。噫！相三君而無私積，范文子所以稱其賢也。顯君之業，固所能爲。使非有黨逆之累，則勤勞恭儉之勳，其建立不有可觀哉？君子謂行父使齊之失，起於三思之惑也。不待貶而罪自見矣。

定之十年，會齊夾谷，魯脩平于鄰也。時則相是會者，有孔子焉。夫犁彌謀而萊兵劫，齊人之橫甚矣。感動之機，信非聖人不能也。幸而神人德義之對，既以格其心；裔夷盟好之責，又以昭其罪。君知悔過，而臣請謝質，是則化之神也已。噫！率其君以行古道，齊景公所以屬其臣也。俄頃之功，於斯可
translation_en:
To observe ritual in pursuit of security was the error of a grand master planning for his state; to follow right principle and thereby transform the powerful was the achievement of the sage assisting in government. This is why Xingfu’s journey to Qi merits censure, while the sage’s wondrous transforming influence finds confirmation in the meeting at Jiagu. In the first year of Duke Xuan, a minister was dispatched to Qi: Lu was seeking security from its neighbor. The man who carried out this mission was indeed Xingfu. Jing Ying had plotted, and Chu Jiang had returned to her natal state; the wickedness of Duke Xuan and Zhong had reached its utmost. From this man I had hoped for a request to undertake punitive action, after ritual bathing. How could he, serving as a mainstay of the ducal house, willingly undertake a mission to offer bribes? How could he, bearing a reputation for loyalty and goodness, bring himself to request a meeting? Private friendly relations were subsequently secured, and Heaven’s punishment was averted: this was simply to become an accomplice in evil. Alas! He served as chief minister to three rulers without accumulating private wealth; this was why Fan Wenzi praised his worthiness. Bringing distinction to his ruler was certainly within his powers. Had he not been stained by complicity in rebellion, would not his achievements in diligence, reverence, and frugality have been considerable? The gentleman says that Xingfu’s error in his mission to Qi arose from the confusion of thinking three times. His guilt is evident without awaiting explicit censure.

In the tenth year of Duke Ding, he met the ruler of Qi at Jiagu: Lu was cultivating peaceful relations with its neighbor. The person assisting at this meeting was Confucius. Li Mi plotted, and troops from Lai threatened coercion; the people of Qi were exceedingly overbearing. Indeed, none but a sage could have seized the opportunity to move their hearts. Fortunately, his response concerning spirits, men, virtue, and righteousness had already reached their hearts; his rebuke concerning the use of outlying barbarians at a meeting intended to affirm friendly relations further exposed their wrongdoing. The ruler recognized his fault and repented, while his minister requested permission to apologize and offer a pledge of good faith [?]. Such was the wondrous power of moral transformation. Alas! Leading one’s ruler to practice the ancient Way was what Duke Jing of Qi enjoined upon his ministers. What could be accomplished in a brief moment can here …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
驗使其得邦家而治則綏來動和之效其治功
不尤可尚哉君子謂仲尼一言之感重於三軍
之威者亦順於理而已矣是則任臣如行父魯
政所以下移也相禮如孔子聖道所以小試也
觀其所用而魯之失得見矣抑孔子用魯之化
不特徵於斯也繼而爲魯司寇攝相事遂墮三
都誅少正卯三月而商賈信男女別魯國大治
朞月而可信其然矣奈之何女樂沮而孔子行
三年有成之化載諸空言而已然六經刪述而
===
其道昭如日星是則萬世之太平固在也故曰
聖人者以人合天不任於天以義立命不委於
命
禮記
考禮正刑一德以尊于天子
俞世傑
同考試官教諭揭批〔述職尊君之意發揮殆盡錄之以勸效忠者〕
考試官教諭毛批〔豐潤可式〕
punctuated:
驗。使其得邦家而治，則綏來動和之效，其治功不尤可尚哉？君子謂仲尼一言之感重於三軍之威者，亦順於理而已矣。是則任臣如行父，魯政所以下移也；相禮如孔子，聖道所以小試也。觀其所用，而魯之失得見矣。抑孔子用魯之化，不特徵於斯也。繼而爲魯司寇，攝相事，遂墮三都，誅少正卯，三月而商賈信、男女別，魯國大治。朞月而可，信其然矣。奈之何女樂沮而孔子行，三年有成之化，載諸空言而已。然六經刪述，而其道昭如日星，是則萬世之太平固在也。故曰：「聖人者，以人合天，不任於天；以義立命，不委於命。」

《禮記》
考禮正刑，一德以尊于天子。
俞世傑
同考試官教諭揭批〔述職尊君之意，發揮殆盡，錄之以勸效忠者。〕
考試官教諭毛批〔豐潤可式。〕
translation_en:
…verified. Had he been entrusted with a state to govern, would not his accomplishments in government—the effects of bringing people to him by pacifying them and bringing them into harmony by stirring them to action—have been still more worthy of esteem? The gentleman says that the moving power of a single utterance by Zhongni outweighed the might of the three armies simply because it accorded with principle. Thus, employing a minister such as Xingfu caused governmental authority in Lu to pass into subordinate hands; having someone such as Kongzi assist at the rites afforded a small trial of the Way of the sage. By observing whom Lu employed, we can see its failures and successes.

Yet the transforming influence of Kongzi’s service in Lu was not demonstrated by this alone. Subsequently, he became Minister of Justice in Lu and concurrently performed the duties of chief minister. He then demolished the fortifications of the three cities and executed Shaozheng Mao. Within three months, merchants were trustworthy, men and women observed proper distinctions, and Lu was well governed. The claim that results could be achieved within a full year was indeed borne out. Alas, female entertainers thwarted his work, and Kongzi departed. The transformation that would have reached fruition in three years remained recorded only in unrealized words. Nevertheless, through his editing and exposition of the Six Classics, his Way shines as brightly as the sun and stars. In this, the foundation for peace throughout all ages assuredly remains. Hence it is said: “The sage brings human action into accord with Heaven, rather than leaving matters to Heaven; he establishes his destiny through righteousness, rather than resigning himself to destiny.”

Book of Rites
“Examine the rites and rectify punishments; make virtue uniform, thereby honoring the Son of Heaven.”
Yu Shijie
Associate Examiner Jie, an Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of reporting on one’s duties and honoring the ruler is expounded almost exhaustively. This is included to encourage those who would serve loyally.〕
Examiner Mao, an Instructor, comments: 〔Rich and polished; worthy of emulation.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王批文字中可占忠敬
人臣盡述職之典將以致尊君之義也夫天王
大一統者也諸侯於述職之時而脩其所當脩
焉非所以尊君者乎記王制者之意蓋謂天下
之不可逃者君臣之分而人臣之不可忽者敬
君之心天子無事與諸侯相見固矣然豈徒侈
乎彌文而已哉蓋自人君之節天下者有禮焉
議諸宗伯雖有定體而奉行於侯邦者得無違
僭乎故於來朝而考之凡所以治神人和上下
===
者無敢自用也稽之以經常之則必使率由乎
舊章斯可矣自人君之威天下者有刑焉議諸
司寇雖有定法而奉行於侯邦者寧無偏枉乎
故於來朝而正之凡所以詰姦慝刑暴亂者無
敢自專也制之以中正之規必使不違乎成憲
斯已矣若夫一德之存又君之所以屬望於臣
而臣之所以自獻者也則於斯時也揆之謀慮
以驗其篤棐之誠察之身心以占其靖共之節
必使勿貳以二勿參以三咸有一德足以近天
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：文字中可占忠敬。

人臣盡述職之典，將以致尊君之義也。夫天王，大一統者也。諸侯於述職之時，而脩其所當脩焉，非所以尊君者乎？記《王制》者之意，蓋謂天下之不可逃者，君臣之分；而人臣之不可忽者，敬君之心。天子無事，與諸侯相見，固矣。然豈徒侈乎彌文而已哉？蓋自人君之節天下者，有禮焉。議諸宗伯，雖有定體，而奉行於侯邦者，得無違僭乎？故於來朝而考之。凡所以治神人、和上下者，無敢自用也。稽之以經常之則，必使率由乎舊章，斯可矣。自人君之威天下者，有刑焉。議諸司寇，雖有定法，而奉行於侯邦者，寧無偏枉乎？故於來朝而正之。凡所以詰姦慝、刑暴亂者，無敢自專也。制之以中正之規，必使不違乎成憲，斯已矣。若夫一德之存，又君之所以屬望於臣，而臣之所以自獻者也。則於斯時也，揆之謀慮，以驗其篤棐之誠；察之身心，以占其靖共之節。必使勿貳以二，勿參以三，咸有一德，足以近天
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “Loyalty and reverence can be discerned in the writing.”

When a subject fully performs the prescribed duties of reporting on his administration, he thereby fulfills the obligation to honor his ruler. The heavenly king presides over the great unity of the realm. When the feudal lords report on their administration and put in order what they ought to put in order, is this not how they honor their ruler? The intention of those who recorded the “Royal Regulations” was presumably this: no one under Heaven can escape the distinction between ruler and subject, and no subject may neglect a reverent heart toward his ruler. In times free of trouble, it is fitting that the Son of Heaven should meet with the feudal lords. Yet could this be merely an extravagant display of elaborate ceremony?

Now, ritual is the means by which the ruler regulates all under Heaven. Although its established forms have been deliberated upon by the Minister of Rites, could its implementation in the feudal states be entirely free of transgression and usurpation? Thus, when the lords come to court, their ritual practices are examined. In everything concerning the ordering of relations with spirits and people and the harmonizing of superiors and inferiors, none dare act on their own judgment. Their practices are checked against enduring standards; only when they are made to follow the old institutions is this satisfactory.

Punishments are the means by which the ruler holds all under Heaven in awe. Although established laws have been deliberated upon by the Minister of Justice, could their implementation in the feudal states be entirely free of partiality and injustice? Thus, when the lords come to court, their punishments are rectified. In everything concerning the investigation of wickedness and the punishment of violence and disorder, none dare exercise authority on their own. They are regulated by standards of impartiality and correctness; they must be made to observe the established laws without deviation.

As for maintaining singleness of virtue, this is what the ruler expects of his subjects and what his subjects offer him in service. At this time, therefore, their plans and deliberations are assessed to test the sincerity of their devoted assistance; their conduct and hearts are examined to discern their steadfast reverence. They must not let a second purpose divide them, nor a third further fragment them. All must possess a single virtue, sufficient to draw near to the Son of Heaven …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
子之光斯可矣若此者謂非所以尊於天子耶
蓋天子者建惟皇之極而德教期於不悖操獨
運之權而邦令期於必行其所以綦天下之貴
者固於此乎在也今於來朝而考禮正刑焉見
其自天子出非人臣所得紛更也肅將而無失
者皆所以盡對揚之忱又於來朝而一德焉見
其心在王室非斯須所得慢易也侯度之克謹
者實所以遵紀法之宗事之在於諸侯者無異
政則尊之在於天子者豈復有二上乎是則人
===
臣之義既盡則天王之分自明於諸侯之朝不
可以想見盛世之風乎雖然禮也刑也德也三
者固皆人臣之所當盡然一德爲要焉書曰德
惟一動罔不吉人臣能一其德則其所以考禮
正刑者出之有本自無私意之累而可以稱明
王之治矣苟爲不然則其施之於禮樂刑政之
間者皆霸術功利之私耳何以四達而不悖也
後之欲爲純臣者當自一德始
外無敵內順治此之謂盛德
punctuated:
子之光，斯可矣。若此者，謂非所以尊於天子耶？蓋天子者，建惟皇之極，而德教期於不悖；操獨運之權，而邦令期於必行。其所以綦天下之貴者，固於此乎在也。今於來朝而考禮正刑焉，見其自天子出，非人臣所得紛更也。肅將而無失者，皆所以盡對揚之忱。又於來朝而一德焉，見其心在王室，非斯須所得慢易也。侯度之克謹者，實所以遵紀法之宗。事之在於諸侯者無異政，則尊之在於天子者，豈復有二上乎？是則人臣之義既盡，則天王之分自明。於諸侯之朝，不可以想見盛世之風乎？雖然，禮也、刑也、德也，三者固皆人臣之所當盡，然一德爲要焉。《書》曰：「德惟一，動罔不吉。」人臣能一其德，則其所以考禮正刑者，出之有本，自無私意之累，而可以稱明王之治矣。苟爲不然，則其施之於禮樂刑政之間者，皆霸術功利之私耳，何以四達而不悖也？後之欲爲純臣者，當自一德始。

外無敵，內順治，此之謂盛德。
translation_en:
…the radiance of the Son of Heaven: only then will it suffice. Could such conduct be said not to honor the Son of Heaven? The Son of Heaven establishes the sovereign’s supreme standard, seeking to ensure that moral instruction does not deviate from it; he exercises sole authority, seeking to ensure that the commands of the realm are invariably carried out. Here, indeed, lies the basis of his supreme eminence throughout the world. When the feudal lords come to court and he examines their rites and rectifies their punishments, this shows that these proceed from the Son of Heaven and may not be arbitrarily altered by his subjects. In reverently carrying them out without error, they fully express their sincere desire to acknowledge and uphold his commands. Furthermore, when they come to court and are made steadfast in virtue, this shows that their hearts are devoted to the royal house and that they may not be negligent or disrespectful even for a moment. Their scrupulous observance of the standards governing feudal lords is precisely how they adhere to the ultimate source of order and law. If the feudal lords conduct their affairs without divergent policies, how could the supremacy vested in the Son of Heaven admit of two rulers? Thus, once the duties of subjects are fully discharged, the rightful station of the heavenly king becomes clear of itself. Can we not envision the character of a flourishing age in these court audiences of the feudal lords?

Nevertheless, although rites, punishments, and virtue are all matters in which subjects must fulfill their duties, steadfastness in virtue is the essential one. The Book of Documents says: “When virtue is single, no action is inauspicious.” If subjects can remain steadfast in virtue, their examination of rites and rectification of punishments will proceed from a sound foundation. They will naturally be free of the encumbrance of selfish intentions and can accord with the government of an enlightened king. Otherwise, all that they put into practice in rites, music, punishments, and government will merely be the self-serving pursuit of achievement and advantage through the techniques of hegemonic rule. How could this extend in all four directions without contravening the proper order? Those in later ages who wish to become subjects of unalloyed loyalty should begin with steadfastness in virtue.

“To have no adversaries abroad, and obedience and good order at home: this is called consummate virtue.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
潘龍
同考試官教諭揭批講盛德處甚得旨啓發興起之士
觀此可以興矣
考試官教諭毛批爾雅之作
考試官學正王批辭簡意盡
君子隨用而成功可以觀其所養矣夫無敵順
治功之著於內外者溥矣非盛德能如是乎聘
射有取於勇敢强有力者以其有養也意若曰
功莫難於兼濟德必要於渾全即勇敢强有力
===
者觀之而盛德存乎其中矣蓋斯人也用之於
軍旅而威敵焉所以攘外也則見嚴毅行於征
伐而一怒奮安民之勇震疊本乎德威而一舉
收靖遠之功師以貞勝也而天下畏之武烈昭
矣不謂之無敵乎用於邦國而附衆焉所以安
內也則見治道達於禮義之立而施之以不悖
德澤沛於輯綏之久而動焉以有孚治以順達
也而天下懷之文教敷矣不謂之順治乎夫不
足於武則外患之未弭偏於柔而已不足於文
punctuated:
潘龍

同考試官教諭揭批：講盛德處甚得旨，啓發興起之士，觀此可以興矣。
考試官教諭毛批：爾雅之作。
考試官學正王批：辭簡意盡。

君子隨用而成功，可以觀其所養矣。夫無敵順治，功之著於內外者溥矣，非盛德能如是乎？聘射有取於勇敢强有力者，以其有養也。意若曰：功莫難於兼濟，德必要於渾全。即勇敢强有力者觀之，而盛德存乎其中矣。蓋斯人也，用之於軍旅而威敵焉，所以攘外也。則見嚴毅行於征伐，而一怒奮安民之勇；震疊本乎德威，而一舉收靖遠之功。師以貞勝也，而天下畏之，武烈昭矣，不謂之無敵乎？用於邦國而附衆焉，所以安內也。則見治道達於禮義之立，而施之以不悖；德澤沛於輯綏之久，而動焉以有孚。治以順達也，而天下懷之，文教敷矣，不謂之順治乎？夫不足於武，則外患之未弭，偏於柔而已；不足於文，
translation_en:
Pan Long

Comment by Associate Examiner Jie, Instructor: His discussion of abundant virtue captures the meaning very well. It enlightens and inspires aspiring scholars; reading this, they can indeed be stirred to action.
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: A refined and elegant composition.
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: Concise in wording, complete in meaning.

The gentleman achieves success in whatever capacity he is employed, revealing what he has cultivated within himself. To be without rivals abroad and to govern harmoniously at home—how far-reaching are the achievements thus manifested within and without! Could anyone accomplish this without abundant virtue? That diplomatic visits and archery [?] value men who are courageous, strong, and powerful is because such men possess inward cultivation. The meaning is as if to say: no achievement is harder than bringing benefit to all, and virtue must above all be whole and complete. Even if we consider only the courageous, strong, and powerful man, abundant virtue resides within him.

When such a man is employed in the army, he overawes the enemy: this is how he repels external threats. We then see his stern resolution exercised in punitive campaigns, a single outburst of wrath rousing the courage that brings peace to the people. His awe-inspiring force rests upon the majesty of virtue, and in a single undertaking he achieves the pacification of distant regions. His army wins through rectitude, and all under Heaven fear him. His martial accomplishments shine forth: is this not what it means to be without rivals?

When employed in governing a state, he wins the allegiance of the multitude: this is how he secures peace within. We then see the Way of government realized through the establishment of ritual and righteousness, and implemented without deviation. His beneficent influence flows abundantly through sustained efforts to bring people together and settle them in peace, and his actions inspire trust. Government succeeds through accordance with what is right, and all under Heaven cherish him. Civilizing instruction spreads everywhere: is this not harmonious governance?

If he is deficient in martial ability, external troubles remain unquelled, and he is merely inclined too far toward softness; if he is deficient in civil accomplishment, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則內治之未脩偏於剛而已皆未足語盛德也
今順治之中而嚴威者存焉勇之發於軍旅者
不徇乎血氣之私剛健中正而非徒柔者矣果
毅之中而禮讓者寓焉道之敷於邦國者皆得
於躬行之實優柔平中而非徒剛者矣剛克柔
克而同歸於至一之協兼體而不累也允文允
武而動合乎時措之宜相濟以成能也不謂之
盛德而何哉是則所貴於勇敢者爲其行禮也
所貴於行禮者爲其致用也蓋至於無敵順治
===
===
而德斯盛矣勇敢之士可不知所以自養乎抑
非勇敢強有力者不足以行禮故先王貴之也
然必責其行禮焉非有他也蓋人之賦性鮮有
不偏勇固可貴而害亦甚先王蓋欲裁成變化
以歸於中也是故責之以禮義而要其成功勇
而無禮則爲剛愎爲不遜何以收無敵順治之
功乎周宣王威嚴順治而詩人歸其美於文武
之吉甫使夫人而勇於行禮也夫孰非吉甫哉
第貳場
punctuated:
則內治之未脩，偏於剛而已，皆未足語盛德也。今順治之中而嚴威者存焉，勇之發於軍旅者，不徇乎血氣之私，剛健中正而非徒柔者矣。果毅之中而禮讓者寓焉，道之敷於邦國者，皆得於躬行之實，優柔平中而非徒剛者矣。剛克柔克，而同歸於至一之協，兼體而不累也；允文允武，而動合乎時措之宜，相濟以成能也。不謂之盛德而何哉？是則所貴於勇敢者，爲其行禮也；所貴於行禮者，爲其致用也。蓋至於無敵順治，而德斯盛矣。勇敢之士，可不知所以自養乎？抑非勇敢強有力者，不足以行禮，故先王貴之也。然必責其行禮焉，非有他也。蓋人之賦性，鮮有不偏，勇固可貴，而害亦甚。先王蓋欲裁成變化，以歸於中也。是故責之以禮義，而要其成功。勇而無禮，則爲剛愎，爲不遜，何以收無敵順治之功乎？周宣王威嚴順治，而詩人歸其美於文武之吉甫。使夫人而勇於行禮也，夫孰非吉甫哉？

第貳場
translation_en:
…then internal government remains uncultivated, inclining solely toward hardness. Neither condition warrants speaking of consummate virtue. Now, within harmonious government, stern authority remains: the courage displayed in military affairs does not indulge the selfish impulses of blood and vital energy, but is firm, vigorous, centered, and upright, rather than merely yielding. Within resolution and determination reside ritual propriety and deference: the Way extended throughout the realm is grounded entirely in actual personal practice, being gentle, accommodating, balanced, and centered, rather than merely hard. Governing through firmness and governing through gentleness converge in perfect unity and harmony; both are embodied without encumbering each other. Truly accomplished in both civil and military affairs, one acts as circumstances require; the two complement each other to achieve their full capacity. What could this be called but consummate virtue? Thus, courage is valued because it enables the practice of ritual propriety; the practice of ritual propriety is valued because it enables effective action. When one achieves invincibility and harmonious government, virtue is indeed consummate. Can courageous men afford not to understand how to cultivate themselves?

Yet those who lack courage, strength, and power are insufficiently equipped to practice ritual propriety; hence the former kings valued these qualities. Nevertheless, they invariably required such men to practice ritual propriety, and for no other reason than this: human beings are endowed with dispositions that are seldom free of partiality. Courage is certainly valuable, but its harm can also be great. The former kings wished to shape and transform it so that it would return to the mean. They therefore held such men to ritual propriety and righteousness, and demanded that they bring their work to completion. Courage without ritual propriety becomes obstinacy and insubordination. How could it achieve invincibility and harmonious government? King Xuan of Zhou exercised stern authority and governed harmoniously, and the poet attributed the credit to Jifu, accomplished in both civil and military affairs. If everyone were courageous in practicing ritual propriety, who would not be a Jifu?

Second Session

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
論
聖人太極之全體
許鎡
同考試官教諭浦批自性之初發太極全體詞意親
切議論宏邃視掇拾蔓華者遠矣宜冠多士
考試官教諭毛批理致淵然具占造詣之純
考試官學正王批才贍理足積學之士也取之
聖人者其得天之厚者乎其渾然夫性之初者
乎夫凡稟命於天者皆性也聖人何言乎其初
===
也太極之理繼之者善而氣不與存焉人之所
得於天地之初也惟初故一惟一故全其偏焉
者氣之囿一之漓而蔽其初者耳性之初者未
嘗漓故聖人之心未始雜人見其未始雜也以
爲聖人之心渾然一貫萬理具足則聖人之學
致然而不知聖人所以全其性之初者蓋非有
待於外也聖人者天將命之以兼攝萬類均理
萬化則非以其渾然而至一者厚之以爲宰制
和一之具未能也故聖人之性一天之性也未
punctuated:
論
聖人太極之全體
許鎡

同考試官教諭浦批：自性之初發太極全體，詞意親切，議論宏邃，視掇拾蔓華者遠矣，宜冠多士。
考試官教諭毛批：理致淵然，具占造詣之純。
考試官學正王批：才贍理足，積學之士也，取之。

聖人者，其得天之厚者乎？其渾然夫性之初者乎？夫凡稟命於天者皆性也，聖人何言乎其初也？太極之理，繼之者善，而氣不與存焉，人之所得於天地之初也。惟初故一，惟一故全。其偏焉者，氣之囿、一之漓，而蔽其初者耳。性之初者未嘗漓，故聖人之心未始雜。人見其未始雜也，以爲聖人之心渾然一貫，萬理具足，則聖人之學致然，而不知聖人所以全其性之初者，蓋非有待於外也。聖人者，天將命之以兼攝萬類，均理萬化，則非以其渾然而至一者厚之，以爲宰制和一之具，未能也。故聖人之性，一天之性也，未
translation_en:
Discourse
The Sage Embodies the Supreme Ultimate in Its Entirety
Xu Zi 許鎡

Comment by Associate Examiner Pu, Instructor: He elucidates the entirety of the Supreme Ultimate from the original state of human nature. His wording and meaning are apt and incisive, and his argument broad and profound, far surpassing those who merely gather ornamental verbiage. He deserves to rank first among the candidates.
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: His exposition of principle is profound and reveals [?] the purity of his attainment.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Abundant talent and ample reasoning: he is a man of accumulated learning. Accept him.

Is the sage one whom Heaven has richly endowed? Is he one who remains an undivided whole in the original state of his nature? Now, whatever is received as an endowment from Heaven is human nature. Why, in speaking of the sage, do we speak of its original state? As for the principle of the Supreme Ultimate, that which continues it is goodness, with material force (qi) having no part therein: this is what human beings receive at their beginning from Heaven and Earth. Precisely because it is original, it is one; precisely because it is one, it is complete. Any partiality is merely the confinement imposed by material force and the fragmentation of unity, obscuring that original state. The original state of human nature has never been fragmented; hence the sage’s mind has never been mixed. People see that it has never been mixed and suppose that the sage’s mind forms an undivided unity, with all principles fully present, because his learning has brought this about. They do not understand that the sage’s preservation of the original state of his nature in its entirety does not depend on anything external. Heaven intends to charge the sage with comprehensively governing the myriad kinds of beings and equitably ordering the myriad transformations. Unless Heaven richly endowed him with that which is undivided and supremely one, as the means of governing, harmonizing, and unifying, he could not accomplish this. Thus the sage’s nature is wholly the nature of Heaven; never …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之有漓焉爾聖人之心一天之心也未之有雜
焉爾是故湛乎其常虛而非寂也犂乎其常覺
而非感也淵乎其與神俱入天下不見其機焉
而非內也倏乎其與化俱出天下不見其迹焉
而非外也寂感皆融內外合一而中正仁義之
極無不在夫是之謂太極之全體夫是之謂聖
人夫所謂太極者何也夫子蓋甞言之矣曰易
有太極夫易之爲道言屢遷也風雨露雷無弗
變也天各一其象矣水火土石無弗化也地各
===
一其形矣皇帝王霸道德功力無弗錯綜也人
各一其感矣是易者天下之至渙然而不可以
一者也聖人乃悉櫽括而歸之於太極何哉噫
斯所謂理之渾然一者固有以一之也夫方其
未兩也渾然爾矣動靜分焉則一者兩之矣方
其未五也渾然爾矣木火土金水生焉則一者
五之矣方事之未感也渾然爾矣五性動而剛
柔善惡以類分焉則一者萬之矣夫其有所分
也卽不可以言全然二者一之始分猶未甚漓
punctuated:
之有漓焉爾。聖人之心，一天之心也，未之有雜焉爾。是故湛乎其常虛而非寂也，犂乎其常覺而非感也，淵乎其與神俱入，天下不見其機焉，而非內也；倏乎其與化俱出，天下不見其迹焉，而非外也。寂感皆融，內外合一，而中正仁義之極無不在。夫是之謂太極之全體，夫是之謂聖人。
夫所謂太極者何也？夫子蓋甞言之矣，曰：「易有太極。」夫易之爲道，言屢遷也。風雨露雷，無弗變也，天各一其象矣；水火土石，無弗化也，地各一其形矣；皇帝王霸，道德功力，無弗錯綜也，人各一其感矣。是易者，天下之至渙然而不可以一者也。聖人乃悉櫽括而歸之於太極，何哉？噫！斯所謂理之渾然一者，固有以一之也。夫方其未兩也，渾然爾矣；動靜分焉，則一者兩之矣。方其未五也，渾然爾矣；木火土金水生焉，則一者五之矣。方事之未感也，渾然爾矣；五性動而剛柔善惡以類分焉，則一者萬之矣。夫其有所分也，卽不可以言全。然二者，一之始分，猶未甚漓
translation_en:
…has undergone no dispersal, that is all. The sage’s mind is one with Heaven’s mind; it has undergone no admixture, that is all. Thus, profoundly clear, it is always empty, yet not quiescent; lucid, it is always aware, yet not responding to stimuli. Fathomlessly, it enters together with the numinous, so that none under Heaven can perceive its workings, yet it is not merely inward. Swiftly, it emerges together with transformation, so that none under Heaven can perceive its traces, yet it is not merely outward. Quiescence and response are wholly integrated; inward and outward unite as one. The utmost standard of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness is present throughout. This is what is called the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate (taiji); this is what is called the sage.
What is meant by the Supreme Ultimate? The Master once spoke of it, saying: “In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate.” As for the Way of the Changes, its formulations repeatedly shift. Wind, rain, dew, and thunder all change; in Heaven, each has its distinct manifestation. Water, fire, earth, and stone all undergo transformation; on Earth, each has its distinct form. August sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons; the Way, virtue, achievement, and force—all are interwoven, and among human beings each has its distinct response. Thus, change is the most thoroughly dispersed thing under Heaven, seemingly impossible to unify. Yet the sage comprehensively embraces it and brings it back to the Supreme Ultimate. Why? Ah! What is called the undivided unity of principle assuredly provides the means to unify it.
Before it becomes two, it is simply an undivided whole. When movement and stillness separate, the one becomes two. Before it becomes five, it is simply an undivided whole. When wood, fire, earth, metal, and water arise, the one becomes five. Before affairs evoke a response, it is simply an undivided whole. When the five constituents of human nature are stirred, and firmness and softness, goodness and evil separate according to their kinds, the one becomes the myriad. Once there is division, one can no longer speak of wholeness. Yet the two are only the beginning of the division of the one, and have not yet become greatly dispersed…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乎其初及太極之妙乘乎其機于是乎一而二
二而五二五絪縕之氣互爲變合而紛紜雜揉
卒不可勝窮蓋至是而太極渾淪之初愈分愈
漓雖欲反其萬之漓而會之至一之初也非甚
矯拂困勉必不能矣故人滯於所賦高明沉潛
者之不能以相克溺於所習仁智者之不能以
互資隨所見而目爲全體焉何則漓之者使然
也天地以民生之寢漓焉而不可以還其初於
是聖人生焉是聖人者天之所厚而以太極之
===
全體畀之者也是故闔者之不能爲闢言殊性
也聖人則闔闢涵其機矣覆者之不能爲載言
殊職也聖人則覆載兼其用矣生者之不能爲
成言殊能也聖人則生成合其撰矣百姓得其
漓故常化於物聖人得其一則粹乎不以天下
萬物撓已也天下見聖人之動而不知其不囿
於動何者所以爲動之本體者未甞動也天下
見聖人之靜而不知其不囿於靜何者所以爲
靜之本體者未甞靜也夫聖人之心方其寂也
punctuated: 乎其初。及太極之妙乘乎其機，于是乎一而二，二而五，二五絪縕之氣互爲變合，而紛紜雜揉，卒不可勝窮。蓋至是而太極渾淪之初愈分愈漓，雖欲反其萬之漓而會之至一之初也，非甚矯拂困勉，必不能矣。故人滯於所賦，高明沉潛者之不能以相克；溺於所習，仁智者之不能以互資；隨所見而目爲全體焉。何則？漓之者使然也。天地以民生之寢漓焉，而不可以還其初，于是聖人生焉。是聖人者，天之所厚而以太極之全體畀之者也。是故闔者之不能爲闢，言殊性也，聖人則闔闢涵其機矣；覆者之不能爲載，言殊職也，聖人則覆載兼其用矣；生者之不能爲成，言殊能也，聖人則生成合其撰矣。百姓得其漓，故常化於物；聖人得其一，則粹乎不以天下萬物撓已也。天下見聖人之動，而不知其不囿於動，何者？所以爲動之本體者未甞動也。天下見聖人之靜，而不知其不囿於靜，何者？所以爲靜之本體者未甞靜也。夫聖人之心，方其寂也，
translation_en: …from its original state. When the wondrous workings of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) take advantage of the incipient impulse, the One becomes Two, and the Two become Five. The intermingling vital energies of the Two and the Five transform and combine with one another, becoming so profusely intertwined that their possibilities can never be exhausted. By this stage, the original undivided wholeness of the Supreme Ultimate becomes increasingly dispersed as it differentiates. Even if one wishes to reverse this dispersion into myriad things and bring them together in the original state of utmost unity, one certainly cannot do so without strenuous correction of one’s tendencies and arduous effort. Thus people remain confined by their endowments: those of lofty intelligence and those of deep reserve cannot use these qualities to counterbalance one another. They become immersed in their accustomed practices: the benevolent and the wise cannot draw upon one another. Each follows what he sees and regards it as the whole. Why is this? Dispersion makes it so. Because human life grows increasingly dispersed and cannot return to its original state, Heaven and Earth bring forth the sage. The sage is one whom Heaven richly favors, bestowing upon him the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. Thus, that what closes cannot open expresses a difference in nature; yet the sage encompasses the impulses of both closing and opening. That what covers cannot support expresses a difference in function; yet the sage combines the operations of both covering and supporting. That what generates cannot bring to completion expresses a difference in capacity; yet the sage unites the work of both generation and completion. Ordinary people receive what is dispersed and are therefore constantly transformed by external things. The sage receives the unity and is thus so pure that he does not allow the myriad things under Heaven to disturb him. The world sees the sage’s activity but does not know that he is not confined by activity. Why? Because the fundamental substance underlying his activity has never been active. The world sees the sage’s stillness but does not know that he is not confined by stillness. Why? Because the fundamental substance underlying his stillness has never been still. Now, as for the sage’s mind, when it is quiescent…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
淵乎其深純之至也冲乎其凝湛之極也頽乎
其一化之神也當是時雖鬼神無以窺其微天
地無以指其蘊焉非不可以爲靜也然淵然深
者惺然而常照也冲然凝者盎然而常運也頽
然一者洞然而常貫也蓋鬼神微是無以爲之
宅天地微是無以爲之宰而中正仁義之極常
周流於動靜之間而不離故泯然無感之中若
非虛明應物之妙而幾微之際一有感焉則凡
思之而通觸之而應蓋有渾然全體應物而不
===
窮者是乃天命流行生生不已之機卽一日之
間幾務沓至而其寂然之本體則固未甞不存
也所謂未發已發其機一焉而已所謂大本達
道其理均焉而已所謂天地位萬物育其化齊
焉而已雖然聖人亦豈以其天之所獨厚者顧
漫然無所用其心哉昔者堯舜大聖人也書稱
德曰欽明文思安安允恭克讓曰濬哲文明温
恭允塞其於太極之體可謂合矣其稱治曰協
和萬邦黎民於變時雍曰四方風動從欲以治
punctuated:
淵乎其深，純之至也；冲乎其凝，湛之極也；頽乎其一，化之神也。當是時，雖鬼神無以窺其微，天地無以指其蘊焉，非不可以爲靜也。然淵然深者，惺然而常照也；冲然凝者，盎然而常運也；頽然一者，洞然而常貫也。蓋鬼神微是，無以爲之宅；天地微是，無以爲之宰。而中正仁義之極，常周流於動靜之間而不離。故泯然無感之中，若非虛明應物之妙，而幾微之際一有感焉，則凡思之而通，觸之而應，蓋有渾然全體應物而不窮者。是乃天命流行、生生不已之機。卽一日之間，幾務沓至，而其寂然之本體，則固未甞不存也。所謂未發已發，其機一焉而已；所謂大本達道，其理均焉而已；所謂天地位、萬物育，其化齊焉而已。
雖然，聖人亦豈以其天之所獨厚者，顧漫然無所用其心哉？昔者堯舜，大聖人也。《書》稱德曰：「欽明文思安安，允恭克讓。」曰：「濬哲文明，温恭允塞。」其於太極之體，可謂合矣。其稱治曰：「協和萬邦，黎民於變時雍。」曰：「四方風動，從欲以治。」
translation_en:
…fathomless in its depth, it is purity at its utmost; empty and still in its concentration, it is lucidity at its highest; effortlessly merged into unity, it is the wondrous efficacy of transformation. At such a time, even spirits cannot discern its subtleties, nor can Heaven and Earth point out what it holds within. It may indeed be called still. Yet what is fathomlessly deep remains alert and constantly illuminates; what is empty and concentrated remains full of vitality and constantly operates; what effortlessly merges into unity remains penetrating and constantly pervades. Without this, spirits would have no dwelling, and Heaven and Earth would have no governing master. The supreme standard of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness constantly circulates between activity and stillness, never departing from them. Thus, in its undifferentiated state, untouched by any stimulus, it seems not to display the subtle capacity of empty clarity to respond to things [?]. Yet the moment a stimulus arises at the most subtle juncture, whatever it considers is understood, and whatever touches it receives a response. Its integral wholeness responds to things without exhaustion. This is the working of Heaven’s mandate as it circulates, generating life without cease. Even when the manifold affairs of government crowd upon it within a single day, its fundamentally quiescent substance never fails to remain present. What are called the states before and after arousal share but one operation; what are called the great foundation and the universally prevailing Way share but one principle; what is called Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad things being nourished shares but one transforming efficacy.
Nevertheless, could the sage, because Heaven has endowed him with exceptional generosity, simply remain heedless and leave his mind unapplied? Yao and Shun of antiquity were great sages. Describing their virtues, the Book of Documents says of Yao: “Reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, naturally at ease in these qualities; truly respectful and capable of yielding.” Of Shun it says: “Profoundly wise and brilliantly accomplished, gentle and respectful, truly sincere.” They may be said to have accorded with the substance of the Supreme Ultimate. Describing their government, it says of Yao: “He harmonized the myriad states, and the common people were transformed and brought into concord.” Of Shun it says: “The four quarters were stirred as by the wind”; “He followed his desires and achieved good government.” …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
錫極之化亦可謂孚突然當時君臣之相告戒
也惟精惟一惟時惟幾日孳孳焉而喜起交脩
昌言互益常不敢以一日寧者斯豈有所勉焉
而試爲之者與噫斯其爲太極全體之心也聖
人心通太極之運無止息之時太極爲天地萬
物之體聖人以天地萬物爲體故精一之戒所
以察吾之大體也而百體于此流焉時幾之勅
所以察吾之百體也而大體于此宰焉苟一癢
疴之及其害無幾而其相爲抑搔也不言而自
===
喻何則其中固有以貫之也至誠惻怛昭明不
昧故常不以其大者自足而以其猶有憾者自
見其所未能是固其心體之未始漓未始雜者
穆然運之雖欲已之而不可得者也未始漓故
常覺未始雜故常一常覺常一皆非有待於外
者也心極全體之眞其神矣哉雖然所謂漓者
亦未始不可使反於一也一之分而爲二也二
之分而爲五也五之分而爲萬也所謂一者未
始不存也上之而生知安行也次之而學知利
punctuated:
錫極之化亦可謂孚突然。當時君臣之相告戒也，惟精惟一，惟時惟幾，日孳孳焉，而喜起交脩，昌言互益，常不敢以一日寧者，斯豈有所勉焉而試爲之者與？噫！斯其爲太極全體之心也。聖人心通太極之運，無止息之時。太極爲天地萬物之體，聖人以天地萬物爲體，故精一之戒，所以察吾之大體也，而百體于此流焉；時幾之勅，所以察吾之百體也，而大體于此宰焉。苟一癢疴之及，其害無幾，而其相爲抑搔也，不言而自喻。何則？其中固有以貫之也。至誠惻怛，昭明不昧，故常不以其大者自足，而以其猶有憾者自見其所未能。是固其心體之未始漓、未始雜者，穆然運之，雖欲已之而不可得者也。未始漓，故常覺；未始雜，故常一。常覺常一，皆非有待於外者也。心極全體之眞，其神矣哉！

雖然，所謂漓者，亦未始不可使反於一也。一之分而爲二也，二之分而爲五也，五之分而爲萬也，所謂一者未始不存也。上之而生知安行也，次之而學知利
translation_en:
…The transforming influence of bestowing the supreme norm may also be said to have won trust [?]. Yet when ruler and ministers admonished one another in those days, they urged refinement and single-mindedness, attention to the proper time and to the incipient signs of change. Diligent every day, they joyfully roused one another to action and cultivated themselves together, benefiting one another through excellent counsel. They never dared allow themselves even a day of repose. Could this have been something they merely attempted through effort? Ah! This was their mind embodying the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) in its entirety. The sage’s mind participates in the workings of the Supreme Ultimate, never for a moment ceasing. The Supreme Ultimate constitutes the substance of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things; the sage takes Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as his own body. Thus, the admonition to refinement and single-mindedness serves to examine our greater body, from which the functioning of all its members flows. The injunction to attend to timing and incipient change serves to examine all our bodily members, over which the greater body presides. Should even a little itching or pain occur, its harm is slight, yet the members respond by pressing or scratching, understanding one another without words. Why is this? Because something within them inherently unites them. Utterly sincere and compassionate, luminous and unobscured, the sage is never satisfied with his greatness, but uses his remaining shortcomings to perceive what he has not yet achieved. It is precisely the substance of his mind, never diluted or adulterated, that serenely sets this in motion: even if he wished to stop, he could not. Because it is never diluted, it is always aware; because it is never adulterated, it is always unified. Constant awareness and constant unity depend on nothing external. How wondrous is the true entirety of the mind and the Supreme Ultimate!

Nevertheless, what is called dilution can still be brought back to unity. The One divides into the Two; the Two divide into the Five; the Five divide into the myriad things. Yet what is called the One is never absent. At the highest level are those who know innately and act with ease; next are those who know through learning and [act] for the benefit…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
行也又次之而困知勉行也所謂性之一者亦
未始不存也孟子曰人之有是四端也猶其有
是四體也厚於仁而薄於義通於禮而寡於智
非不可謂得太極之一體也有而未至焉者具
體而微者也故擴其端則火然泉達之機著推
其極則上際下蟠之化神而要之自主靜始是
靜者又合動靜而一之者也周子作通書曰士
希賢賢希聖聖希天噫至於天則全體之極敷
乎天下矣斯其爲竟太極之蘊者乎
===
表
擬禮部尚書陶凱進宴享九奏樂章表〔洪武四年〕
李維唐
同考試官教諭許批駢儷中寫揄揚之意且典則可
誦錄之以式多士
考試官教諭毛批得當時進樂本意
考試官學正王批體裁雅麗可觀
洪武四年某月某日禮部尚書臣陶凱撰
punctuated:
行也，又次之而困知勉行也，所謂性之一者亦未始不存也。孟子曰：「人之有是四端也，猶其有是四體也。」厚於仁而薄於義，通於禮而寡於智，非不可謂得太極之一體也。有而未至焉者，具體而微者也。故擴其端，則火然泉達之機著；推其極，則上際下蟠之化神。而要之，自主靜始。是靜者，又合動靜而一之者也。周子作《通書》曰：「士希賢，賢希聖，聖希天。」噫！至於天，則全體之極敷乎天下矣。斯其爲竟太極之蘊者乎？

表
擬禮部尚書陶凱進宴享九奏樂章表〔洪武四年〕
李維唐

考試官教諭毛批：得當時進樂本意。
考試官學正王批：體裁雅麗可觀。

洪武四年某月某日，禮部尚書臣陶凱撰
translation_en:
…and put it into practice for its benefits; next come those who attain knowledge through difficulty and practice it through strenuous effort. What is called the unity of human nature has likewise never ceased to be present. Mencius said: “People have these four beginnings just as they have these four limbs.” Those who are strong in benevolence but weak in righteousness, conversant with ritual propriety but deficient in wisdom, may indeed be said to have attained one aspect of the Supreme Ultimate. Those who possess it but have not yet attained its fullness have the whole constitution in miniature. Thus, when these beginnings are expanded, the incipient workings become manifest, like a fire catching or a spring breaking forth; when they are extended to their utmost, the transforming power that reaches above and spreads below becomes numinous. Yet, in essence, this begins with making stillness primary. This stillness, moreover, unites movement and stillness as one. Master Zhou wrote in the Book of Penetration (Tongshu): “The scholar aspires to be a worthy; the worthy aspires to be a sage; the sage aspires to Heaven.” Ah! Once Heaven is attained, the ultimate perfection of the whole constitution extends throughout all under Heaven. Is this what it means to fathom fully the profundities of the Supreme Ultimate?

Memorial
A memorial composed in the role of Tao Kai, Minister of Rites, presenting the musical texts for the nine performances at court banquets. 〔Fourth year of Hongwu [1371]〕
By Li Weitang.

Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: “It captures the original intent behind the presentation of this music at that time.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Its form and style are elegant and beautiful, well worth reading.”
