立萬世論性之宗者也。賢人之學以明道也，有意於立言以命世也。子思之言曰：「天命之謂性。」孟子之言曰：「乃若其情，則可以為善矣，乃所謂善也。」子思懼相近之難名也，故以天命名之；孟子懼相近之易岐也，一以利善決之。然既謂之天命，則流行賦予，理固乘氣而有立矣；既謂之利善，則故利為本，善固與惡而相待矣。《詩》曰：「天生蒸民，有物有則。民之秉彝，好是懿德。」是命也，言乎其生也；利也，言乎其好也。發夫子未發之旨者也。然此皆統理氣、通人物、合內外、一動靜而言，而領惡全好、以變異反同之事，則存乎其人矣。
後世儒者莫不知宗子思、孟軻以師孔子，至其立言則犁然異者，何哉？非必角出以相勝也。學有純駁，而識之偏正隨之矣；造有淺深，而辭之疵粹因之矣。彼莊、荀、董、楊，非不儼然稱通儒也，然工於立言者也。工於立言，則言恒各指
translation_en:
…thereby establishing the guiding principle for discussions of human nature for all ages. The learning of worthy men serves to illuminate the Way; they consciously seek to formulate teachings that will guide their age. Zisi said: “What Heaven decrees is called nature.” Mengzi said: “As for their genuine dispositions, these can become good; this is what I mean by goodness.” Zisi feared that “being close to one another” was difficult to define, so he defined it through Heaven’s decree. Mengzi feared that “being close to one another” could readily give rise to divergent interpretations, so he settled the matter solely in terms of beneficial goodness [?]. Yet once nature is called Heaven’s decree, principle, in its circulation and bestowal, necessarily becomes established by riding upon material force. Once it is called beneficial goodness [?], inherent constitution and benefit are taken as the basis [?], and goodness necessarily stands in relation to evil. The Book of Odes says: “Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; where there are things, there are norms. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this admirable virtue.” This is decree, spoken of in terms of their birth; this is benefit, spoken of in terms of their liking. These statements bring out meanings that the Master had not expressed. Yet all of this is said by treating principle and material force together, encompassing human beings and other things, joining the inner and outer, and unifying activity and stillness. As for governing evil and preserving what is good [?], and returning to sameness through transforming differences, that rests with the individual.
Later Confucian scholars all knew to take Zisi and Meng Ke as their authorities in following Kongzi as their teacher. Why, then, did their formulations of doctrine differ so markedly? It was not necessarily because they sought to outdo one another with competing innovations. Learning may be pure or mixed, and understanding accordingly becomes partial or correct; attainment may be shallow or deep, and expression accordingly becomes flawed or refined. Zhuang, Xun, Dong, and Yang could indeed claim with due dignity to be scholars of comprehensive learning. Yet they were adept at formulating doctrines. Being adept at formulating doctrines, their words invariably each point toward…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其所之故荀子曰性天之就不可以學不
可以事言善惡之限于天成矣而董子則
曰質樸之謂性性非教化不成夫教化以
成其質樸則學問之功固大也何天成之
可限哉莊子曰繕性於俗俗學以求復其
初言復初之必由於繕學矣而楊子則曰
善惡混氣也者所適於善惡之馬也夫善
惡惟氣之所適則繕學之功誠不可廢詎
容任其趨而不之救哉夫四子之言非以
===
相反也所究之旨不同也求其得乎利善
之要歸則莊之復初董之成教近之矣而
就之不可變混之不可分則故非其利而
利失其眞不已謬哉以至周程朱邵非不
褒然稱大儒也然專於講學者也專於講
學則言必各發其所蘊故周子曰剛柔善
惡中而已者莫非性也易其惡至乎中治
性之功也而朱子則曰仁義禮智人性之
綱夫仁義禮智以爲綱則粹然一出於善
punctuated:
其所之。故荀子曰：「性，天之就，不可以學，不可以事。」言善惡之限于天成矣。而董子則曰：「質樸之謂性，性非教化不成。」夫教化以成其質樸，則學問之功固大也，何天成之可限哉？莊子曰：「繕性於俗，俗學以求復其初。」言復初之必由於繕學矣。而楊子則曰：「善惡混。氣也者，所適於善惡之馬也。」夫善惡惟氣之所適，則繕學之功誠不可廢，詎容任其趨而不之救哉？夫四子之言，非以相反也，所究之旨不同也。求其得乎利善之要歸，則莊之復初、董之成教近之矣。而就之不可變、混之不可分，則故非其利，而利失其眞，不已謬哉？

以至周、程、朱、邵，非不褒然稱大儒也，然專於講學者也。專於講學，則言必各發其所蘊。故周子曰：「剛柔善惡中而已者，莫非性也。」易其惡至乎中，治性之功也。而朱子則曰：「仁義禮智，人性之綱。」夫仁義禮智以爲綱，則粹然一出於善。
translation_en:
…the direction each pursues. Thus Xunzi said: “Human nature is what Heaven brings to completion; it cannot be acquired through study or through deliberate effort.” This says that the bounds of good and evil are fixed by what Heaven has completed. Master Dong, however, said: “The unadorned substance is called human nature; without teaching and transformation, human nature is not completed.” If teaching and transformation complete this unadorned substance, then the contribution of learning is certainly great. How could what Heaven has completed set its limits? Zhuangzi said: “Cultivate one’s nature amid worldly customs, through customary learning seeking to recover its original state [?].” This says that recovering the original state must proceed through cultivation and learning. Master Yang, however, said: “Good and evil are mixed. Vital energy is the horse by which one travels toward good or evil.” If movement toward good or evil depends entirely on the direction of vital energy, then the work of cultivation and learning truly cannot be neglected. How could one allow it to follow its course without attempting a remedy? The statements of these four masters were not intended to contradict one another; the points they investigated differed. If we ask which grasped the essential end of promoting goodness [?], Zhuangzi’s recovery of the original state and Master Dong’s completion through teaching came close. But to hold that what has been completed cannot change, or that what is mixed cannot be separated, is surely not beneficial to it; when benefit loses its true meaning [?], is this not gravely mistaken?

As for Zhou, Cheng, Zhu, and Shao, they too were illustriously acclaimed as great Confucian scholars. Yet they specialized in the exposition of learning. In expounding learning, each necessarily expressed the insights he held within. Thus Master Zhou said: “Strength, softness, good, evil, and the mean—these are all aspects of human nature.” To transform its evil and reach the mean is the achievement of ordering one’s nature. Master Zhu, however, said: “Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are the guiding principles of human nature.” If benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constitute its guiding principles, then it proceeds wholly and purely from goodness…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
果何惡之可易也邵子曰性者道之形體
心者性之郛郭莫非性也具乎道涵於心
語性之妙也而程子則曰自內以立本自
外以致用夫合內外以同歸則渾然一統
於性又何形體郛郭之可岐也夫四子之
言非以相勝也所明之理各適其當也求
其合於天命之名義則朱之仁義禮智爲
實體程之已發未發爲中和得之矣而周
之善惡至中邵之道心具體卽天之與人
===
而人之成天豈不益詳哉他如生之謂性
告子之妄君子以爲不可詆矣而飲食男
女生之類也亦以爲性者兼言之也蓋仁
義禮智之粹然者理也知覺運動之蠢然
者氣也人物之生理與氣合而已故天命
之性以理言也然命之自天則二五之精
妙合而凝者矣故謂飲食男女卽性固不
可而謂飲食男女非性生亦不可天下豈
有離氣之理耶惡以名性荀子之謬君子
punctuated:
果何惡之可易也？邵子曰：「性者，道之形體；心者，性之郛郭。」莫非性也，具乎道，涵於心，語性之妙也。而程子則曰：「自內以立本，自外以致用。」夫合內外以同歸，則渾然一統於性，又何形體郛郭之可岐也？夫四子之言，非以相勝也，所明之理各適其當也。求其合於天命之名義，則朱之仁義禮智爲實體，程之已發未發爲中和，得之矣。而周之善惡至中，邵之道心具體，卽天之與人，而人之成天，豈不益詳哉？

他如「生之謂性」，告子之妄，君子以爲不可詆矣。而飲食男女，生之類也，亦以爲性者，兼言之也。蓋仁義禮智之粹然者，理也；知覺運動之蠢然者，氣也。人物之生，理與氣合而已。故天命之性，以理言也。然命之自天，則二五之精，妙合而凝者矣。故謂飲食男女卽性，固不可；而謂飲食男女非性生，亦不可。天下豈有離氣之理耶？惡以名性，荀子之謬，君子
translation_en:
…what evil, then, could there actually be to transform? Master Shao said: “Nature is the embodied form of the Way; the mind is the outer wall of nature.” Nothing here is other than nature: fully present in the Way and contained within the mind—this speaks of nature’s subtlety. Master Cheng, however, said: “From within, establish the foundation; from without, bring its functioning to realization.” If inner and outer are brought together toward the same end, they form an undivided unity in nature. How, then, can embodied form and outer wall be distinguished? The words of these four masters were not intended to prevail over one another; the principle each elucidated was appropriate to its particular concern. If we seek their correspondence with the meaning of “Heaven’s mandate,” Master Zhu’s benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom as the substantive reality, and Master Cheng’s equilibrium and harmony as the states before and after arousal, capture it. Master Zhou’s account of good and evil attaining the mean, and Master Shao’s account of the Way and mind embodying nature, concern precisely what Heaven gives to human beings and how human beings fulfill Heaven’s work. Do these not make the account still more detailed?

Take another example: “What is inborn is called nature.” This is Gaozi’s error, which gentlemen consider impossible to criticize [?]. Yet eating, drinking, and relations between men and women belong to the activities of life; when these too are considered nature, the term is being used inclusively. For the purity of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is principle; the stirring activity of perception and movement is material force. The coming into being of human beings and other creatures is simply the conjunction of principle and material force. Thus, the nature conferred by Heaven’s mandate is spoken of in terms of principle. Yet what Heaven confers consists of the essences of the two forces and the five phases, which unite wondrously and congeal. Thus, to say that eating, drinking, and relations between men and women are themselves nature is certainly inadmissible; but to say that they do not arise from nature [?] is also inadmissible. Could there be any principle in the world detached from material force? To designate nature as evil is Xunzi’s error; gentlemen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以爲不足辨矣而强梁邪佞惡之類也亦
以爲性者析言之也蓋直義順慈之得中
者本有之善也剛惡柔惡之失中者戾氣
之所生也人之所禀氣與理俱而已故純
粹至善以理言也然受之自人則形生神
發五性七情出焉故謂性爲惡固不可而
謂惡不出於性亦不可天下豈有離理之
氣耶是故論性不論氣不備論氣不論性
不明二之則不是矣然此特其是非之較
===
然者不有動靜寂感之機内外通一之奧
者乎吾心者虛靈不昧之體也情者應感
起物之用也彼以性之動爲情情固性之
所由以順應者矣而又以性之動爲心則
心豈性之所由以主宰者乎性有定理而
心無定鄉如心不能主宰乎性則應事感
物性又何緣心而動也是知心也者太虛
湛一之真也性則其生生之理情則其感
應之神理故一神故化莫不統於吾心故
punctuated:
以爲不足辨矣。而强梁邪佞，惡之類也，亦以爲性者，析言之也。蓋直義順慈之得中者，本有之善也；剛惡柔惡之失中者，戾氣之所生也。人之所禀，氣與理俱而已，故純粹至善，以理言也。然受之自人，則形生神發，五性七情出焉。故謂性爲惡，固不可；而謂惡不出於性，亦不可。天下豈有離理之氣耶？是故，論性不論氣，不備；論氣不論性，不明；二之則不是矣。然此特其是非之較然者，不有動靜寂感之機、内外通一之奧者乎？

吾心者，虛靈不昧之體也；情者，應感起物之用也。彼以性之動爲情，情固性之所由以順應者矣；而又以性之動爲心，則心豈性之所由以主宰者乎？性有定理，而心無定鄉。如心不能主宰乎性，則應事感物，性又何緣心而動也？是知心也者，太虛湛一之真也；性則其生生之理，情則其感應之神。理故一，神故化，莫不統於吾心，故
translation_en:
…consider it unworthy of debate. Yet overbearing violence, perversity, and flattery belong to the category of evil; to regard these too as nature is to speak of nature by distinguishing its aspects. Uprightness, righteousness, compliance, and kindness, when they attain due measure, are the goodness originally possessed; the evils of hardness and softness, when they lose due measure, arise from aberrant material force (qi). What human beings are endowed with comprises material force together with principle (li), and nothing more. Thus, to speak of nature as pure and supremely good is to speak in terms of principle. Yet as received by human beings, bodily form comes into being and spirit becomes active, and the five constant virtues of nature and the seven emotions emerge. Hence, although it is certainly unacceptable to call nature evil, it is also unacceptable to say that evil does not emerge from nature. How could there be material force anywhere under Heaven apart from principle? Thus, to discuss nature without discussing material force is incomplete; to discuss material force without discussing nature is unclear; to treat them as two separate things is incorrect. Yet these are merely the points on which right and wrong are evident. Are there not also the subtle workings of movement and stillness, quiescence and responsiveness, and the mystery of the unity that joins inner and outer?

Our mind is an inherently empty, numinous, and undimmed substance; the emotions are its functioning in responding to stimuli and arising in relation to things [?]. That thinker takes the movement of nature to be emotion. Emotion is indeed that through which nature responds appropriately. But if he also takes the movement of nature to be mind, how could mind then be that through which nature exercises mastery? Nature has a fixed principle, whereas mind has no fixed abode. If mind cannot exercise mastery over nature, then, in responding to affairs and being affected by things, how could nature move through mind? From this we know that mind is the true reality of the Great Void, lucid and undivided. Nature is its principle of ceaseless generation, while emotion is its numinous capacity for responding to stimuli. As principle, it is one; as numinous efficacy, it transforms. Nothing falls outside the unifying governance of our mind. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
曰心統性情未失也夫性本吾心之生理
而非塊然者也萬事萬化皆吾性之所自
出非外至者也彼以感物而動為欲則未
感之先渾然在中無欲可知又以不能無
感為性則應感在物本然不離非性而何
蓋性有定體而感無定時使性非至靜以
涵乎所感之理則憧憧往來感又何緣性
而順也是知性也喜怒哀樂未發之中也
感則因物而動欲則緣動以生其本則寂
===
然而已故曰至靜無感未失也此動靜寂
感之微通一無二之理而繼之善成之性
命之天而利之自人旨益密矣執事復疑
之曰主相近而言則渾淪而似於善惡之
混而不知相近之中固自有純粹至精者
存何疑於混也曰主天命而言則太廣而
同乎人物之生而不知天之所命固自有
各一其性者在何嫌於同也又曰主利善
而言則太峻而遺乎氣質之稟而不知故
punctuated:
曰：「心統性情」，未失也。夫性本吾心之生理，而非塊然者也。萬事萬化，皆吾性之所自出，非外至者也。彼以感物而動為欲，則未感之先，渾然在中，無欲可知；又以不能無感為性，則應感在物，本然不離，非性而何？蓋性有定體，而感無定時。使性非至靜以涵乎所感之理，則憧憧往來，感又何緣性而順也？是知性也，喜怒哀樂未發之中也；感則因物而動，欲則緣動以生，其本則寂然而已。故曰：「至靜無感」，未失也。此動靜寂感之微，通一無二之理，而繼之善、成之性，命之天而利之自人，旨益密矣。
執事復疑之曰：「主相近而言，則渾淪而似於善惡之混。」而不知相近之中，固自有純粹至精者存，何疑於混也？曰：「主天命而言，則太廣而同乎人物之生。」而不知天之所命，固自有各一其性者在，何嫌於同也？又曰：「主利善而言，則太峻而遺乎氣質之稟。」而不知故
translation_en:
…to say, “The mind governs human nature and the feelings,” is not mistaken. Human nature is fundamentally the life-generating principle of our minds, not an inert lump. All affairs and transformations issue from our nature; they do not arrive from outside. He takes being stirred by contact with things to be desire. Before such contact, then, everything lies undifferentiated within, and we may know that there is no desire. He also takes the inability to remain without response to be human nature. If, in responding to things, one never departs from what is inherently so, what could this be but human nature? Nature has a settled constitution, but responses have no fixed time. If nature were not supremely still, containing the principles of whatever it responds to, then amid restless comings and goings, how could response follow nature and proceed harmoniously? Thus we know that nature is the equilibrium before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise. Response is movement occasioned by things, and desire arises in consequence of that movement; their foundation is simply stillness. Hence to say, “Supremely still and without response,” is not mistaken. Such are the subtleties of movement and stillness, quiescence and response: a principle that is wholly one, without duality. What continues it is goodness; what completes it is nature. Heaven ordains it, while its beneficial operation proceeds from human beings. The meaning becomes still more exact.
You, sir, further question this, saying: “To speak primarily in terms of the closeness of human natures leaves them undifferentiated and seems to mingle good and evil.” Yet you do not recognize that within this closeness there inherently exists something pure and supremely refined. Why suspect any mingling? You say: “To speak primarily in terms of Heaven’s mandate is too broad, treating the birth of humans and other creatures alike.” Yet you do not recognize that what Heaven ordains inherently allows each to have its own distinct nature. Why object to their being treated alike? You further say: “To speak primarily in terms of benefit and goodness sets the standard too high and leaves out the endowment of material force and physical constitution.” Yet you do not recognize that what is inherently so…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
者以利爲本人物各循其性之自然是其
知覺之所之也又何遺於氣質也是故相
近之㫖萬世性學之宗其渾然者也子思
孟軻發夫子未發之蘊其粹然者也莊荀
諸儒求工於言而不求工於理故多疵而
寡醇有宋諸儒求工於理而不求工於言
故大醇而小疵若周之成性程之定性朱
之理性張之存性則根極要領而獨得其
宗後有作者雖百世不能易其言矣雖然
===
語焉而必詳擇焉而必精此固學者事也
然詳焉而莫之存精焉而莫之盡卒歸於
習讀談聽而已者何益哉善夫程子之言
曰性猶山也自聖人以至於庶人登山者
也或蹈其半或止其下其强力者出入上
下無所不至無所不至者聖人也或蹈其
半或止其下斯賢否之别與蓋能盡其性
則氣命于理無所不至之聖人由此也不
能盡其性則理命於氣蹈半止下爲賢爲
punctuated:
者以利爲本，人物各循其性之自然，是其知覺之所之也，又何遺於氣質也？是故相近之㫖，萬世性學之宗，其渾然者也。子思、孟軻發夫子未發之蘊，其粹然者也。莊、荀諸儒求工於言，而不求工於理，故多疵而寡醇；有宋諸儒求工於理，而不求工於言，故大醇而小疵。若周之成性、程之定性、朱之理性、張之存性，則根極要領，而獨得其宗。後有作者，雖百世不能易其言矣。

雖然，語焉而必詳，擇焉而必精，此固學者事也。然詳焉而莫之存，精焉而莫之盡，卒歸於習讀談聽而已者，何益哉？善夫程子之言，曰：「性猶山也，自聖人以至於庶人，登山者也。或蹈其半，或止其下，其强力者出入上下，無所不至。無所不至者，聖人也。或蹈其半，或止其下，斯賢否之别與！」蓋能盡其性，則氣命于理，無所不至之聖人由此也；不能盡其性，則理命於氣，蹈半止下，爲賢爲
translation_en:
…take smooth, unimpeded functioning as their basis. People and other beings each follow the spontaneous course of their nature; this is the direction in which their awareness moves. How, then, does this neglect their material endowment? Thus, the teaching that human natures are close to one another is the guiding principle of the study of nature for all ages: it presents nature in its undivided wholeness. Zisi and Meng Ke brought out implications that the Master had not articulated: they presented nature in its purity. Zhuang, Xun, and other scholars sought refinement in words rather than in principle, and thus had many flaws and little purity. The scholars of the Song sought refinement in principle rather than in words, and thus were largely pure, with only minor flaws. As for Zhou’s teaching on completing one’s nature, Cheng’s on stabilizing one’s nature, Zhu’s on nature as principle, and Zhang’s on preserving one’s nature, they penetrated to the roots of the essentials and uniquely grasped the governing principle. Even a hundred generations hence, later authors will be unable to alter their words.

Nevertheless, to discuss this with thoroughness and to discriminate with precision is certainly the scholar’s task. But if one is thorough without preserving what one understands, and precise without fully realizing it, ultimately doing no more than repeatedly reading, talking, and listening, what benefit is there? Well did Master Cheng say: “Nature is like a mountain. From sages down to ordinary people, all are climbers of that mountain. Some reach halfway; some stop at its foot. Those who exert themselves vigorously travel in and out, up and down, leaving nowhere unreached. Those who leave nowhere unreached are sages. Some reach halfway, while others stop at the foot: is this not the distinction between the worthy and the unworthy?” For when one can fully realize one’s nature, material force is governed by principle; this is how one becomes a sage who leaves nowhere unreached. When one cannot fully realize one’s nature, principle is governed by material force; reaching halfway or stopping at the foot, becoming worthy or becoming …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不肖者由此也故學者之於性不貴於知
而貴於盡也天下之物未有逃於吾性之
表而吾性盡天下之能事者也故自其取
諸內以立本也爲聖人之神大而至於參
天地廣而至於賛化育極天下之高明而
寂然不動以待萬物之至者非天下之大
本乎自其取諸外以致用也爲王者之事
凡觀變以應天下之動利用以成天下之
務鼓衆宜民與一世同患無所感而不通
===
盛德大業待之以立者非天下之達道乎
本乎天而成乎人動於無爲而著於有形
此所謂天下之物未有逃於吾性之表而
吾性盡天下之能事者矣故曰一言而盡
天下之道者性也一言而盡天下之性者
理也合內外之道也張子曰形而後有氣
質之性善反之則天地之性存焉天地之
性存則天下之能事畢矣此未必非執事
策愚生意也敢以敬復
punctuated: 不肖者由此也。故學者之於性，不貴於知而貴於盡也。天下之物，未有逃於吾性之表，而吾性盡天下之能事者也。故自其取諸內以立本也，爲聖人之神，大而至於參天地，廣而至於賛化育，極天下之高明，而寂然不動以待萬物之至者，非天下之大本乎？自其取諸外以致用也，爲王者之事，凡觀變以應天下之動，利用以成天下之務，鼓衆宜民，與一世同患，無所感而不通，盛德大業待之以立者，非天下之達道乎？本乎天而成乎人，動於無爲而著於有形，此所謂天下之物未有逃於吾性之表，而吾性盡天下之能事者矣。故曰：「一言而盡天下之道者，性也；一言而盡天下之性者，理也。」合內外之道也。張子曰：「形而後有氣質之性，善反之，則天地之性存焉。」天地之性存，則天下之能事畢矣。此未必非執事策愚生意也，敢以敬復。
translation_en: …or unworthy arises from this. Thus, for those who study human nature, what matters is not knowing it but fully realizing it. Nothing in the world lies outside my nature, and my nature embraces all that can be accomplished in the world. Drawing upon what is within to establish the foundation constitutes the sage’s spiritual efficacy: so great as to form a triad with Heaven and Earth, so broad as to assist their transforming and nourishing work, reaching the utmost loftiness and clarity in the world, yet remaining still and unmoving while awaiting the arrival of all things. Is this not the great foundation of the world? Drawing upon what is outside to bring it into practical operation constitutes the work of a true king: observing changes to respond to the world’s movements, making things useful to accomplish the world’s tasks, inspiring the multitude and benefiting the people, sharing the troubles of an entire age, and responding without obstruction to every stimulus. Since flourishing virtue and great achievements depend upon this for their establishment, is it not the universally operative Way of the world? Rooted in Heaven and completed in humanity, moving through nonaction and manifesting in tangible forms: this is what is meant by saying that nothing in the world lies outside my nature, and that my nature embraces all that can be accomplished in the world. Thus it is said: “The single word that encompasses the Way of the world is ‘nature’; the single word that encompasses all nature in the world is ‘principle.’” This is the Way that unites the internal and the external. Master Zhang said: “Only after bodily form comes into being is there a nature conditioned by material endowment. If one is adept at returning to the source, the nature of Heaven and Earth is preserved.” When the nature of Heaven and Earth is preserved, all that can be accomplished in the world is fulfilled. This may indeed be your intention, honored examiner, in putting this policy question to your humble student. I venture to offer this respectful reply.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第三問
李維唐
同考試官教諭許批姓氏之學不講已久子獨能言
其詳必究心而有得者
考試官教諭毛批歷歷有據非苟作者
考試官學正王批有醖藉有發揮
嘗聞聖人之立教也别生分類雖以勵天
下之善而立賢無方未嘗阻夫人之進何
也吾於氏族之法而知之矣昔者聖人爲
===
姓氏之别而公卿士庶其源流燦然以辨
所以勸誘世胄之自立能克紹其家聲使
國有世臣鄉有世族所以勵天下之善也
而其官人也則唯其賢而已苟賢矣雖賤
必舉非賢雖世胄弗庸其不阻人之進也
如此視後世之崇廕籍而遺寒素相沿以
爲選舉使利孔數出流弊滋多者固不可
同年而語也知乎此而姓氏之說可得而
言矣執事發策以姓氏爲問豈不以草茅
punctuated:
第三問
李維唐
同考試官教諭許批：姓氏之學不講已久，子獨能言其詳，必究心而有得者。
考試官教諭毛批：歷歷有據，非苟作者。
考試官學正王批：有醖藉，有發揮。
嘗聞聖人之立教也，别生分類，雖以勵天下之善，而立賢無方，未嘗阻夫人之進，何也？吾於氏族之法而知之矣。昔者聖人爲姓氏之别，而公卿士庶，其源流燦然以辨，所以勸誘世胄之自立，能克紹其家聲，使國有世臣，鄉有世族，所以勵天下之善也。而其官人也，則唯其賢而已。苟賢矣，雖賤必舉；非賢，雖世胄弗庸。其不阻人之進也如此。視後世之崇廕籍而遺寒素，相沿以爲選舉，使利孔數出，流弊滋多者，固不可同年而語也。知乎此，而姓氏之說可得而言矣。執事發策，以姓氏爲問，豈不以草茅
translation_en:
Third Policy Question
Li Weitang
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The study of surnames and clan names has long been neglected. You alone can discuss it in detail; surely you have devoted careful thought to it and gained understanding.”
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Every point has clear supporting evidence. This is no carelessly composed work.”
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: “It has depth and restraint, as well as elaboration.”
I have heard that when the sages established their teachings, they distinguished people by birth and classified them by category. Although this was intended to encourage goodness throughout the realm, they appointed the worthy without restriction and never obstructed anyone’s advancement. Why was this? I have come to understand it through the rules governing clans and lineages. In antiquity, the sages established distinctions between surnames and clan names, so that the origins and lines of descent of dukes, ministers, gentlemen, and commoners were clearly differentiated. This encouraged descendants of hereditary houses to establish themselves and carry on their families’ good names, so that the state would have hereditary ministerial families and local communities would have established lineages. This was how they encouraged goodness throughout the realm. Yet when appointing people to office, they considered only their worthiness. If someone was worthy, even if of humble status, he would certainly be recommended; if unworthy, even a descendant of a hereditary house would not be employed. Such was their refusal to obstruct people’s advancement. This certainly cannot be spoken of in the same breath as later ages, when ancestral privilege was exalted and men of humble, unadorned backgrounds were neglected. Such practices were perpetuated as the method of selecting officials, causing avenues for private gain to multiply and attendant abuses to increase. Once this is understood, surnames and clan names can be discussed. You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question asking about surnames and clan names. Is this not because you believe that among those living in rustic obscurity…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之中亦有肉譜如李守素者乎而愚非其
人也嘗聞其槩矣春秋傳曰天子因生以
賜姓胙之土而命之氏諸侯以字爲謚因
以爲族官有世功則有公族邑亦如之則
惟天子得以賜姓命氏諸侯則有命氏而
無賜姓傳曰黃帝之子二十五人得姓者
十有四人所謂姓也范宣子曰匄之祖在
周爲唐杜氏晉主夏盟爲范氏所謂氏也
姓者統其祖考之所自出者也百世而不
===
===
變者也氏者別其子孫之所自分者也數
世而一變者也別姓則爲氏如有扈氏斟
尋氏皆同出於姒姓者也別氏則爲族如
十六族皆同出於高陽高辛氏者也天子
因生以賜姓其得姓雖一而子孫別而爲
氏者不勝其多焉或氏於國則齊魯蔡吳
之類是也氏於謚則文武成宣之類是也
氏於官則司馬司徒之類是也氏於爵則
王孫公孫之類是也氏於事則巫乙匠陶
punctuated: 之中亦有肉譜如李守素者乎？而愚非其人也。嘗聞其槩矣。《春秋傳》曰：「天子因生以賜姓，胙之土而命之氏。諸侯以字爲謚，因以爲族。官有世功，則有公族，邑亦如之。」則惟天子得以賜姓命氏，諸侯則有命氏而無賜姓。傳曰：「黃帝之子二十五人，得姓者十有四人。」所謂姓也。范宣子曰：「匄之祖，在周爲唐杜氏；晉主夏盟，爲范氏。」所謂氏也。姓者，統其祖考之所自出者也，百世而不變者也。氏者，別其子孫之所自分者也，數世而一變者也。別姓則爲氏，如有扈氏、斟尋氏，皆同出於姒姓者也。別氏則爲族，如十六族，皆同出於高陽、高辛氏者也。天子因生以賜姓，其得姓雖一，而子孫別而爲氏者，不勝其多焉。或氏於國，則齊、魯、蔡、吳之類是也；氏於謚，則文、武、成、宣之類是也；氏於官，則司馬、司徒之類是也；氏於爵，則王孫、公孫之類是也；氏於事，則巫乙匠陶
translation_en:
…among those living in obscurity there might also be someone like Li Shousu, a living repository of genealogies? But I am not such a person. I have, however, heard the general outlines of the subject. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “The Son of Heaven bestows a surname according to birth, grants land, and assigns a clan name. The feudal lords use a courtesy name as a posthumous name and thereby establish a lineage. When an officeholder has rendered meritorious service over successive generations, there is a lineage recognized by the lord; the same applies to a fief.” Thus only the Son of Heaven may bestow surnames and assign clan names; feudal lords may assign clan names but may not bestow surnames. The Commentary says: “Of the Yellow Emperor’s twenty-five sons, fourteen received surnames.” This is what is meant by a surname (xing). Fan Xuanzi said: “My ancestors—those of Gai—were the Tang and Du clans under the Zhou; when Jin presided over the alliance of the Xia states, they became the Fan clan.” This is what is meant by a clan name (shi).

A surname unites those descended from a common ancestral source and remains unchanged for a hundred generations. A clan name distinguishes the branches into which descendants divide and changes every few generations. A branch of a surname becomes a clan: the Youhu and Zhenxun clans, for example, both sprang from the Si surname. A branch of a clan becomes a lineage (zu): the sixteen lineages, for example, all sprang from the Gaoyang and Gaoxin clans. The Son of Heaven bestows surnames according to birth. Although the surname received may be one and the same, the clans into which the descendants branch are innumerable. Some take their clan names from states, such as Qi, Lu, Cai, and Wu; others from posthumous names, such as Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Xuan; others from offices, such as Sima (Minister of War) and Situ (Minister of Education); others from noble rank, such as Wangsun (royal grandson) and Gongsun (ducal grandson); and others from occupations, such as Wu, Yi, Jiang, and Tao [“shaman,” unclear, “craftsman,” and “potter”; the grouping is doubtful]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之類是也姓以別婚姻故百世而婚姻不
通氏以辨貴賤則公卿大夫士庶之族易
辨而可攷其所由來者尚矣三代而上有
賜姓命氏之繁自秦而下則直以氏爲姓
世守一氏傳千萬年而不變執事謂古者
枝分縷析若叅錯而難考而反易知後代
守一不變固甚簡易而人罕能辨其源者
愚聞之呂伯恭矣在譜牒之明與廢而已
夫譜牒之明與廢不獨民間爲然也周人
===
小史掌邦國之志奠繫世辨昭穆蓋專官
以掌其事而後世則未聞有專掌矣且氏
族之不辨不特譜牒爲然也古者有大宗
小宗之法宗法立則姓氏益明二者寔相
維繫而後世則宗法之廢久矣譜牒不明
宗法不立而欲姓氏之辨得哉矧其中又
有以去國而改如范蠡者有以避禍而改
如智果者以避仇而改如張祿者以賜姓
而改如婁敬者以吹律而改如京房者以
punctuated: 之類是也。姓以別婚姻，故百世而婚姻不通；氏以辨貴賤，則公卿大夫士庶之族易辨，而可攷其所由來者尚矣。三代而上，有賜姓命氏之繁；自秦而下，則直以氏爲姓，世守一氏，傳千萬年而不變。執事謂古者枝分縷析，若叅錯而難考，而反易知；後代守一不變，固甚簡易，而人罕能辨其源者，愚聞之呂伯恭矣：在譜牒之明與廢而已。夫譜牒之明與廢，不獨民間爲然也。周人小史掌邦國之志，奠繫世，辨昭穆，蓋專官以掌其事，而後世則未聞有專掌矣。且氏族之不辨，不特譜牒爲然也。古者有大宗小宗之法，宗法立則姓氏益明，二者寔相維繫，而後世則宗法之廢久矣。譜牒不明，宗法不立，而欲姓氏之辨，得哉？矧其中又有以去國而改，如范蠡者；有以避禍而改，如智果者；以避仇而改，如張祿者；以賜姓而改，如婁敬者；以吹律而改，如京房者；以
translation_en:
…are examples of this kind. Ancestral surnames (xing) distinguish those eligible for marriage: even after a hundred generations, people sharing one cannot intermarry. Lineage names (shi) distinguish noble from humble, making the lineages of dukes, ministers, great officers, gentlemen, and commoners readily distinguishable; the practice of tracing their origins is ancient. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, surnames were bestowed and lineage names assigned in great profusion. From the Qin onward, however, lineage names were simply treated as surnames. Each family preserved a single lineage name through successive generations, transmitting it unchanged for thousands upon thousands of years. You observe that in antiquity the branches divided and subdivided, seemingly intermingled and difficult to investigate, yet were actually easy to trace; in later ages, people retained a single name unchanged, a very simple arrangement, yet few could distinguish its origins. I have learned the explanation from Lü Bogong: it lies solely in whether genealogical records are kept clear or allowed to lapse.

The maintenance or neglect of genealogical records is not merely a matter concerning private families. Under the Zhou, the Minor Scribe kept the records of the states, established genealogical successions, and distinguished the zhao and mu generational ranks. Thus a designated official was responsible for this work, whereas in later ages we hear of no official specifically charged with it. Moreover, the inability to distinguish lineages is not attributable to genealogical records alone. In antiquity there were rules governing the major and minor lineage branches. When the lineage system was established, ancestral surnames and lineage names became all the clearer: the two indeed sustained one another. In later ages, however, the lineage system has long been abandoned. With genealogical records unclear and the lineage system unestablished, can one expect ancestral surnames and lineage names to remain distinguishable?

Furthermore, among these people were those who changed their names upon leaving their state, such as Fan Li; those who changed them to escape calamity, such as Zhi Guo; those who changed them to evade enemies, such as Zhang Lu; those who changed them upon receiving an imperially bestowed surname, such as Lou Jing; those who changed them because of blowing pitch pipes, such as Jing Fang; and those who, because of…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
避難而改如束晳者以被嘲而改如氏儀
者以筮易而改如陸羽者而張孟之灌鄭
注之鄭知遠之劉敬瑭之石依附假托變
更淆亂而欲源流之燦然可攷亦難矣若
賈弼摯虞何承天之所撰許敬宗韋述路
敬淳之所錄其意主於矜誇門第崇尚廕
籍吾不知其於姓氏之學果有所發明否
也執事又舉唐柳芳所論謂漢高帝興徒
步始尚官魏氏立九品始尚姓又謂山東
===
之人尚婚姻江右之人尚人物關中之人
尚冠冕代北之人尚貴戚有若是其不同
者愚甞聞芳之言曰山東之人質故尚婚
姻其信可與也江右之人文故尚人物其
智可與也關中之人雄故尚冠冕其達可
與也代北之人武故尚貴戚其泰可與也
此所尚之得也又曰尚婚姻者先外族後
本宗尚人物者進庶孽退嫡長尚冠冕者
略伉儷慕容華尚貴戚者徇勢利忘禮教
punctuated:
避難而改，如束晳者；以被嘲而改，如氏儀者；以筮易而改，如陸羽者。而張孟之灌、鄭注之鄭、知遠之劉、敬瑭之石，依附假托，變更淆亂，而欲源流之燦然可攷，亦難矣。若賈弼、摯虞、何承天之所撰，許敬宗、韋述、路敬淳之所錄，其意主於矜誇門第，崇尚廕籍，吾不知其於姓氏之學果有所發明否也。
執事又舉唐柳芳所論，謂漢高帝興徒步，始尚官；魏氏立九品，始尚姓。又謂山東之人尚婚姻，江右之人尚人物，關中之人尚冠冕，代北之人尚貴戚，有若是其不同者。愚甞聞芳之言曰：「山東之人質，故尚婚姻，其信可與也；江右之人文，故尚人物，其智可與也；關中之人雄，故尚冠冕，其達可與也；代北之人武，故尚貴戚，其泰可與也。」此所尚之得也。又曰：「尚婚姻者，先外族，後本宗；尚人物者，進庶孽，退嫡長；尚冠冕者，略伉儷，慕容華；尚貴戚者，徇勢利，忘禮教。」
translation_en:
…who changed their surname to escape danger, like Shu Xi; those who changed it after being mocked, like Shi Yi; and those who changed it through divination with the Book of Changes, like Lu Yu. As for the surname Guan of Zhang Meng, Zheng of Zheng Zhu, Liu of Zhiyuan, and Shi of Jingtang, affiliations and falsely claimed connections brought changes and confusion. To expect the origins and subsequent lines of descent to remain clearly traceable is indeed difficult. As for the works compiled by Jia Bi, Zhi Yu, and He Chengtian, and the records made by Xu Jingzong, Wei Shu, and Lu Jingchun, their principal aim was to vaunt distinguished lineages and exalt hereditary privilege. I do not know whether they actually shed any light on the study of surnames.
You also cite the discussion by Liu Fang of the Tang, who said that when Emperor Gao of the Han rose from the ranks of commoners, people began to esteem official position; when the Wei ruling house established the Nine Ranks, people began to esteem surnames. He further said that people in Shandong esteemed marriage alliances, those in Jiangyou esteemed personal distinction, those in Guanzhong esteemed official rank, and those in Daibei esteemed imperial relatives. Such were the differences among them. I have heard these words of Liu Fang: “The people of Shandong are plain and sincere, and therefore esteem marriage alliances; their trustworthiness deserves approval. The people of Jiangyou are cultivated, and therefore esteem personal distinction; their intelligence deserves approval. The people of Guanzhong are forceful, and therefore esteem official rank; their worldly understanding deserves approval. The people of Daibei are martial, and therefore esteem imperial relatives; their self-assurance deserves approval.” These are the merits of what they esteem. He also said: “Those who esteem marriage alliances put relatives through marriage before their own lineage; those who esteem personal distinction advance sons of concubines and set back the eldest sons of principal wives; those who esteem official rank slight their spouses and admire outward splendor; those who esteem imperial relatives pursue power and profit and forget the teachings of ritual propriety.”…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則所尚之弊也夫此數弊者蓋有所由來
矣自曹魏立中正九品之次上品無寒門
下品無世族而齊宋亦因以取士北齊之
制非四姓不得選舉故士之假托媒衒習
以成風賣婚鬻譜流弊滋甚逮及唐世而
其弊猶存以是較之則不如漢世尚官者
之得也嗟夫古之官人者明揚側陋未嘗
論其世也而魏氏之法不論其材而論其
世矣古之別氏族也欲使朝有世臣鄉有
===
世族故公卿之子孫降在皂隸則恥之所
以進人於善也後世之別氏族也則寒素
不得舉側陋不得揚雖懷才抱德者無由
進矣不免阻人之善也其得失遠矣夫王
滿連姻實駭物聽有如沈約之所糾者豈
論婚姻哉事去名存比之鐵步有如柳子
厚所譏者豈論冠冕哉李陵生降隤其家
聲隴西之士羞言李氏豈論人物哉弭仲
叔高德美名命世之才張伯英以為非弭
punctuated: 則所尚之弊也。夫此數弊者，蓋有所由來矣。自曹魏立中正九品之次，上品無寒門，下品無世族，而齊宋亦因以取士。北齊之制，非四姓不得選舉，故士之假托媒衒，習以成風，賣婚鬻譜，流弊滋甚。逮及唐世，而其弊猶存。以是較之，則不如漢世尚官者之得也。嗟夫！古之官人者，明揚側陋，未嘗論其世也；而魏氏之法，不論其材，而論其世矣。古之別氏族也，欲使朝有世臣，鄉有世族，故公卿之子孫降在皂隸則恥之，所以進人於善也。後世之別氏族也，則寒素不得舉，側陋不得揚，雖懷才抱德者無由進矣，不免阻人之善也。其得失遠矣！夫王滿連姻，實駭物聽，有如沈約之所糾者，豈論婚姻哉？事去名存，比之鐵步，有如柳子厚所譏者，豈論冠冕哉？李陵生降，隤其家聲，隴西之士羞言李氏，豈論人物哉？弭仲叔高德美名，命世之才，張伯英以為非弭
translation_en:
…these, then, are the abuses arising from what they esteem. These several abuses have their origins. After Cao Wei established the nine grades administered by Rectifiers, no men from humble families occupied the upper grades, and no men from hereditary elite families occupied the lower grades. The Qi and Song dynasties likewise followed this method in recruiting officials. Under the Northern Qi system, those outside the four surnames were ineligible for selection. Thus scholars habitually claimed false affiliations and used intermediaries to advertise themselves, until these practices became customary. Selling marriage connections and peddling genealogies produced ever greater abuses. Even in the Tang, these abuses persisted. Judged against these practices, the Han preference for official standing was more sound.

Alas! Those who appointed officials in antiquity sought out and promoted men of humble and obscure station, without considering their ancestry. The Wei system, however, considered ancestry rather than talent. In antiquity, distinctions among lineages were intended to ensure that the court had families serving it for generations and that local communities had established lineages. Thus, it was considered shameful for the descendants of dukes and ministers to sink to the status of menial servants: this encouraged people toward goodness. Later distinctions among lineages, however, prevented men of humble origins from being recommended and men of obscure station from being promoted. Even those possessing talent and virtue had no means of advancement. Such distinctions inevitably obstructed people’s pursuit of goodness. How far apart were the merits of the former and the failings of the latter!

The marriage alliance between the Wang and Man families profoundly shocked those who heard of it, as in the case censured by Shen Yue. How could marriage connections be the criterion? When the substance has vanished but the name remains, it is likened to an “iron step” [?], as in the case ridiculed by Liu Zihou. How could the cap and robes of office be the criterion? Li Ling surrendered alive and brought down his family’s reputation, so that men of Longxi were ashamed to mention the Li surname. How could distinguished individuals be the criterion? Mi Zhongshu possessed lofty virtue, an excellent reputation, and talent such as appears once in an age; yet Zhang Boying considered him someone whom the Mi …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
氏小族所宜有新豐瘠土所宜出豈論貴
戚哉士之自立亦何必以世系爲重乎
國初編脩吳沉之進千家姓也其言曰使天
下之人有以知
聖朝土地廣大人民衆盛
恩德深厚而思各保其族於悠久以同躋仁壽
之鄉也無前代矜誇之失而有維世翼教
之助其言得之矣今姓氏之學日廢其敝
也使世數莫攷源流不知不可以莫之究
===
也唯師隆古三代之意使譜牒詳明族類
有稽如呂伯恭所言立大宗小宗之法使
朝有世臣人知重本如程子張子所論二
者交相維繫藉是以爲尊祖睦族勵世興
行之具如成周九兩之法所謂以族得民
者而黜魏晉矜誇媒衒偏重矯冒之失則
善矣執事又謂滇中士族固中國之流裔
而欲多士之論其世與其所尚夫自莊蹻
略地唐蒙遣使而華人之錯居于滇者始
punctuated:
氏小族所宜有、新豐瘠土所宜出，豈論貴戚哉？士之自立，亦何必以世系爲重乎？

國初編脩吳沉之進《千家姓》也，其言曰：「使天下之人有以知聖朝土地廣大、人民衆盛、恩德深厚，而思各保其族於悠久，以同躋仁壽之鄉也。」無前代矜誇之失，而有維世翼教之助，其言得之矣。今姓氏之學日廢，其敝也，使世數莫攷、源流不知，不可以莫之究也。唯師隆古三代之意，使譜牒詳明、族類有稽，如呂伯恭所言；立大宗、小宗之法，使朝有世臣、人知重本，如程子、張子所論。二者交相維繫，藉是以爲尊祖睦族、勵世興行之具，如成周九兩之法所謂以族得民者，而黜魏晉矜誇媒衒、偏重矯冒之失，則善矣。

執事又謂滇中士族固中國之流裔，而欲多士之論其世與其所尚。夫自莊蹻略地、唐蒙遣使，而華人之錯居于滇者始
translation_en:
…a person whom the humble Mi clan should possess or whom the barren soil of Xinfeng should produce—how could this be a matter of noble kinship? In establishing himself, why must a scholar place such weight on his lineage?

When Wu Chen, a Hanlin Academy Compiler at the beginning of our dynasty, presented the Surnames of a Thousand Families (Qianjia xing), he said: “Let the people throughout the realm recognize the vast territory, abundant population, and profound benevolence of our sagely dynasty, and resolve each to preserve their lineage far into the future, so that all may together attain a realm of benevolence and longevity.” His words avoided the boastfulness of earlier ages and helped sustain society and support moral teaching. They expressed the matter well. Today, the study of surnames is increasingly neglected. The resulting harm is that the succession of generations cannot be traced and the origins and branches of lineages remain unknown. This cannot be left unexamined. We should take as our model the intent of the Three Dynasties of high antiquity, making genealogies clear and detailed and kinship groups verifiable, as Lü Bogong advocated. We should establish the institutions of the greater and lesser descent lines, so that the court has families serving it across generations and people understand the importance of their roots, as Masters Cheng and Zhang discussed. These two measures would sustain one another, providing means to honor ancestors, foster harmony within lineages, encourage society, and promote virtuous conduct. This would resemble what the nine bonds of the Zhou dynasty called “binding the people through kinship.” If we also rejected the faults of the Wei and Jin periods—the boasting and self-advertisement, excessive emphasis on pedigree, and fraudulent claims to ancestry—then all would be well.

You further state that the scholarly lineages of Dian are indeed descendants of people from the Central Lands, and ask the assembled candidates to discuss their ancestry and what they esteem. Now, with Zhuang Qiao’s conquest of territory and Tang Meng’s mission, the interspersed settlement of Hua people in Dian began…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此矣哀牢內附武侯南征而華人之錯居
于滇者益眾矣加以
國初守戍之兵近日吳越荊襄流寓之族生
齒繁衍其間則華人已十之五六矣欲推
衣冠之族而論其本則更僕未易數也然
愚以謂執事豈真欲多士之論其世系所
出哉有以窺執事宣風廣化之盛心矣大
約滇俗之所尚最貴重漢姓其次則僰人
而夷姓為下故漢僰不屑與諸夷齒而諸
===
===
夷亦不敢望漢僰今僰人之起家儒籍及
由佐史登仕者相望而諸夷獨擯不與諸
夷之執役輸賦無異漢僰也春秋之法夷
狄進於中國則中國之諸夷之慕中華而
重漢姓也是欲棄幽谷而遷于喬木者若
之何絕之也絕之則彼甘以夷狄自待而
進之則其慕義之心益固愚以謂諸夷之
求齒於中國者雖吏之可也雖隸之學官
可也書曰欲竝生哉此之謂也故士之能
punctuated: 此矣。哀牢內附，武侯南征，而華人之錯居于滇者益眾矣。加以國初守戍之兵、近日吳越荊襄流寓之族，生齒繁衍其間，則華人已十之五六矣。欲推衣冠之族而論其本，則更僕未易數也。然愚以謂執事豈真欲多士之論其世系所出哉？有以窺執事宣風廣化之盛心矣。大約滇俗之所尚，最貴重漢姓，其次則僰人，而夷姓為下。故漢僰不屑與諸夷齒，而諸夷亦不敢望漢僰。今僰人之起家儒籍及由佐史登仕者相望，而諸夷獨擯不與。諸夷之執役輸賦，無異漢僰也。《春秋》之法，夷狄進於中國，則中國之。諸夷之慕中華而重漢姓也，是欲棄幽谷而遷于喬木者，若之何絕之也？絕之，則彼甘以夷狄自待；而進之，則其慕義之心益固。愚以謂諸夷之求齒於中國者，雖吏之可也，雖隸之學官可也。《書》曰：「欲竝生哉！」此之謂也。故士之能
translation_en:
…at this time. When Ailao submitted to imperial rule and the Marquis of Wu [Zhuge Liang] campaigned in the south, still more Chinese came to live interspersed among the inhabitants of Yunnan. Added to these were the garrison soldiers of the dynasty’s founding years and, more recently, families who settled here from Wu, Yue, Jing, and Xiang. As their population multiplied, Chinese came to constitute five or six out of every ten inhabitants. Were one to trace the origins of the families of the educated elite, they could not readily be enumerated even through successive changes of attendants.

Yet, in my humble opinion, can you really wish the candidates merely to discuss the origins of their lineages? I discern something of your great desire to spread good customs and extend moral transformation. Broadly speaking, in the customary esteem of Yunnan, Han surnames rank highest, the Bo people come next, and non-Han surnames rank lowest. Thus Han and Bo disdain to be ranked alongside the various non-Han peoples, while those peoples dare not aspire to equality with Han and Bo. Today, Bo people who establish themselves through registration as Confucian students or enter official service through subordinate clerical posts appear in succession, while the other non-Han peoples alone are excluded from participation. Yet their performance of labor service and payment of taxes are no different from those of Han and Bo.

According to the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when the Yi and Di advance toward the Central States, they are treated as people of the Central States. These peoples’ admiration for Chinese civilization and esteem for Han surnames show that they wish to leave the dark valley and ascend to the tall trees. How could we shut them out? If excluded, they will willingly regard themselves as barbarians; if advanced, their aspiration toward righteousness will grow still firmer. In my humble opinion, those among these peoples who seek to rank alongside the people of the Central States may even be appointed to office or enrolled in the government schools. The Book of Documents says, “Would that all might live together!” This is what it means. Thus, scholars who can…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
自立者不當問其世夷之求進於華者不
必問其類不識執事以爲何如
第四問
楊道東
考試官敎諭毛批任事之忠折衝之略讀之具見
子其以孔明希文自待者矣敬羡敬羡
考試官學正王批才識俊逸議論慷慨必素以忠
勇自負者
世之論將者有曰學敵萬人闊視孫吳者
===
矣此則武力之士而非國家之急有曰起
身文墨高談韜鈐者矣此則議論之士而
非國家之急國家之所急在於忠勇之兼
資名實之相副也蓋勇而匪忠則雄赳有
之矣而不足以立貞純之節實不副名則
聲譽歸之矣而不足以究心術之蘊以是
處之無事猶懼蹶於用也况於緩急之際
乎故必忠勇兼資然後才適於用而成敗
非所論名實相副然後任當其才而眞似
punctuated:
自立者，不當問其世；夷之求進於華者，不必問其類。不識執事以爲何如？

第四問
楊道東

考試官敎諭毛批：任事之忠，折衝之略，讀之具見。子其以孔明、希文自待者矣！敬羡！敬羡！

考試官學正王批：才識俊逸，議論慷慨，必素以忠勇自負者。

世之論將者，有曰學敵萬人、闊視孫吳者矣，此則武力之士，而非國家之急；有曰起身文墨、高談韜鈐者矣，此則議論之士，而非國家之急。國家之所急，在於忠勇之兼資、名實之相副也。蓋勇而匪忠，則雄赳有之矣，而不足以立貞純之節；實不副名，則聲譽歸之矣，而不足以究心術之蘊。以是處之無事，猶懼蹶於用也，况於緩急之際乎？故必忠勇兼資，然後才適於用，而成敗非所論；名實相副，然後任當其才，而眞似
translation_en:
…those capable of establishing themselves should not be questioned about their ancestry; non-Han people who seek to advance into Chinese civilization need not be questioned about their ethnic category. I wonder what you, sir, think of this?

Fourth Policy Question
Yang Daodong

Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: Your loyalty in undertaking responsibilities and your strategies for repelling aggression are fully evident upon reading this. Surely you hold yourself to the standards of Kongming and Xiwen! My respectful admiration! My respectful admiration!

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Your ability and discernment are outstanding, and your arguments are impassioned. Surely you have long prided yourself on loyalty and courage.

Among those who discuss generalship, some speak of learning to contend against ten thousand men and looking disdainfully upon Sun and Wu. Such men possess martial prowess, but they are not what the state urgently needs. Others speak of rising through literary pursuits and discoursing loftily on military strategy. Such men excel in discussion, but they are not what the state urgently needs. What the state urgently needs is the combination of loyalty and courage, with reputation and actual ability matching one another. For if a man is courageous but not loyal, he may possess martial boldness, yet lack the means to establish steadfast and pure integrity. If his actual ability does not match his reputation, acclaim may accrue to him, yet this is insufficient to ascertain his underlying intentions and principles. Even when employing such men in peaceful times, one fears that they will falter when put to use; how much more so in moments of crisis! Thus, only when loyalty and courage are combined is a man's ability suited to service, with success or failure no longer the point at issue; only when reputation and actual ability match is his appointment commensurate with his talents, and whether these are genuine or merely apparent…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
非所慮何也才有真似而功有成敗持必
成之畫者難與論事操似是之見者幾於
失人如是而曰才難其然豈其然乎夫經
武莫要乎兵需材莫難於將書曰克詰戎
兵言備武也詩曰文武吉甫言任將也蓋
將者國之輔三軍之司命安內攘外胥此
焉而可弗慎乎唐虞三代之盛也兵無專
統將無專設無事則濟濟師師而將歸卿
列有事則赫赫業業而諸卿皆將故有扈
===
之戰南征之師取之股肱而辦非別為推
轂之謀也魯之伐徐韓之追貊取之屏翰
而足非別為授鉞之命也當是時君知其
臣臣知其君將帥由於環衛折衝本於尊
俎非嘗試而泛使之也非冥授而妄投之
也其果毅沉鷙忠義勇武皆君所目濡耳
涵者夫是以才適於用任當其才頌于襄
之績而稱來威之功者至今猶奕奕也吁
可易言哉逮德下衰以兵力相雄長者莫
punctuated: 非所慮。何也？才有真似，而功有成敗。持必成之畫者，難與論事；操似是之見者，幾於失人。如是而曰才難，其然？豈其然乎？夫經武莫要乎兵，需材莫難於將。《書》曰：「克詰戎兵。」言備武也。《詩》曰：「文武吉甫。」言任將也。蓋將者，國之輔，三軍之司命，安內攘外胥此焉，而可弗慎乎？唐虞三代之盛也，兵無專統，將無專設。無事則濟濟師師，而將歸卿列；有事則赫赫業業，而諸卿皆將。故有扈之戰、南征之師，取之股肱而辦，非別為推轂之謀也；魯之伐徐、韓之追貊，取之屏翰而足，非別為授鉞之命也。當是時，君知其臣，臣知其君，將帥由於環衛，折衝本於尊俎，非嘗試而泛使之也，非冥授而妄投之也。其果毅沉鷙、忠義勇武，皆君所目濡耳涵者。夫是以才適於用，任當其才，頌于襄之績而稱來威之功者，至今猶奕奕也。吁！可易言哉？逮德下衰，以兵力相雄長者莫
translation_en:
…whether their talent was genuine or merely apparent would be no cause for concern. Why? Talent may be genuine or apparent, while endeavors may succeed or fail. Those who insist upon plans certain to succeed are difficult to deliberate with; those who hold superficially plausible views are liable to overlook worthy men. To proceed thus and then declare that talent is scarce—is that really so? How could it be so?

In managing military affairs, nothing matters more than the troops; in seeking talent, nothing is harder than finding commanders. The Book of Documents says, “Be able to put the forces in order”: this speaks of military preparedness. The Book of Odes says, “Jifu, accomplished in civil and military affairs”: this speaks of appointing commanders. A commander is the state's support and the arbiter of the lives of its armies. Securing order within and repelling enemies without both depend upon him. Can one fail to exercise care?

In the flourishing age of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, troops had no separate permanent command, and commanders held no separately established posts. In peaceful times, dignified and mutually respectful, the commanders stood among the ministers; when trouble arose, imposing and formidable, all the ministers became commanders. Thus, for the battle against Youhu and the expedition south, men were drawn from the ruler's trusted ministers, and the tasks were accomplished; no separate arrangements were made to dispatch commanders by ceremonially pushing their chariot wheels. For Lu's attack on Xu and Han's pursuit of the Mo, men were drawn from the state's protective bulwarks, and these sufficed; no separate orders were issued to confer the battle-axe of command.

At that time, rulers knew their ministers, and ministers knew their rulers. Commanders came from those who guarded the ruler; the thwarting of enemy attacks had its foundation at the court's ritual vessels and banquet tables. Men were neither casually employed as an experiment nor blindly appointed and recklessly committed to action. Their resolve, composure and fierceness, loyalty and righteousness, courage and martial prowess were all qualities the ruler had absorbed through his own eyes and ears. Thus their talents suited their employment, and their assignments matched their abilities. The praises of their achievements in rendering aid [?] and of their success in bringing others to submit in awe remain splendid even today. Ah! Can such matters be spoken of lightly?

When virtue subsequently declined, among those who vied for supremacy through military strength, none…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
如晉楚然興師遣將猶不失先王之遺意
若卻穀欒枝孫叔敖子反子庚之徒皆以
上卿董戎旅邢伯養叔伯州犁苗賁皇之
徒皆以大夫備行列此非周人居則爲比
閭族黨州鄉之卿士出則爲伍兩卒旅師
軍之將帥之制乎德又下衰此意漸泯業
俎豆者不問軍旅之事習紈袴者蔑視詩
書之澤進取之途旣廣文武之用自殊執
事所謂章縫之士諱言戰伐書生不可任
===
以軍旅者是矣然吾聞之瑟不可以膠柱
調士不可以拘方論愚生不敏甞讀史而
慨於中矣孔明之於漢也祖逖之於晉也
同一興復之事也一則三顧托心而許先
帝以驅馳一則聞雞扼腕而以廓清爲巳
任彼羽扇綸巾貌若迂闊然七擒孟獲而
曰天威走生仲達而曰奇才流馬木牛之
制思巧若神此豈章句之儒能辦哉漢史
以將略非其所長蓋不知亮矣擊楫中流
punctuated:
如晉楚，然興師遣將，猶不失先王之遺意。若卻穀、欒枝、孫叔敖、子反、子庚之徒，皆以上卿董戎旅；邢伯、養叔、伯州犁、苗賁皇之徒，皆以大夫備行列。此非周人居則爲比、閭、族、黨、州、鄉之卿士，出則爲伍、兩、卒、旅、師、軍之將帥之制乎？德又下衰，此意漸泯。業俎豆者不問軍旅之事，習紈袴者蔑視詩書之澤。進取之途旣廣，文武之用自殊。執事所謂章縫之士諱言戰伐，書生不可任以軍旅者，是矣。
然吾聞之，瑟不可以膠柱調，士不可以拘方論。愚生不敏，甞讀史而慨於中矣。孔明之於漢也，祖逖之於晉也，同一興復之事也。一則三顧托心，而許先帝以驅馳；一則聞雞扼腕，而以廓清爲巳任。彼羽扇綸巾，貌若迂闊，然七擒孟獲而曰天威，走生仲達而曰奇才。流馬木牛之制，思巧若神，此豈章句之儒能辦哉？漢史以將略非其所長，蓋不知亮矣。擊楫中流，
translation_en:
…equaled Jin and Chu. Yet in raising armies and dispatching generals, they still preserved something of the intentions bequeathed by the former kings. Men such as Que Gu [?], Luan Zhi, Sun Shu’ao, Zifan, and Zigeng all directed military forces as senior ministers; men such as Xing Bo, Yang Shu, Bo Zhouli, and Miao Benhuang all served in the ranks as grand masters. Was this not the Zhou system, under which men at home served as ministers and officers of the residential groupings—bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang—and on campaign served as commanders of the military units—wu, liang, zu, lü, shi, and jun? As virtue declined still further, this conception gradually vanished. Those whose occupation concerned ritual vessels took no interest in military affairs, while those accustomed to silken trousers scorned the civilizing influence of the Odes and Documents. As avenues of advancement multiplied, civil and military service naturally diverged. This is precisely what you mean, sir, when you say that scholars wearing the ceremonial cap shun discussion of warfare, and that bookish men cannot be entrusted with armies.
Yet I have heard that a zither cannot be tuned with its bridges glued in place, nor can a gentleman be judged by rigid rules. Dull though this humble student is, I have often read history and felt deeply stirred. Kongming’s service to the Han and Zu Ti’s to the Jin were alike undertakings of restoration. The former, entrusted with the ruler’s confidence after three visits, pledged himself to the late emperor’s service; the latter, hearing the cock crow, clenched his wrist in resolve and took clearing the realm of enemies as his own responsibility. With his feather fan and silken headcloth, Kongming appeared impractical and remote from affairs. Yet after capturing Meng Huo seven times, his prowess was called “Heaven’s might”; after putting the living Zhongda to flight, he was called “an extraordinary talent.” His invention of the flowing horses and wooden oxen displayed ingenuity seemingly divine. Could a scholar versed only in textual exegesis have accomplished this? The history of the Han holds that military strategy was not his strength: its author surely did not understand Liang. Striking his oar in midstream…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
氣甚激烈故一戰而起淮陰再戰而克譙
城練兵積穀之計志慮甚遠信非忠義之
士不能矣晉史謂職爲貪亂蓋不諒逖矣
馬謖之於孔明也劉秩之於房琯也均之
信任之專也一則巵言投于夙交而謂其
才術過人一則詭論售於簪盍而謂其能
敵多賊然街亭之旅舉措煩擾致違節制
之誅攻心之說徒左券耳豈非大言無當
之效乎昭烈有曰謖言過其實不可大用
===
信矣而亮不之察何哉陳濤斜之師車戰
不利乃遭輿尸之凶鑄錢之議猶直鉤耳
毋亦拘泥古法之過與進明嘗曰琯迂闊
大言引用浮黨審矣而琯不之悟何哉夏
元昊恃其强悍數寇邊鄙匪河隴間一羌
酋也宋固不能以羈縻其父祖者而制畜
之矣時則范仲淹經略環慶夫淹草萊經
生也而付以邊寄非投之至艱乎乃務持
重不急近功小利至決策取橫山復靈武
punctuated:
氣甚激烈，故一戰而起淮陰，再戰而克譙城。練兵積穀之計，志慮甚遠，信非忠義之士不能矣。晉史謂職爲貪亂，蓋不諒逖矣。
馬謖之於孔明也，劉秩之於房琯也，均之信任之專也。一則巵言投于夙交，而謂其才術過人；一則詭論售於簪盍，而謂其能敵多賊。然街亭之旅，舉措煩擾，致違節制之誅；攻心之說，徒左券耳，豈非大言無當之效乎？昭烈有曰：「謖言過其實，不可大用。」信矣，而亮不之察，何哉？陳濤斜之師，車戰不利，乃遭輿尸之凶；鑄錢之議，猶直鉤耳，毋亦拘泥古法之過與？進明嘗曰：「琯迂闊大言，引用浮黨。」審矣，而琯不之悟，何哉？
夏元昊恃其强悍，數寇邊鄙，匪河隴間一羌酋也。宋固不能以羈縻其父祖者而制畜之矣。時則范仲淹經略環慶。夫淹草萊經生也，而付以邊寄，非投之至艱乎？乃務持重，不急近功小利，至決策取橫山、復靈武。
translation_en:
…his spirit was intensely ardent. Thus, in one battle he rose at Huaiyin [?], and in a second he captured Qiaocheng. His plans to train troops and stockpile grain showed far-reaching purpose and foresight: surely only a loyal and righteous man could have accomplished this. The History of the Jin describes him as coveting disorder [?]; this surely fails to understand Zu Ti.
Ma Su’s relationship with Kongming and Liu Zhi’s with Fang Guan were alike in the exclusive trust placed in them. In the first case, glib words appealed to a longstanding friend, who pronounced his talents and methods superior to those of others; in the second, specious arguments won acceptance among assembled associates, who pronounced him capable of opposing numerous rebels. Yet in the campaign at Jieting, confused and disruptive actions led to execution for disobeying military orders. His doctrine of winning over men’s hearts proved merely an empty guarantee of success. Was this not the consequence of grandiose but impractical talk? Emperor Zhaolie once said: “Su’s words exceed his actual abilities; he must not be entrusted with great responsibilities.” True indeed! Why, then, did Zhuge Liang fail to perceive this? In the campaign at Chentaoxie, chariot warfare proved unsuccessful, bringing the calamity of carrying home corpses. The proposal to mint coins was likewise merely a straight fishing hook—ineffectual. Was this not also the fault of rigid adherence to ancient methods? Jinming once said: “Guan is impractical and given to grandiose talk; he recruits and promotes frivolous partisans.” An accurate judgment! Why, then, did Guan fail to recognize it?
Yuanhao of Xia relied on his strength and ferocity to raid the borderlands repeatedly; he was no mere Qiang chieftain in the He–Long region. The Song certainly could not restrain and control him through the means of loose rein previously used to manage his father and grandfather. At that time, Fan Zhongyan directed military affairs in Huanqing. Zhongyan was a scholar of the classics from humble circumstances; was entrusting him with responsibility for the frontier not to cast him into the greatest difficulty? Yet he made prudence his priority, seeking neither immediate achievements nor small gains, and went so far as to resolve upon taking Hengshan and recovering Lingwu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
威德著聞蕃部震竦破膽之謡自軍中頌
之此其名將之選乎金虜逞其驕逆深躪
江淮誠脅背間一疽毒也王權已不能力
拒于合肥而思退保矣時則虞允文犒師
江上夫虞白面書生也而迫於勁賊非臨
之卒然乎乃徇軍中檄權先遁之罪至措
畫列馬步分戈船鼓勇倂進俘斬甚衆媿
死之嘆自劉錡發之此其仁者之勇乎就
而論之馬謖之負孔明劉秩之負房琯斯
===
皆以市井之心肆狙詐之術而不免焉無
足論已虞允文保障江淮而金人北遁人
主褒之曰今之裴度范仲淹捍蔽鄜延而
僞夏乞和羌人仰之曰龍圖老子此則威
名著於天下勛業滿於邊陲君子固嘉其
能成天下之事矣乃若孔明負王佐之才
而鼎據巴蜀不能進取中原尺寸祖逖抱
恢復之志而憤恚發疾卒之河南復爲荆
棘蓋天方厭亂雖十孔明百祖逖無救於
punctuated:
威德著聞，蕃部震竦，破膽之謡自軍中頌之，此其名將之選乎？金虜逞其驕逆，深躪江淮，誠脅背間一疽毒也。王權已不能力拒于合肥，而思退保矣。時則虞允文犒師江上，夫虞白面書生也，而迫於勁賊，非臨之卒然乎？乃徇軍中，檄權先遁之罪，至措畫列馬步，分戈船，鼓勇倂進，俘斬甚衆。媿死之嘆自劉錡發之，此其仁者之勇乎？就而論之，馬謖之負孔明，劉秩之負房琯，斯皆以市井之心肆狙詐之術而不免焉，無足論已。
虞允文保障江淮，而金人北遁，人主褒之曰：「今之裴度。」范仲淹捍蔽鄜延，而僞夏乞和，羌人仰之曰：「龍圖老子。」此則威名著於天下，勛業滿於邊陲，君子固嘉其能成天下之事矣。乃若孔明負王佐之才，而鼎據巴蜀，不能進取中原尺寸；祖逖抱恢復之志，而憤恚發疾，卒之河南復爲荆棘。蓋天方厭亂，雖十孔明、百祖逖，無救於
translation_en:
…his might and virtue became widely known, and the tribal peoples trembled in fear. Songs of his striking terror into the enemy were sung in praise of him within the army. Was he not a worthy choice as an eminent general? The Jin invaders indulged their arrogance and defiance, ravaging deep into the Jiang–Huai region: truly a poisonous abscess between the flank and back. Wang Quan was already unable to mount an effective resistance at Hefei and was contemplating retreat to a defensible position. At that time Yu Yunwen was rewarding the troops on the Yangzi. Yu was a pale-faced scholar; confronted by a powerful enemy, was he not thrust into the crisis without warning? He went through the army, issuing a proclamation denouncing Wang Quan’s offense of fleeing first. He then made dispositions, arraying cavalry and infantry and dividing the warships into groups. Rousing their courage, he sent them forward together, capturing and killing great numbers. Liu Qi himself exclaimed that he was ashamed enough to die. Was this not the courage of a benevolent man? Considering these cases, Ma Su’s failure of Kongming and Liu Zhi’s failure of Fang Guan both arose from their giving free rein to cunning and deceit with the mentality of marketplace schemers; neither escaped the consequences. They merit no further discussion.
Yu Yunwen secured the Jiang–Huai region, and the Jin forces fled north. The sovereign praised him as “the Pei Du of our day.” Fan Zhongyan shielded Fu–Yan, and the illegitimate Xia regime sued for peace. The Qiang looked up to him, calling him “the Venerable Master of the Dragon Diagram Hall.” Their martial renown thus became known throughout the realm, and their achievements extended throughout the frontier regions. The gentleman certainly commends their ability to accomplish the affairs of the realm. Yet Kongming, possessed of the talents of a king’s assistant, held Ba and Shu as one of three contending powers but could not advance to take so much as an inch of the Central Plain. Zu Ti cherished the ambition of restoring the lost territories, but indignation brought on illness, and in the end Henan again became a wilderness of brambles. For Heaven was then weary of disorder; even ten Kongmings and a hundred Zu Tis could not have averted…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敗故曰若夫成功則天也二賢之謂矣要
之允文志於勤王祖逖志於匡晉仲淹忠
於輔宋孔明忠於扶劉成敗雖殊忠勇則
一果可以優劣論哉夫天下有真才焉諸范祖虞
秩馬謖之謂矣天下有似才焉劉
之謂矣嗟夫淄澠合而味殊宮商奏而響
異之四臣者皆賢矣君子寧無折衷之見
乎希文之言曰爲之自我者當如是其成
與否不在我者聖賢不能必孔明之言曰
===
鞠躬盡瘁斃而後已成敗利鈍非所逆覩
推是心也即書之篤棐詩之匪懈孔子之
以忠皆是物也噫二賢之見又過於祖虞
遠矣豈非後世爲將者之蓍蔡乎今
聖天子在上總攬萬幾
明照四海南征北討霆迅風馳文武忠良之
臣固懍懍慄慄奔走役使不給况豎布之
賤乎周王壽考兔罝干城漢室治安賈生
抗請愚也海谷顓蒙摘尋章句浸沐
punctuated:
敗。故曰：「若夫成功，則天也。」二賢之謂矣。要之，允文志於勤王，祖逖志於匡晉，仲淹忠於輔宋，孔明忠於扶劉，成敗雖殊，忠勇則一，果可以優劣論哉？夫天下有真才焉，諸范祖虞秩馬謖之謂矣。天下有似才焉，劉之謂矣。嗟夫！淄澠合而味殊，宮商奏而響異。之四臣者皆賢矣，君子寧無折衷之見乎？希文之言曰：「爲之自我者當如是，其成與否，不在我者，聖賢不能必。」孔明之言曰：「鞠躬盡瘁，斃而後已。成敗利鈍，非所逆覩。」推是心也，即《書》之篤棐、《詩》之匪懈、孔子之以忠，皆是物也。噫！二賢之見，又過於祖虞遠矣，豈非後世爲將者之蓍蔡乎？
今聖天子在上，總攬萬幾，明照四海，南征北討，霆迅風馳。文武忠良之臣，固懍懍慄慄，奔走役使不給，况豎布之賤乎？周王壽考，兔罝干城；漢室治安，賈生抗請。愚也海谷顓蒙，摘尋章句，浸沐
translation_en:
…defeat. Hence the saying, “As for achieving success, that rests with Heaven.” This describes those two worthy men. In essence, Yu Yunwen aspired to serve his sovereign, and Zu Ti to uphold the Jin; Fan Zhongyan loyally supported the Song, and Zhuge Liang loyally sustained the house of Liu. Though their success and failure differed, their loyalty and courage were alike. Can they really be ranked as superior or inferior? There are men of true talent in the world: Zhuge Liang, Fan Zhongyan, Zu Ti, and Yu Yunwen. There are men of seeming talent: Liu Zhi and Ma Su [the transcription is disordered here; this grouping is uncertain]. Alas! Though the waters of the Zi and Sheng mingle, their tastes differ; though the gong and shang notes sound together, their tones remain distinct. These four ministers were all worthy, but should a gentleman not form a discriminating judgment? Fan Zhongyan, whose courtesy name was Xiwen, said: “In what depends upon my own action, this is how I ought to act. Whether it succeeds is beyond my control; even sages and worthies cannot guarantee it.” Zhuge Liang, whose courtesy name was Kongming, said: “I shall bend to the task and exhaust my strength, ceasing only at death. Success or failure, advantage or setback—these cannot be foreseen.” Extend this disposition, and it is the same as the earnest assistance spoken of in the Book of Documents, the unflagging diligence of the Book of Odes, and Confucius’s injunction to act with loyalty. Ah! The understanding of these two worthies far surpassed even that of Zu Ti and Yu Yunwen. Are they not like divining stalks and tortoise shells for the generals of later ages?
Now the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, overseeing the myriad affairs of government. His illumination reaches throughout the Four Seas; his expeditions south and north move swiftly as thunder and wind. His loyal and worthy civil and military ministers already tremble with earnest apprehension, hastening to carry out their duties with scarcely time enough. How much more should a lowly commoner [?] do so? Under the long-lived king of Zhou, rabbit-netters served as shield and wall; when the Han realm enjoyed peace and order, Master Jia nevertheless submitted an earnest appeal. Foolish, shallow, and benighted as I am [?], I search out passages and phrases, steeped in …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
閭澤爭自濯磨軍旅之事非所敢議寧無效
一命之寄殫致身之義而以孔明希文自
期待乎夫南越之脩簳礪以金鏃括以勁
羽加諸强弩之上以射犀兕於千步之外
無不立穿者此天下之利器而決勝覿武
之所寶也故孔明希文者南越之脩簳天
下之利器而國家之所急也今人置盂以
注水盂圓則水圓盂方則水方設車以駕
馬車右則馬右車左則馬左何也其所置
===
設然也有志尚友者希亮而亮希范而范
無所於尼也在夫所自置設耳夫仲淹自
秀才時以天下爲已任而墨帳然燈攻苦
問學所以豫養其先憂後樂之志者非苟
而已孔明處隆中躬耕隴畝棲志澹泊抱
膝梁父之吟一莘野樂道之高也孔子曰
隱居以求志行義以達道由是觀之則孔
明希文之所養固有本矣故後之學者
可無二賢之位望而不可無二賢之忠勇
punctuated: 閭澤，爭自濯磨。軍旅之事，非所敢議，寧無效一命之寄、殫致身之義，而以孔明、希文自期待乎？夫南越之脩簳，礪以金鏃，括以勁羽，加諸强弩之上，以射犀兕於千步之外，無不立穿者。此天下之利器，而決勝覿武之所寶也。故孔明、希文者，南越之脩簳、天下之利器，而國家之所急也。今人置盂以注水，盂圓則水圓，盂方則水方；設車以駕馬，車右則馬右，車左則馬左。何也？其所置設然也。有志尚友者，希亮而亮，希范而范，無所於尼也，在夫所自置設耳。夫仲淹自秀才時，以天下爲已任，而墨帳然燈，攻苦問學，所以豫養其先憂後樂之志者，非苟而已。孔明處隆中，躬耕隴畝，棲志澹泊，抱膝梁父之吟，一莘野樂道之高也。孔子曰：「隱居以求志，行義以達道。」由是觀之，則孔明、希文之所養，固有本矣。故後之學者，可無二賢之位望，而不可無二賢之忠勇。
translation_en:
…beneficence [?], striving to cleanse and refine myself. Military affairs are not something I dare discuss. Yet could I fail to fulfill the trust of even the lowest official appointment, discharge to the utmost my duty to devote myself to service, and take Kongming and Xiwen as the standards to which I aspire?

The long bamboo arrow shafts of Nanyue, fitted with sharpened metal heads and sturdy feather fletching, are placed on powerful crossbows and shot at rhinoceroses and wild oxen more than a thousand paces away: none fails to pierce its target at once. These are the finest weapons under Heaven, treasured for securing victory in armed encounters. Thus Kongming and Xiwen are like the long bamboo shafts of Nanyue—the finest weapons under Heaven, urgently needed by the state.

Now, when someone sets out a basin and pours water into it, if the basin is round, the water is round; if the basin is square, the water is square. When a carriage is made ready and horses harnessed to it, if the carriage goes right, the horses go right; if the carriage goes left, the horses go left. Why? The arrangement makes it so. Those resolved to seek fellowship with worthy men of antiquity may aspire to be like Zhuge Liang and become like Liang, or aspire to be like Fan Zhongyan and become like Fan. Nothing bars their way; it depends only on how they situate and prepare themselves.

From his days as a student, Zhongyan took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. Lighting a lamp within a black bed-curtain, he endured hardship and pursued learning. The means by which he nurtured beforehand his resolve to worry before others and rejoice after them were anything but casual. When Kongming lived at Longzhong, he tilled the fields himself, grounded his aspirations in tranquil simplicity, and clasped his knees while chanting the Song of Liangfu. His lofty delight in the Way was just like that of Yi Yin in the fields of Shen.

Confucius said: “Live in retirement to pursue your aspirations; practice righteousness to give full expression to the Way.” Viewed in this light, the self-cultivation of Kongming and Xiwen certainly had firm foundations. Thus scholars of later generations may lack the rank and prestige of these two worthies, but must not lack their loyalty and courage…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
可無二賢之事業而不可無二賢之問學
第五問
俞世傑
同考試官教諭盧批此作援古證今切中滇中夷情
必留心於世故者錄之
考試官教諭毛批才格恢弘文詞倜儻
考試官學正王批籌畫精詳足占經濟
帝王制治有綏遠之道焉有威遠之道焉
其綏之也以德而威之也以兵德也者常
===
施之義治心之術也兵也者制變之權輔
其治之不及者也有以綏之無以威之則
法弛而民玩玩則亂心生焉有以威之無
以綏之則暴勝而民殘殘則變志作焉生
亂而長變則偏勝以爲囮此仁義並用所
以爲長久安寧之道也且所謂德非必慈
柔寬縱而姑息之爲也其道有三曰示之
禮信以和其志阜之財求以厚其生同其
教化以維其俗也所謂兵非必猛奮窮黷
punctuated:
可無二賢之事業，而不可無二賢之問學。

第五問
俞世傑

同考試官教諭盧批：此作援古證今，切中滇中夷情，必留心於世故者，錄之。
考試官教諭毛批：才格恢弘，文詞倜儻。
考試官學正王批：籌畫精詳，足占經濟。

帝王制治，有綏遠之道焉，有威遠之道焉。其綏之也以德，而威之也以兵。德也者，常施之義、治心之術也；兵也者，制變之權，輔其治之不及者也。有以綏之，無以威之，則法弛而民玩，玩則亂心生焉；有以威之，無以綏之，則暴勝而民殘，殘則變志作焉。生亂而長變，則偏勝以爲囮。此仁義並用，所以爲長久安寧之道也。且所謂德，非必慈柔寬縱而姑息之爲也。其道有三，曰：示之禮信，以和其志；阜之財求，以厚其生；同其教化，以維其俗也。所謂兵，非必猛奮窮黷
translation_en:
…One may lack the achievements of these two worthies, but one must not lack their dedication to inquiry and learning.

Fifth Policy Question
Yu Shijie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: This essay draws on antiquity to illuminate the present and precisely addresses the circumstances of the non-Han peoples of Yunnan. Its author must pay close attention to worldly affairs. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: His talent and scope are expansive; his literary expression is bold and untrammeled.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: His planning is meticulous and thorough, sufficient to demonstrate his capacity for statecraft.

In establishing good government, emperors and kings have a way to pacify distant peoples and a way to overawe them. They pacify them through virtue and overawe them through military force. Virtue is the principle to be applied constantly, the means of governing people's hearts. Military force is the discretionary means of controlling emergencies, supplementing what government cannot reach. If there are means to pacify them but none to overawe them, the laws become lax and the people treat them lightly; such disregard gives rise to rebellious thoughts. If there are means to overawe them but none to pacify them, violence prevails and the people suffer injury; such injury gives rise to intentions of revolt. To engender disorder and foster revolt is to let a one-sided predominance serve as a lure [?]. Thus the joint application of benevolence and righteousness is the way to lasting peace and tranquility.

Moreover, what is called virtue does not necessarily mean being kindly and yielding, indulgent and permissive, merely accommodating people. It has three methods: demonstrate ritual propriety and trustworthiness to harmonize their intentions; increase their wealth and resources [?] to enrich their livelihood; and unify their moral instruction to sustain their customs. What is called military force does not necessarily mean violent aggression and the unrestrained abuse of arms…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而凌殄之爲也其道有三曰養將士以固
其謀習戰守以勵其氣蓄財用以裕其施
也六者之行今日之急而執事者覩滇民
之日變抵冒殊扞熟爛而不可救大壞之
極也憂而咨之曰是非民之罪也故爲之
策曰撲滅之勳孰與輯綏不假兵威使自
警服抑有道乎吁此甚盛意也任德而不
任刑古之道也而愚生察今時之流漸積
猥似有大謬不然者夫治之有德威猶天
===
之有陰陽陽爲德而陰爲威德主生而威
主殺董子曰刑不可任以治世猶陰之不
可任以成歲非執事任德之說乎貴輯綏
而賤威戮之義乎然天使陽出布施於上
而主歲功又使陰入伏於下而時出以佐
陽則終陽以成歲陰之力也是天任陽而
不能廢陰猶治之任德而不能廢威也通
於斯義可以復執事之策矣策曰滇省以
中國之人處夷僰之間所謂夷僰者固亦
punctuated:
而凌殄之爲也。其道有三，曰：養將士以固其謀，習戰守以勵其氣，蓄財用以裕其施也。六者之行，今日之急。而執事者覩滇民之日變，抵冒殊扞，熟爛而不可救，大壞之極也。憂而咨之曰：「是非民之罪也。」故爲之策曰：「撲滅之勳，孰與輯綏？不假兵威，使自警服，抑有道乎？」吁！此甚盛意也。任德而不任刑，古之道也。而愚生察今時之流漸積猥，似有大謬不然者。
夫治之有德威，猶天之有陰陽。陽爲德而陰爲威，德主生而威主殺。董子曰：「刑不可任以治世，猶陰之不可任以成歲。」非執事任德之說乎？貴輯綏而賤威戮之義乎？然天使陽出布施於上而主歲功，又使陰入伏於下而時出以佐陽，則終陽以成歲，陰之力也。是天任陽而不能廢陰，猶治之任德而不能廢威也。通於斯義，可以復執事之策矣。策曰：「滇省以中國之人處夷僰之間，所謂夷僰者，固亦
translation_en:
…and subjecting them to oppression and extermination. There are three methods: nurturing commanders and soldiers to make their plans firm; practicing warfare and defense to strengthen their spirit; and accumulating funds and supplies to provide ample resources for their deployment. Putting these six measures into practice is an urgent task today. Yet you, observing how the people of Yunnan change by the day, becoming defiant and resistant [?], their corruption so ingrained as to be beyond remedy—the very extreme of disorder—have anxiously considered the matter, saying: “This is not the people’s fault.” You therefore posed this policy question: “How can the merit of crushing and exterminating them compare with that of bringing them peace? Is there perhaps a way to make them take heed and submit of their own accord, without resorting to military force?” Ah! This is a most generous intention. To rely on virtue rather than punishment was the way of antiquity. Yet when I, an ignorant student, examine how present tendencies have gradually accumulated and worsened [?], it seems that this view may be greatly mistaken and inapplicable.
Government possesses virtue and coercive authority just as Heaven possesses yin and yang. Yang represents virtue, and yin represents coercive authority; virtue governs life, while coercive authority governs death. Master Dong said: “Punishment cannot be relied upon to govern the world, just as yin cannot be relied upon to complete the year.” Is this not your argument for relying on virtue? Is it not the principle of valuing pacification and devaluing coercion and execution? Yet Heaven causes yang to emerge and spread its bounty above, taking charge of the year’s accomplishments; it also causes yin to withdraw and lie hidden below, emerging at the proper times to assist yang. Thus, it is through yin’s power that yang’s work is brought to completion and the year fulfilled. Heaven relies on yang but cannot dispense with yin, just as government relies on virtue but cannot dispense with coercive authority. Understanding this principle makes it possible to answer your policy question. The question states: “In Yunnan Province, people from the Central Lands dwell among the Yi and Bo. Those called Yi and Bo certainly also …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
耕田供稅非化外也愚曰此其所以最難
治而不可純任德者也何也其地不可耕
也其民不可使也居荒徼之外政教號令
之所不加此名夷而實夷者則一以夷治
之其來也不拒其去也不追其附也羈縻
而不齒度雖併包而防則峻焉治之不亦
易乎其地經界也其民編戶也居綏服之
內仁義禮樂所常被服此名中國而實中
國者則一以中國治之其善也必庸其梗
===
也必誅其誅賞也一法而不議恩雖涵煦
而威必行焉治之不亦易乎若夫滇省則
異於是矣其地可耕也而土力未盡任也
其民可使也而番戶未盡入也以中國五
方之華冑而與夷僰雜處其言語通矣其
服食同矣其居室其田疇相屬矣其原隰
衍沃屯落崖險寨柵之居相錯矣使漢人
者聲名文物之軌禮樂章程之節稍自陵
替幾何不胥而為夷也哉以夷僰土著之
punctuated:
耕田供稅，非化外也。愚曰：此其所以最難治，而不可純任德者也。何也？其地不可耕也，其民不可使也，居荒徼之外，政教號令之所不加，此名夷而實夷者，則一以夷治之。其來也不拒，其去也不追，其附也羈縻而不齒，度雖併包而防則峻焉，治之不亦易乎？其地經界也，其民編戶也，居綏服之內，仁義禮樂所常被服，此名中國而實中國者，則一以中國治之。其善也必庸，其梗也必誅，其誅賞也一法而不議，恩雖涵煦而威必行焉，治之不亦易乎？
若夫滇省，則異於是矣。其地可耕也，而土力未盡任也；其民可使也，而番戶未盡入也。以中國五方之華冑而與夷僰雜處，其言語通矣，其服食同矣，其居室、其田疇相屬矣，其原隰衍沃屯落、崖險寨柵之居相錯矣。使漢人者，聲名文物之軌、禮樂章程之節稍自陵替，幾何不胥而為夷也哉？以夷僰土著之
translation_en:
…till the fields and pay taxes; they are not beyond the reach of civilizing influence. In my humble view, this is precisely why they are most difficult to govern and why one cannot rely solely upon virtue. Why is this? Where the land cannot be cultivated and the people cannot be put to service, where they dwell beyond the remote frontiers and government, instruction, commands, and ordinances do not reach them, they are barbarians in both name and reality. Govern them, then, entirely as barbarians. Do not turn them away when they come; do not pursue them when they leave. When they submit, maintain loose ties with them without admitting them to equal standing. Though one's magnanimity embraces them all, one's defenses remain strict. Is governing them not easy? Where the land has its boundaries demarcated and the people are registered as households, where they dwell within the pacified domains and are continually imbued with benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music, this is the Central Realm in both name and reality. Govern them, then, entirely according to the ways of the Central Realm. The good must be employed, and the recalcitrant must be punished. Punishment and reward follow a single standard, without dispute. Though benevolence nurtures them, authority must be enforced. Is governing them not easy?
Yunnan Province, however, differs from these cases. Its land can be cultivated, but its productive capacity has not yet been fully used; its people can be put to service, but the indigenous households have not yet all been registered. Descendants of the Hua people from all five regions of the Central Realm live intermingled with the Yi and Bo. Their languages are mutually intelligible; their clothing and food are the same; their houses and fields adjoin one another. Their settlements on broad, fertile plains and lowlands are interspersed with stockaded dwellings on precipitous heights. If, among the Han people, the norms of cultural refinement and the observances prescribed by rites, music, and institutions should gradually decline, how soon would they all become barbarians? As for the indigenous Yi and Bo…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人而與郡縣雜處其賦輸矣其繇供矣其
於官府之法度常奔走之矣其間秀而儁
者亦學詩書游庠序而觀上國矣使羣其
族類於聲名文物之軌禮樂章程之節咸
率由之毋自棄焉幾何不胥而爲中國之
民哉惟其言語服用田廬險阻之相錯賦
繇供作奔走之相仵獨其犬羊桀傲獷悍
跳梁之性不可終馴侵暴時作鬬亂日興
此其治之也誠難執事者懼而求爲萬世
===
之長策愚於此亦爲執事難之也昔者晉
武之世西北諸部皆爲戎居郭欽慮其漸
之不可長也乃爲之疏欲及平吳之威而
徙之外地以峻出入之防焉晉惠之世戎
居內地輒爲暴橫江統懼其強之不可制
也乃爲之論欲及兵威之盛而徙還彼土
以遠腹心之疾焉茲二者皆其初自外而
之內徙所宜徙者也當時莫之悟而不徙
以致四起而爲雲擾之變德不足而威屈
punctuated:
人而與郡縣雜處，其賦輸矣，其繇供矣，其於官府之法度常奔走之矣。其間秀而儁者，亦學詩書，游庠序，而觀上國矣。使羣其族類，於聲名文物之軌、禮樂章程之節，咸率由之，毋自棄焉，幾何不胥而爲中國之民哉？惟其言語服用、田廬險阻之相錯，賦繇供作奔走之相仵，獨其犬羊桀傲、獷悍跳梁之性不可終馴，侵暴時作，鬬亂日興，此其治之也誠難。執事者懼而求爲萬世之長策，愚於此亦爲執事難之也。
昔者晉武之世，西北諸部皆爲戎居。郭欽慮其漸之不可長也，乃爲之疏，欲及平吳之威而徙之外地，以峻出入之防焉。晉惠之世，戎居內地，輒爲暴橫。江統懼其強之不可制也，乃爲之論，欲及兵威之盛而徙還彼土，以遠腹心之疾焉。茲二者，皆其初自外而之內，徙所宜徙者也。當時莫之悟而不徙，以致四起而爲雲擾之變，德不足而威屈
translation_en:
…people living intermingled with the inhabitants of prefectures and counties: they pay their taxes, perform their labor service, and regularly comply with the laws and regulations of the authorities. The outstanding and talented among them also study the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, attend schools, and visit the central realm. If all their kind were brought together to follow the norms of civilized institutions and culture and the prescriptions of rites, music, and regulations, without abandoning themselves, how soon might they all become people of the Central Kingdom? Their languages, clothing, and everyday usages intermingle; their fields, dwellings, and defensible terrain lie interspersed; and their payment of taxes, performance of labor service, and attendance upon official duties are comparable [?]. Yet their nature—arrogant and unruly like dogs and sheep, fierce, violent, and rebellious—cannot be permanently tamed. Aggression and violence recur, and fighting and disorder arise daily. Governing them is indeed difficult. You gentlemen in charge are apprehensive and seek an enduring policy for ten thousand generations. In my humble view, I too find this difficult on your behalf.
Formerly, in the reign of Emperor Wu of Jin, the various regions of the northwest were all inhabited by the Rong. Guo Qin feared that this gradual development must not be allowed to continue. He therefore submitted a memorial, proposing to take advantage of the prestige gained by pacifying Wu to relocate them to outer territories and tighten restrictions on entry and departure. In the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Rong residing in the interior repeatedly committed violent outrages. Jiang Tong feared that their power would become uncontrollable. He therefore wrote a discourse, proposing to take advantage of the strength of imperial arms to move them back to their own lands, thereby removing a disease from the empire’s vital organs. In both these cases, the people concerned had originally come from outside into the interior; they were people whom it was appropriate to relocate. At the time, no one understood this, and they were not relocated. Consequently, they rose up on all sides, producing upheavals as tumultuous as swirling clouds. Virtue proved insufficient, and coercive power failed…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
焉又何言哉今滇省之夷僰皆土著而內
附者也漢人僑居而夷僰土著驅之而不
能使之外也外之而不能使之遠也不能
使遠而外之是固激之也不能使外而驅
之是固絕之也激而絕之其不生禍而長
變者幾希故求爲今日之長策莫先於輯
綏而輯綏之道非禮信則求敎化不可甞
聞夷僰性至詐也而可以信孚至貪也而
可以廉感至無賴也而可以敎導上之人
===
每以其夷也而夷之惜已夫上之人猶御
也民猶馬也御得其道則駑範馳驅御失
其道則良馬泛駕矣上之人猶冶也民猶
金也鑄得其法則頑鐵就器鑄失其法則
良金躍冶矣執事之策曰孔明用其豪傑
而財賦足用梁毗清節自持而酋長感悅
之二賢者蓋善御也良冶也夷僰雖駑也
頑也亦安得泛駕而躍冶也何也孔明征
夷而就用其豪傑豈借才於裔土哉誠以
punctuated:
焉，又何言哉？今滇省之夷僰，皆土著而內附者也。漢人僑居，而夷僰土著，驅之而不能使之外也，外之而不能使之遠也。不能使遠而外之，是固激之也；不能使外而驅之，是固絕之也。激而絕之，其不生禍而長變者幾希。故求爲今日之長策，莫先於輯綏；而輯綏之道，非禮信，則求敎化不可。甞聞夷僰性至詐也，而可以信孚；至貪也，而可以廉感；至無賴也，而可以敎導。上之人每以其夷也而夷之，惜已！
夫上之人猶御也，民猶馬也。御得其道，則駑範馳驅；御失其道，則良馬泛駕矣。上之人猶冶也，民猶金也。鑄得其法，則頑鐵就器；鑄失其法，則良金躍冶矣。執事之策曰：「孔明用其豪傑，而財賦足用；梁毗清節自持，而酋長感悅之。」二賢者蓋善御也，良冶也。夷僰雖駑也、頑也，亦安得泛駕而躍冶也？何也？孔明征夷，而就用其豪傑，豈借才於裔土哉？誠以
translation_en:
…what more can be said? The Yi and Bo of Yunnan Province today are all indigenous inhabitants who have submitted to imperial authority. The Han people reside here as settlers, whereas the Yi and Bo are native to the land. Even if driven out, they cannot be made to live beyond the borders; even if placed beyond the borders, they cannot be made to go far away. To expel them when they cannot be made to go far is certainly to provoke them; to drive them away when they cannot be made to leave is certainly to alienate them. If provoked and alienated, they will scarcely fail to bring about calamity and foment unrest. Thus, in seeking a lasting policy for the present day, nothing takes precedence over bringing them peace and security. Yet without ritual propriety and trustworthiness, this approach cannot achieve moral transformation through teaching. I have heard that the Yi and Bo are exceedingly deceitful by nature, yet their confidence can be won through trustworthiness; exceedingly avaricious, yet they can be moved by integrity; exceedingly unruly, yet they can be guided through instruction. Those in authority constantly treat them as barbarians simply because they are Yi. What a pity!
Those in authority are like charioteers, and the people like horses. If the charioteer handles them properly, even inferior horses will run as directed [?]; if he handles them improperly, even fine horses will break free of the harness. Those in authority are like metal founders, and the people like metal. If the casting method is correct, even stubborn iron becomes a useful vessel; if it is incorrect, even fine metal leaps out of the furnace. Your policy question states: “Kongming employed their outstanding men, and revenues were sufficient for expenditure; Liang Pi maintained his purity and integrity, and the chieftains were moved and delighted by him.” These two worthies were indeed skilled charioteers and accomplished founders. Even if the Yi and Bo resemble inferior horses or stubborn metal, how could they break free of the harness or leap out of the furnace under such men? Why was this so? When Kongming campaigned against the Yi and then employed their outstanding men, was it merely to borrow talent from distant lands? It was truly because …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
中國之人而臨夷僰於荒徼吾懼其太峻
必將鄙其俗之薄惡以為不足與興教化
也必將惡其情之蠢野以為不足與聞禮
義也日蹙迫以繩之不已復多其文法以
更張之不能習而安之安在其為善御也
孔明深知其然也乃以其疇昔所服之豪
臨其土著相馴之民因其俗而不易其常
維其情而不拂其欲勸之耕織以興其本
業結之然諾以孚其心志是故舉欣欣然
===
出其賦以供上而不以為厲己也奔走州
郡承事長吏莫不以為得也所以致軍國
之足用由此道也孔明其天下之善御已
梁毗治夷而清節自持豈矯情以鎮物哉
誠以大夫師帥下民之所視效遠方之所
瞻曁以為叛服者顧緣其俗之薄惡而嚚
訟好鬭也置之法以罔之因其情之蠢野
而安富崇積也籠其愚而奪之乘其資力
以與民爭利於下日削月朘民安得不窮
punctuated:
中國之人而臨夷僰於荒徼，吾懼其太峻，必將鄙其俗之薄惡，以為不足與興教化也；必將惡其情之蠢野，以為不足與聞禮義也。日蹙迫以繩之不已，復多其文法以更張之，不能習而安之，安在其為善御也？孔明深知其然也，乃以其疇昔所服之豪，臨其土著相馴之民，因其俗而不易其常，維其情而不拂其欲，勸之耕織以興其本業，結之然諾以孚其心志。是故舉欣欣然出其賦以供上，而不以為厲己也；奔走州郡，承事長吏，莫不以為得也。所以致軍國之足用，由此道也。孔明其天下之善御已！

梁毗治夷而清節自持，豈矯情以鎮物哉？誠以大夫師帥，下民之所視效，遠方之所瞻曁以為叛服者。顧緣其俗之薄惡而嚚訟好鬭也，置之法以罔之；因其情之蠢野而安富崇積也，籠其愚而奪之，乘其資力以與民爭利於下，日削月朘，民安得不窮
translation_en:
…if men from the Central Lands were set over the Yi and Bo peoples in the remote borderlands, I fear they would be too harsh. They would surely despise these peoples’ customs as base and wicked, judging them unworthy of moral instruction; they would surely detest their dispositions as dull and uncultivated, judging them unworthy of learning ritual propriety and righteousness. Day after day they would press and constrain them without cease, then multiply written regulations to reform them. Unable to bring the people to become accustomed to these measures and content with them, how could they count as skilled charioteers? Kongming understood this well. He therefore appointed the local notables whom these peoples had long obeyed to govern the indigenous inhabitants, who were accustomed to them. He accommodated their customs without changing their established practices, attended to their feelings without thwarting their desires, encouraged farming and weaving to develop their fundamental livelihoods, and bound them through promises faithfully kept, thereby winning their trust and allegiance. Thus all gladly paid their taxes to support their superiors, without regarding this as an injury to themselves. They hastened to serve the prefectural and commandery administrations and attended upon their senior officials, all considering themselves well served by this arrangement. This was the way he secured sufficient resources for the army and the state. Kongming was indeed a skilled charioteer of the realm!

When Liang Pi governed the Yi peoples and maintained his own integrity, was he merely putting on a show of virtue to keep others in check? It was truly because high officials serve as teachers and leaders: the common people look to them as examples, and those in distant regions watch them in deciding whether to rebel or submit. Yet officials might take advantage of these peoples’ base and wicked customs—their contentiousness, litigiousness, and fondness for fighting—to set legal snares for them. They might exploit their dull and uncultivated dispositions—their contentment in wealth and their esteem for accumulated possessions—to dupe them in their ignorance and seize their property. Using their own resources and power to compete for profit with the people below, they whittle away the people’s means day after day and drain them month after month. How could the people fail to become impoverished…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
且憤哉語曰皇皇求仁義惟恐不能化民
者大夫之意也皇皇求財利惟恐不足者
庶人之事也居大夫之位而行庶人之事
何以帥人梁毗深知其然也乃砥礪名行
無妄取焉夫不發其積則所藏於民者富
矣不易其守則所風於人者遠矣損之自
上而益之自下民知守矣而不敢欺民知
富矣而不敢淫一廉立而利溥矣所以致
