酋長之感悅由此道也梁毗其天下之善
===
鑄巳故由此而言禮信則足以和志由此
而言導利則足以厚生由此而言敎化則
足以維俗二事舉而三善備虞集以其術
爲最簡易可以鑒觀豈不信然哉夫善御
則天下無不可使之民善鑄則天下無不
樂生之民民皆可使而樂生則又何惡於
夷而外之也執事欲以輯綏易撲滅蓋亦
籌之熟矣而愚生測蠡之見則又以威武
之脩不可以盡弛蓋滇夷自漢而唐而宋
punctuated: 且憤哉？語曰：「皇皇求仁義，惟恐不能化民者，大夫之意也；皇皇求財利，惟恐不足者，庶人之事也。」居大夫之位，而行庶人之事，何以帥人？梁毗深知其然也，乃砥礪名行，無妄取焉。夫不發其積，則所藏於民者富矣；不易其守，則所風於人者遠矣。損之自上，而益之自下，民知守矣，而不敢欺；民知富矣，而不敢淫。一廉立而利溥矣。所以致酋長之感悅，由此道也。梁毗其天下之善鑄巳！故由此而言禮信，則足以和志；由此而言導利，則足以厚生；由此而言敎化，則足以維俗。二事舉而三善備，虞集以其術爲最簡易，可以鑒觀，豈不信然哉？夫善御，則天下無不可使之民；善鑄，則天下無不樂生之民。民皆可使而樂生，則又何惡於夷而外之也？執事欲以輯綏易撲滅，蓋亦籌之熟矣。而愚生測蠡之見，則又以威武之脩不可以盡弛。蓋滇夷自漢而唐而宋，
translation_en:
…and resentful as well? As the saying goes: “Earnestly seeking benevolence and righteousness, fearing only that one cannot transform the people: this is the aspiration of a great officer. Earnestly seeking wealth and profit, fearing only that one will not have enough: this is the business of a commoner.” If one occupies the position of a great officer but conducts the business of a commoner, how can one lead others? Liang Pi understood this deeply. He therefore cultivated his reputation and conduct, taking nothing improperly. By not drawing upon the people's accumulated stores, he left abundant wealth among them; by not changing his principles, he exerted a far-reaching moral influence. Those above reduced what they took, and those below gained the benefit. The people learned to uphold their principles and dared not deceive; they learned to enjoy prosperity and dared not indulge in excess. Once integrity was established, its benefits spread widely. This was how he won the gratitude and affection of the chieftains. Liang Pi was surely among the world's finest molders of men!

Thus, viewed in terms of ritual propriety and trustworthiness, this approach suffices to harmonize people's dispositions; viewed in terms of guiding them toward benefit, it suffices to enrich their livelihood; viewed in terms of moral instruction, it suffices to sustain their customs. These two undertakings encompass all three virtues. Yu Ji considered their methods the simplest and easiest, worthy of examination as models. Was he not right? With skillful governance, there are no people under Heaven who cannot be employed; with skillful molding, there are none who do not delight in life. If all the people can be employed and delight in life, what grounds remain for disliking the Yi and treating them as outsiders?

You, honored officials, wish to replace extermination with conciliation and pacification, and surely you have deliberated thoroughly on this. Yet in this foolish student's narrowly limited view, the maintenance of military strength must not be wholly relaxed. For the Yi of Yunnan, from the Han through the Tang and Song…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
屢服屢叛屢叛屢征爰曁我
明一統而郡縣之列之以漢官實之以漢人齊
之以漢法而後夷者日漸於漢彬彬乎夷
夏同風矣惟夫犬羊之性反側不常而官
師之長又或制御失道邇者東川武定之
變易門嶍峨之警可鑒矣威武之備詎容
一日弛耶然竊計此亦不遠於孔明梁毗
之術而得之所謂養將士以固其謀者不
必于他求也選今時土酋之豪立以爲長
===
部落之壯僉以爲兵若猶慮其不可以獨
用也復僉吾中國之可任將領者予之以
駕御統理之權選諸府衞之可爲卒徒者
寓之以主客相維之勢猶身之使臂臂之
使指何敵之不可制而亂之不可遏也所
謂習戰守以勵其氣者不必于他求也蓋
上下山坂出入崖箐夷僰之足至捷也長
戟利刃游弩往來夷僰之技至便也今就
其素所服屬者繫之什伍以時飭之因其
punctuated: 屢服屢叛，屢叛屢征。爰曁我明一統而郡縣之，列之以漢官，實之以漢人，齊之以漢法，而後夷者日漸於漢，彬彬乎夷夏同風矣。惟夫犬羊之性，反側不常，而官師之長又或制御失道，邇者東川、武定之變，易門、嶍峨之警，可鑒矣。威武之備，詎容一日弛耶？然竊計此亦不遠於孔明、梁毗之術而得之。所謂養將士以固其謀者，不必于他求也。選今時土酋之豪，立以爲長；部落之壯，僉以爲兵。若猶慮其不可以獨用也，復僉吾中國之可任將領者，予之以駕御統理之權；選諸府衞之可爲卒徒者，寓之以主客相維之勢。猶身之使臂，臂之使指，何敵之不可制，而亂之不可遏也？所謂習戰守以勵其氣者，不必于他求也。蓋上下山坂，出入崖箐，夷僰之足至捷也；長戟利刃，游弩往來，夷僰之技至便也。今就其素所服屬者，繫之什伍，以時飭之，因其
translation_en:
…time and again they submitted and rebelled; time and again they rebelled and were subjected to punitive campaigns. Only when our Ming unified the realm and organized their lands into prefectures and counties, stationed Han officials among them, settled Han people there, and regulated them by Han laws did the indigenous peoples gradually become imbued with Han ways, until indigenous and Chinese alike shared the same refined customs. Yet their nature, like that of dogs and sheep, is fickle and inconstant, while the officials in charge sometimes also fail to govern them properly. The recent disturbances in Dongchuan and Wuding, and the alarms in Yimen and Xi’e, offer warnings. How could military preparedness be relaxed for even a day?

Yet I venture to think that the means of achieving this lie close to the methods of Kongming and Liang Pi. As for what is called nurturing commanders and soldiers to make their plans secure, there is no need to seek elsewhere. Select the outstanding men among today’s native chieftains and establish them as leaders; levy the able-bodied men of their tribes as soldiers. If there is still concern that they cannot be employed alone, further select men from our central realm who are fit to serve as commanders, and give them authority to direct and administer these forces. Select men from the prefectures and guards who can serve as troops, arranging matters so that local and outside forces sustain one another. It would be like the body directing its arms and the arms directing their fingers: what enemy could not be subdued, and what rebellion could not be checked?

As for what is called practicing warfare and defense to encourage their spirit, there is likewise no need to seek elsewhere. In ascending and descending mountain slopes and passing through cliffs and bamboo thickets, the indigenous peoples, including the Bo, are exceptionally swift of foot. With long halberds and sharp blades, and in maneuvering with crossbows [?], their skills are exceptionally adept. Now, working through those to whom they have customarily owed allegiance, organize them into units of tens and fives and drill them at regular intervals, taking advantage of their…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
技擊之素閑者優其廩餼以利導之然後
畫地使之守分城使之防而吾之所以操
縱而錯綜之者不失其柄而亦不失其宜
焉則何士氣之不振而威武之不揚也所
謂蓄財用以裕其施者又非厚斂以豐財
也蓋天地生財祗此數也不在民則在官
誠如孔明之敎耕織有以開其源如梁毗
之不取有以節其流則出之者衆蓄之者
富資之裹糧者不匱於以鼓舞其將領而
===
成其致身之忠者此也於以鼓舞其卒徒
而得其死力者此也何患於待哺枵腹而
軍國之不給哉是三者威遠之道也若非
所先也而實濟乎輯綏之所不及故曰天
生五材孰能去兵雖然今滇之民非復昔
之民矣其財賦日勤其顓蒙日開其崖險
日闢其異等者日被冠帶錯郡縣而儕漢
吏矣今滇之吏非復昔之吏矣其置法日
密其施令日威其懷來日至又冒險阻麾
punctuated:
技擊之素閑者，優其廩餼以利導之。然後畫地使之守，分城使之防，而吾之所以操縱而錯綜之者，不失其柄，而亦不失其宜焉，則何士氣之不振而威武之不揚也？所謂蓄財用以裕其施者，又非厚斂以豐財也。蓋天地生財，祗此數也，不在民則在官。誠如孔明之敎耕織，有以開其源；如梁毗之不取，有以節其流，則出之者衆，蓄之者富，資之裹糧者不匱。於以鼓舞其將領而成其致身之忠者，此也；於以鼓舞其卒徒而得其死力者，此也。何患於待哺枵腹而軍國之不給哉？是三者，威遠之道也，若非所先也，而實濟乎輯綏之所不及。故曰：「天生五材，孰能去兵？」

雖然，今滇之民，非復昔之民矣。其財賦日勤，其顓蒙日開，其崖險日闢，其異等者日被冠帶，錯郡縣而儕漢吏矣。今滇之吏，非復昔之吏矣。其置法日密，其施令日威，其懷來日至，又冒險阻，麾
translation_en:
…those already skilled in combat should receive more generous provisions, so that material benefits may guide them. Then assign them territories to hold and cities to defend. If, in directing and coordinating them, we retain control while acting appropriately, how could the soldiers’ morale fail to rise or military might fail to manifest itself?

What is meant by storing up financial resources to provide amply for expenditure is likewise not heavy taxation to enrich the treasury. The wealth produced by Heaven and Earth is limited: what is not in the people’s hands is in the government’s. If, like Kongming, we teach farming and weaving, thereby opening up the sources of wealth, and, like Liang Pi, refrain from taking wealth, thereby checking its outflow, then those producing it will be numerous, those storing it will have abundance, and supplies of provisions for the march will not run short. This is how to inspire the commanders and bring to fulfillment their loyalty in dedicating themselves to service; this is how to inspire the soldiers and obtain their utmost efforts even unto death. Why then fear empty bellies awaiting food, or insufficient supplies for the army and state? These three measures are ways of overawing distant peoples. Though seemingly not the first priority, they in fact make good what conciliation and pacification cannot accomplish. Thus it is said: “Heaven produced the five materials; who can dispense with arms?”

Nevertheless, the people of Dian are no longer the people of former times. Their fiscal obligations grow more burdensome by the day; their ignorance is increasingly dispelled; their precipitous terrain is increasingly opened up. Those of exceptional standing increasingly receive official caps and girdles, taking their places throughout the prefectures and counties alongside Han officials. The officials of Dian, too, are no longer the officials of former times. The laws they establish grow ever more detailed, the commands they issue ever more forceful, and their efforts to win allegiance ever more thorough. Moreover, they brave dangerous terrain and ward off…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
瘴癘以業乎其官矣然民就窮而賦愈匱
官愈勤而治日蹙其胥而爲盗者不獨夷
與僰焉何哉其繇可知也劉敞曰衣食不
足盗之源也賦役不均盗之源也教化不
行盗之源也使吏于其土者有以足之均
之教之而猶甘心於盗以取戮吾未之信
也雖然求其所以足之均之之道舍梁毗
之潔己孔明之善用無適也求其所以教
之之道舍信義以孚之廉公以服之亦無
===
適也吁孔明梁毗之道勝而郭欽江統之
策窮矣若夫涖之以莊斷之以正威嚴以
防其逸於以輔乎輯綏之理則又在乎執
事者之所諗之
punctuated: 瘴癘，以業乎其官矣。然民就窮而賦愈匱，官愈勤而治日蹙，其胥而爲盗者不獨夷與僰焉。何哉？其繇可知也。劉敞曰：「衣食不足，盗之源也；賦役不均，盗之源也；教化不行，盗之源也。」使吏于其土者有以足之、均之、教之，而猶甘心於盗以取戮，吾未之信也。雖然，求其所以足之、均之之道，舍梁毗之潔己、孔明之善用，無適也；求其所以教之之道，舍信義以孚之、廉公以服之，亦無適也。吁！孔明、梁毗之道勝，而郭欽、江統之策窮矣。若夫涖之以莊，斷之以正，威嚴以防其逸，於以輔乎輯綏之理，則又在乎執事者之所諗之。
translation_en:
…ward off pestilential miasmas in carrying out their official duties. Yet the people sink into poverty and tax revenues become ever more depleted; officials work ever harder, yet governance grows daily more constrained. Those who turn to banditry are not only the Yi and the Bo. Why is this? The causes can be understood. Liu Chang said: “Insufficient food and clothing are a source of banditry; unequal taxes and labor services are a source of banditry; failure to put moral instruction into practice is a source of banditry.” If those serving as officials in this land could provide the people with sufficient sustenance, distribute their burdens equitably, and instruct them, I cannot believe that the people would still willingly turn to banditry and thereby bring execution upon themselves.

Nevertheless, in seeking ways to provide sufficiency and equity, there is no course other than Liang Pi’s personal incorruptibility and Kongming’s skill in employing resources. In seeking ways to instruct them, there is likewise no course other than winning their trust through good faith and righteousness, and securing their submission through integrity and impartiality. Ah! When the way of Kongming and Liang Pi prevails, the policies of Guo Qin and Jiang Tong have no further scope. As for presiding over the people with dignity, deciding matters uprightly, and using stern authority to prevent them from casting off restraint, thereby supporting the work of conciliation and pacification—this, too, rests upon the deliberation of those in charge.

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子秋子翼謬膺徵聘
司雲南試事閱試既畢乃作
而嘆曰美哉
聖天子文德之昭宣也匪徵于近
而徵于遠夫兩京首善之地
江漢
===
皇上二南之化在焉極盛宜矣若
中土禮樂之所洽江南材儁
之所聚風易流化易行也唯
朱提炎方去
京師萬里而遙得與冠裳之會
未久也乃今視
上國或庶幾焉嘗考宣德中舉
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子秋，子翼謬膺徵聘，司雲南試事。閱試既畢，乃作而嘆曰：「美哉！聖天子文德之昭宣也！匪徵于近，而徵于遠。夫兩京首善之地，江漢，皇上二南之化在焉，極盛宜矣。若中土禮樂之所洽，江南材儁之所聚，風易流，化易行也。唯朱提炎方，去京師萬里而遙，得與冠裳之會未久也。乃今視上國，或庶幾焉。嘗考宣德中舉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jiazi year of Jiajing [1564], I, Ziyi, undeservedly received an invitation to oversee the Yunnan examination. When the examination papers had all been reviewed, I rose and exclaimed: “How splendidly the sagely Son of Heaven’s civil virtue is made manifest! Its evidence is found not nearby, but far away. The two capitals are places foremost in goodness; in the Jiang and Han region, His Majesty’s transforming influence, like that celebrated in the ‘Two Southern Sections’ of the Book of Odes, prevails. It is fitting that these places should flourish greatly. In the central lands, rites and music have spread everywhere; in Jiangnan, talented and outstanding men gather. There, exemplary influence spreads readily, and moral transformation is easily effected. But Z huti [Z huti: Z huti 朱提, conventionally Z huti / Z huti?] in the torrid south lies more than ten thousand li from the imperial capital, and only recently has it joined the fellowship of those wearing the caps and robes of civilized society. Yet now, compared with the heartland, it may well approach its standard. I once investigated those recommended during the Xuande reign …

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
于鄉者雲貴合十一人天順
中合三十人逮嘉靖丁酉雲
南始特試舉四十人歷今彬
彬然所錄有不盡者矣夫黎
獻共臣此典謨所以賛帝德
也譽髦斯士此詩人所以美
王化也今
===
聖世雍熙赫奕之治信軼虞廷而
兼周室矣得時無怠多士其
思所以自奮矣乎
國家之所以旁搜博選孜孜求
才者欲校其賢俊而用之也
故自
畿甸達于遐陬凡三代漢唐聲
punctuated:
于鄉者，雲貴合十一人，天順中合三十人。逮嘉靖丁酉，雲南始特試，舉四十人。歷今彬彬然，所錄有不盡者矣。夫黎獻共臣，此典謨所以賛帝德也；譽髦斯士，此詩人所以美王化也。今聖世雍熙赫奕之治，信軼虞廷而兼周室矣。得時無怠，多士其思所以自奮矣乎！

國家之所以旁搜博選，孜孜求才者，欲校其賢俊而用之也。故自畿甸達于遐陬，凡三代漢唐聲
translation_en:
…those selected in the Provincial Examination numbered eleven for Yunnan and Guizhou combined; during the Tianshun reign, the combined number was thirty. In the dingyou year of Jiajing, Yunnan first held a separate examination, selecting forty men. Down to the present, cultivated talent has flourished, and those admitted cannot exhaust its abundance. That the many worthy men should all serve as ministers is how the Canonical Documents and Counsels praise imperial virtue; that these outstanding scholars should be acclaimed is how the poets extol royal transforming influence. Now, in this sagely age, the harmonious, prosperous, and resplendent government truly surpasses the court of Shun and encompasses the excellences of the house of Zhou. Having met with such an age, do not be idle: should you assembled scholars not consider how to exert yourselves?

The state searches everywhere, selects broadly, and tirelessly seeks talent because it wishes to assess worthy and outstanding men and employ them. Thus, from the metropolitan domain to the remotest corners, wherever the civilizing influence of the Three Dynasties, the Han, and the Tang…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
教之所不洽者皆得貢士網
羅之唯恐其遺也此豈爲尋
常尺寸之士設哉夫鴻鵠之
高飛者六翮也至於背上之
毛腹下之毳不與焉主司願
多士爲六翮之用不願其爲
背腹之毳也今天下儒紳翺
===
翔濟濟崒集
闕下若千流萬壑之必歸于海
當此之時非有純懿之操通
方之才卽無以自見往者漢
世滇南風氣未開唯盛覽受
學司馬相如簡册以爲美談
今滇士之懷忠良摛文藻者
punctuated:
教之所不洽者，皆得貢士，網羅之唯恐其遺也。此豈爲尋常尺寸之士設哉？夫鴻鵠之高飛者，六翮也；至於背上之毛、腹下之毳，不與焉。主司願多士爲六翮之用，不願其爲背腹之毳也。
今天下儒紳翺翔濟濟，崒集闕下，若千流萬壑之必歸于海。當此之時，非有純懿之操、通方之才，卽無以自見。往者漢世，滇南風氣未開，唯盛覽受學司馬相如，簡册以爲美談。今滇士之懷忠良、摛文藻者
translation_en:
…even places unreached by the civilizing influence of the Three Dynasties, the Han, and the Tang may all send forward scholars as tribute. The state gathers them in, fearing only that any might be overlooked. Could this arrangement have been established merely for men of ordinary, trifling abilities? What enables a great swan to soar high is its six flight quills; the feathers on its back and the down beneath its belly play no part in this. We who preside over the examination wish you scholars to serve as those six flight quills, not as the down on the back and belly.
Today, the Confucian scholars and gentry of the realm soar aloft in splendid multitudes and throng beneath the palace gates, just as a thousand streams and ten thousand ravines must all flow toward the sea. At such a time, without conduct of unsullied excellence and talents of wide-ranging understanding, one has no means of distinguishing oneself. Formerly, under the Han, when the intellectual culture of southern Yunnan was still undeveloped, Sheng Lan alone studied under Sima Xiangru, and the written histories celebrated this as an admirable episode. Today, those scholars of Yunnan who cherish loyalty and goodness and display literary brilliance…

title: 嘉靖四十三年雲南鄉試錄
text:
何限賓興通籍所舉不過數
十人豈易哉使覽生今之世
聲名尚不出閭里况簡冊耶
故曰時異事異主司願多士
之志其大而毋狃于一時也
昔釡明一言叔向下堂執其
手而信其賢今連篇而閱之
===
累日而試之主司無古人之
明惴惴然慮有遺賢是懼乃
若樹績蜚聲奮六翮之用以
為主司光榮則二三子事也
非主司所得與也
江西吉安府安福縣儒學教
諭毛子翼謹序
punctuated:
何限！賓興通籍，所舉不過數十人，豈易哉！使覽生今之世，聲名尚不出閭里，况簡冊耶？故曰：時異事異。主司願多士之志其大，而毋狃于一時也。
昔釡明一言，叔向下堂執其手而信其賢。今連篇而閱之，累日而試之，主司無古人之明，惴惴然慮有遺賢，是懼。乃若樹績蜚聲，奮六翮之用，以為主司光榮，則二三子事也，非主司所得與也。
江西吉安府安福縣儒學教諭毛子翼謹序。
translation_en:
…how numerous they are! Yet in selecting worthy men for entry into the official registers, no more than a few dozen are recommended. How could this be easy? Had Sheng Lan lived in the present age, his reputation would not even have spread beyond his own neighborhood, much less entered the historical records. Thus it is said: times differ, and circumstances differ. As examiner, I hope that you scholars will set your aspirations high and not remain bound by the circumstances of a single moment.
In former times, upon hearing a single utterance from Fu Ming [?], Shuxiang descended from the hall, took his hand, and recognized his worth. Today, we read page after page and examine candidates over successive days. Lacking the discernment of the ancients, I anxiously fear that worthy men may have been overlooked. As for establishing achievements and winning renown, spreading your six flight feathers to put your abilities to use and thereby bringing honor to your examiner—this is your task, gentlemen, and lies beyond what the examiner can do.
Preface respectfully written by Mao Ziyi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.
